        def generate_turn(self, **kwargs):
            return (
                '<tool_call name="write_component">\n'
                '<tsx>\n'
                'import React from "react";\n'
                'export function Component() { return <div>Self Contained Edit</div>; }\n'
                '</tsx>\n'
                '</tool_call>'
            )

    res = execute_runtime_edit_policy(
        target_file="Component.tsx",
        workspace_root=workspace,
        runner=MockRunner(),
        instruction="Update component to say Self Contained Edit",
        primary_symbol="Component",
    )

    assert res["policy_sequence"] == ["read_file", "inspect_dependencies", "edit", "verify"]
    steps = [s["step"] for s in res["steps_completed"]]
    assert steps == ["read_file", "inspect_dependencies", "edit", "verify"]
    assert res["success"] is True
    assert "Self Contained Edit" in target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_detect_undeclared_identifiers():
    """Verify detect_undeclared_identifiers catches TS2304, TS2307, TS2552, and ReferenceError."""
    sample_output = """
Component.tsx(3,10): error TS2307: Cannot find module '@tanstack/react-table' or its corresponding type declarations.
Component.tsx(15,22): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'useCart'.
Component.tsx(22,5): error TS2552: Cannot find name 'useUndoState'. Did you mean 'useState'?
Uncaught ReferenceError: lodash is not defined
"""
    diagnostics = detect_undeclared_identifiers(sample_output)
    codes = {d["code"] for d in diagnostics}
    identifiers = {d["identifier"] for d in diagnostics}

    assert "TS2307" in codes
    assert "TS2304" in codes
    assert "TS2552" in codes
    assert "ReferenceError" in codes
    assert "@tanstack/react-table" in identifiers
    assert "useCart" in identifiers
    assert "useUndoState" in identifiers
    assert "lodash" in identifiers

"""
tests/test_single_source_context_length.py - Comprehensive Tests for Single Source of Truth Context Length

Verifies:
1. ModelRuntimeConfig as the authoritative single source of truth:
   - Reading and setting ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length
   - Precedence order: explicit override -> SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH env var -> benchmark report -> 8192 fallback
2. ContextBuilder and TokenBudget synchronization:
   - Changing context length in one place automatically updates TokenBudget and ContextBuilder
   - Proportional slice scaling when context length changes (e.g. 6144 vs 8192)
   - Sum of slices always equals total budget
3. Training & Preflight integration:
   - resolve_context_length and train_sft.py preflight respect SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH and ModelRuntimeConfig
4. Inference & Server integration:
   - AgentModelRunner defaults to ModelRuntimeConfig
   - /api/status and connection.ready emit authoritative max_context_tokens
5. Token counting & validation:
   - Final prompt validation uses real tokenizer
   - Enforces prompt_tokens + max_new_tokens <= max_seq_length
   - Clamping dynamically restricts max_new_tokens without error unless prompt_tokens >= max_seq_length
"""

import json
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import pytest
import torch

from agent.config import ModelRuntimeConfig
from agent.context_builder import ContextBuilder, TokenBudget
from agent.agent import AgentModelRunner
from server.sessions import Session
from training.context_decision import resolve_context_length
from training.train_sft import train


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def reset_runtime_config():
    """Ensure clean state before and after each test."""
    ModelRuntimeConfig.reset()
    orig_env = os.environ.get("SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH")
    yield
    ModelRuntimeConfig.reset()
    if orig_env is not None:
        os.environ["SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH"] = orig_env
    else:
        os.environ.pop("SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH", None)


# ── 1. ModelRuntimeConfig Precedence & Resolution ────────────────────────────

def test_model_runtime_config_precedence():
    # 1. Fallback when nothing set (or benchmark report if present)
    ModelRuntimeConfig.reset()
    os.environ.pop("SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH", None)
    default_or_bench = ModelRuntimeConfig.get_max_seq_length()
    assert default_or_bench in (6144, 8192)

    # 2. SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH env var overrides benchmark/default
    os.environ["SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH"] = "6144"
    assert ModelRuntimeConfig.get_max_seq_length() == 6144
    assert ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length == 6144

    os.environ["SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH"] = "4096"
    assert ModelRuntimeConfig.get_max_seq_length() == 4096

    # 3. Explicit code override takes highest precedence
    ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length = 5120
    assert ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length == 5120

    # Reset clears explicit override back to env var
    ModelRuntimeConfig.reset()
    assert ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length == 4096

    os.environ.pop("SLM_CONTEXT_LENGTH", None)
    ModelRuntimeConfig.reset()


# ── 2. ContextBuilder & TokenBudget Auto-Scaling ─────────────────────────────

def test_token_budget_auto_scales_with_runtime_config():
    # When context length is 8192
    ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length = 8192
    budget_8192 = TokenBudget()
    assert budget_8192.total == 8192
    assert budget_8192.system_contracts == 1000
    assert budget_8192.current_instruction == 300
    assert budget_8192.project_metadata == 300
    assert budget_8192.selected_files == 3000
    assert budget_8192.related_files == 1600
    assert budget_8192.recent_conversation == 900
    assert budget_8192.build_diagnostics == 700
    assert budget_8192.reserve == 392
    assert (
        budget_8192.system_contracts
        + budget_8192.current_instruction
        + budget_8192.project_metadata
        + budget_8192.selected_files
        + budget_8192.related_files
        + budget_8192.recent_conversation
        + budget_8192.build_diagnostics
        + budget_8192.reserve
    ) == 8192

# ── 5. Generation Max-Token Clamping: prompt + max_new <= max_seq ────────────

def test_clamp_max_new_tokens_enforces_context_budget():
    ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length = 6144

    # 1. Normal case: plenty of headroom
    clamped = ModelRuntimeConfig.clamp_max_new_tokens(prompt_tokens=2000, requested_max_new_tokens=1024)
    assert clamped == 1024
    assert 2000 + clamped <= 6144

    # 2. Clamping case: prompt + requested > max_seq
    # 5500 + 1024 > 6144 -> clamp to 6144 - 5500 = 644
    clamped = ModelRuntimeConfig.clamp_max_new_tokens(prompt_tokens=5500, requested_max_new_tokens=1024)
    assert clamped == 644
    assert 5500 + clamped == 6144

    # 3. Tight border case: prompt is 6143
    clamped = ModelRuntimeConfig.clamp_max_new_tokens(prompt_tokens=6143, requested_max_new_tokens=500)
    assert clamped == 1
    assert 6143 + clamped == 6144

    # 4. Overflow case: prompt >= max_seq -> raises ValueError
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        ModelRuntimeConfig.clamp_max_new_tokens(prompt_tokens=6144, requested_max_new_tokens=100)
    assert "exceeds or equals" in str(excinfo.value)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ModelRuntimeConfig.clamp_max_new_tokens(prompt_tokens=7000, requested_max_new_tokens=100)


def test_agent_model_runner_clamping_enforcement():
    ModelRuntimeConfig.max_seq_length = 100
    runner = AgentModelRunner(model_path="dummy", is_mock=True)
    assert runner.max_seq_length == 100

    # Case A: max_new_tokens >= max_seq_length raises ValueError
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc:
        runner.generate_turn(example_idx=0, history=[], primary_symbol="Button", max_new_tokens=100)
    assert "must be less than max_seq_length" in str(exc.value)

    # Case B: Prompt exceeds max_seq_length raises ValueError
    huge_history = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are an assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "word " * 300},
    ]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc:
        runner.generate_turn(example_idx=0, history=huge_history, primary_symbol="Button", max_new_tokens=10)
    assert "exceeds" in str(exc.value)

    # Case C: Valid prompt and tokens run and self-correct/generate
    valid_history = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a coding agent."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Write Button"},
    ]
    out = runner.generate_turn(example_idx=0, history=valid_history, primary_symbol="Button", max_new_tokens=20)
    assert "Button" in out

"""
tests/test_task_cancellation.py - Tests for Issue #7: Define New Project Behavior During an Active GPU Task.

Verifies:
1. Backend task cancellation flags the running task and sets _runner.stop_check.
2. Token generation stops via StoppingCriteria when cancelled mid-turn.
3. clear_queue parameter drains queued work.
4. Emits final cancelled task event (type: "cancelled" and "task.cancelled").
5. /api/generation/<task_id>/status and UI agree on "cancelled" status.
6. Frontend active task modal and 3 user options (Cancel & Start New, Keep Running in Background, Stay Here).
"""

import sys
import queue
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
if str(BASE_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR))

from server.app import app, cancelled_tasks, task_queues, _generation_queue, _task_results
from agent.agent import AgentModelRunner


def test_frontend_active_generation_modal_flow():
    """Verify frontend modal behaviors using the headless tsx runner."""
    script_path = BASE_DIR / "scripts" / "test_active_task_modal.mjs"
    assert script_path.exists(), f"Script {script_path} does not exist"

    res = subprocess.run(
        ["npx", "--yes", "tsx", str(script_path)],
        cwd=str(BASE_DIR),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        shell=True,
    )
    assert res.returncode == 0, f"Frontend active task modal test failed:\nSTDOUT:\n{res.stdout}\nSTDERR:\n{res.stderr}"
    assert "ALL FRONTEND MODAL & CONFLICT WORKFLOW TESTS PASSED!" in res.stdout


def test_backend_cancel_task_flags_and_emits_event():
    """Verify /api/cancel/<task_id> flags the task, clears queue on request, and emits task.cancelled."""
    client = app.test_client()
    task_id = "test_cancel_task_123"

    # Setup task queue and pending item
    tq = queue.Queue()
    task_queues[task_id] = tq
    _generation_queue.put({"task_id": "queued_task_999"})

    try:
        # Cancel with clear_queue=true
        resp = client.post(f"/api/cancel/{task_id}?clear_queue=true")
        assert resp.status_code == 200
        data = resp.get_json()
        assert data["status"] == "cancelled"
        assert data["task_id"] == task_id

        # 1. Flags the running task
        assert task_id in cancelled_tasks

        # 2. Clears queued work
        assert _generation_queue.empty()

        # 3. Emits final cancelled task events into the task queue
        events = []
        while not tq.empty():
            events.append(tq.get_nowait())

        event_types = [e.get("type") for e in events]
        assert "cancelled" in event_types, f"Expected 'cancelled' event, got: {event_types}"
        assert "task.cancelled" in event_types, f"Expected 'task.cancelled' event, got: {event_types}"
        assert "done" in event_types, f"Expected 'done' event, got: {event_types}"

        # 4. Status endpoint reflects cancelled status
        status_resp = client.get(f"/api/generation/{task_id}/status")
        assert status_resp.status_code == 200
        status_data = status_resp.get_json()
        assert status_data["status"] == "cancelled"
    finally:
        cancelled_tasks.discard(task_id)
        task_queues.pop(task_id, None)
        _task_results.pop(task_id, None)


def test_agent_runner_exits_token_generation_via_stop_check():
    """Verify AgentModelRunner exits immediately when stop_check returns True."""

    runner.is_mock = False
    runner.max_seq_length = 512

    class DummyTokenizer:
        eos_token_id = 2
        def __call__(self, text, return_tensors="pt"):
            import torch
            return MagicMock(input_ids=torch.ones(1, 10, dtype=torch.long))
        def decode(self, *args, **kwargs):
            return "Generated text"

    runner.tokenizer = DummyTokenizer()
    runner.model = MagicMock()
    runner.model.get_input_embeddings.return_value.weight.device = "cpu"

    # Define a generate implementation that invokes stopping_criteria
    cancelled = [False]
    def mock_generate(**kwargs):
        cancelled[0] = True
        # Verify stopping_criteria was configured and fires
        criteria = kwargs.get("stopping_criteria")
        assert criteria is not None, "StoppingCriteria must be passed to model.generate"
        assert criteria[0](None, None) is True, "StoppingCriteria should evaluate to True when cancelled"
        import torch
        return torch.ones((1, 15), dtype=torch.long)

    runner.model.generate.side_effect = mock_generate

    # Calling generate_turn with stop_check returning True must raise InterruptedError
    import pytest
    with pytest.raises(InterruptedError, match="Generation stopped by user."):
        runner.generate_turn(

            history=[{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],

def test_performance_check_1_no_webgl_errors():
    """Verify rule 1: no WebGL errors."""
    clean_files = {"src/App.tsx": "const gl = canvas.getContext('webgl');"}
    passed, _, _ = validate_no_webgl_errors(clean_files)
    assert passed is True

    error_logs = [{"text": "WebGL: INVALID_OPERATION: drawElements: buffer not bound"}]
    passed, reason, _ = validate_no_webgl_errors(clean_files, runtime_logs=error_logs)
    assert passed is False
    assert "INVALID_OPERATION" in reason


def test_performance_check_2_reasonable_dpr():
    """Verify rule 2: reasonable DPR bounded <= 2.0."""
    # Pass: bounded array
    passed, _, _ = validate_reasonable_dpr({"src/App.tsx": "<Canvas dpr={[1, 1.5]} />"})
    assert passed is True

    # Fail: DPR max 3
    passed, reason, _ = validate_reasonable_dpr({"src/App.tsx": "<Canvas dpr={[1, 3]} />"})
    assert passed is False
    assert "upper bound" in reason

    # Fail: raw unmetered devicePixelRatio
    passed, reason, _ = validate_reasonable_dpr({"src/App.tsx": "<Canvas dpr={window.devicePixelRatio} />"})
    assert passed is False
    assert "unmetered" in reason


def test_performance_check_3_bounded_particle_count():

    assert passed is True

    passed, reason, _ = validate_bounded_particle_count({"src/App.tsx": "<Points count={50000} />"})
    assert passed is False
    assert "5,000" in reason


def test_performance_check_4_no_expensive_unnecessary_shadows():
    """Verify rule 4: maximum 1-2 shadow casting lights and shadow map <= 2048."""
    # Pass: 1 directional light with shadow
    passed, _, _ = validate_no_expensive_unnecessary_shadows({"src/App.tsx": "<directionalLight castShadow />"})
    assert passed is True

    # Fail: 4 lights casting shadows
    bad_code = (
        "<directionalLight castShadow />\n"
        "<pointLight castShadow />\n"
        "<spotLight castShadow />\n"
        "<pointLight castShadow />"
    )
    passed, reason, _ = validate_no_expensive_unnecessary_shadows({"src/App.tsx": bad_code})
    assert passed is False
    assert "Too many shadow-casting lights" in reason


def test_performance_check_5_no_leaking_use_frame_allocations():
    """Verify rule 5: zero allocations inside useFrame animation loops."""
    # Pass: mutating ref position
    good_code = "useFrame((_, delta) => { if (ref.current) ref.current.rotation.y += delta; });"
    passed, _, _ = validate_no_leaking_use_frame_allocations({"src/App.tsx": good_code})
    assert passed is True

    # Fail: new Vector3 inside useFrame
    bad_code = "useFrame(() => { const v = new THREE.Vector3(1, 0, 0); ref.current.position.add(v); });"
    passed, reason, _ = validate_no_leaking_use_frame_allocations({"src/App.tsx": bad_code})
    assert passed is False
    assert "allocations detected" in reason


def test_performance_check_6_no_unbounded_post_processing():

    assert passed is False
    assert "stacked" in reason

# 5. Acceptance Criteria: Separate 3D vs Normal DOM Sites Evaluation
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_separate_evaluation_in_benchmark_scorer():
    """Verify 3D sites are scored with 3D checks and aggregated separately from DOM sites."""
    scorer = SiteBenchmarkScorer()

    # Normal DOM site
    dom_spec = {"task_id": "dom_site_1", "has_3d": False, "domain": "saas", "name": "CloudApp"}
    dom_files = {
        "src/App.tsx": "export function App() { return <div><h1>CloudApp</h1></div>; }",
        "src/components/Header.tsx": "export function Header() { return <header>Nav</header>; }",
    }
    score_dom = scorer.evaluate_site(dom_spec, dom_files)
    assert score_dom.is_3d_site is False

    # 3D site with performant R3F canvas
    three_spec = {"task_id": "three_site_1", "has_3d": True, "domain": "spatial", "name": "SpatialViewer"}
    three_files = {
        "src/App.tsx": (
            "import { Canvas, useFrame } from '@react-three/fiber';\n"
            "const gl = canvas.getContext('webgl');\n"
            "export function App() {\n"
            "  useFrame((_, d) => { if (ref.current) ref.current.rotation.y += d; });\n"
            "  return (\n"
            "    <Canvas dpr={[1, 1.5]} frameloop='demand'>\n"
            "      <ambientLight />\n"
            "      <directionalLight castShadow={false} />\n"
            "    </Canvas>\n"
            "  );\n"
            "}"
        ),
    }
    score_3d = scorer.evaluate_site(three_spec, three_files)
    assert score_3d.is_3d_site is True
    assert "no_webgl_errors" in score_3d.three_d_performance_checks

    # Aggregate both
    batch = [score_dom, score_3d]
    aggregate = aggregate_site_benchmark_scores(batch)

    # Acceptance criteria verification: separate summaries
    assert "dom_sites_summary" in aggregate
    assert "three_d_sites_summary" in aggregate

    dom_sum = aggregate["dom_sites_summary"]
    t3d_sum = aggregate["three_d_sites_summary"]

    assert dom_sum["total_sites"] == 1
    assert t3d_sum["total_sites"] == 1
    assert "three_d_performance_pass_rate" in t3d_sum
    assert "performance_checks_breakdown" in t3d_sum
    assert t3d_sum["three_d_performance_pass_rate"] == 1.0

# ── Rule 1: Scroll Reveal Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────

def test_rule1_scroll_reveal_compliant():
    """Scroll reveal with IntersectionObserver, unobserve cleanup, and reduced-motion passes."""
    tsx = """
    import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
    export function Features() {
        const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
        useEffect(() => {
            const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
                entries.forEach(e => {
                    if (e.isIntersecting) e.target.classList.add('is-visible');
                });
            });
            if (ref.current) observer.observe(ref.current);
            return () => observer.disconnect();
        }, []);
        return <div ref={ref} className="reveal-box">Feature</div>;
    }
    """
    css = """
    .reveal-box {
        opacity: 0;
        transform: translateY(20px);
        transition: opacity 0.5s ease, transform 0.5s ease;
    }
    .reveal-box.is-visible {
        opacity: 1;
        transform: translateY(0);
    }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
        .reveal-box {
            opacity: 1 !important;
            transform: none !important;
        }
    }
    """
    files = {"src/Features.tsx": tsx, "src/Features.css": css}
    res = validate_motion_rules(files, [MotionSpec(type=MotionType.SCROLL_REVEAL, target_section="features")])
    assert res.is_valid is True
    assert len(res.violations) == 0
    assert any("Rule 1" in p for p in res.passed_rules)

def test_rule2_parallax_compliant():
    """Parallax with passive scroll listener, RAF, cleanup, and reduced-motion passes."""
    tsx = """
    import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
    export function Hero() {
        const bgRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
        useEffect(() => {
            let rafId: number;
            const onScroll = () => {
                rafId = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
                    const offset = Math.min(50, window.scrollY * 0.2);
                    if (bgRef.current) bgRef.current.style.transform = `translate3d(0, ${offset}px, 0)`;
                });
            };
            window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });
            return () => {
                window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);
                cancelAnimationFrame(rafId);
            };
        }, []);
        return <div ref={bgRef} className="parallax-hero">Hero</div>;
    }
    """
    css = """
    .parallax-hero {
        position: relative;
        overflow: hidden;

    }

    assert any("Rule 2" in p for p in res.passed_rules)

# ── Rule 3: Horizontal Scroll Tests ──────────────────────────────────────────

def test_rule3_horizontal_scroll_compliant():
    """Horizontal scroll with normal vertical mapping and mobile scroll-snap passes."""
    tsx = """
    import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
    export function Showcase() {
        const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
        useEffect(() => {
            const onScroll = () => {};
            window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });
            return () => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);
        }, []);
        return (
            <div ref={containerRef} className="horizontal-section">
                <div className="sticky-viewport">
                    <div className="horizontal-track">Cards</div>
                </div>
            </div>
        );
    }
    """
    css = """
    .horizontal-section { height: 300vh; }
    .sticky-viewport {
        position: sticky;
        top: 0;
        height: 100vh;
        overflow: hidden;
    }
    .horizontal-track { display: flex; will-change: transform; }
    @media (max-width: 768px) {
        .sticky-viewport {
            position: static;
            height: auto;
            overflow-x: auto;
            scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;
        }
    }
    """
    files = {"src/Showcase.tsx": tsx, "src/Showcase.css": css}
    res = validate_motion_rules(files, [MotionSpec(type=MotionType.HORIZONTAL_SCROLL, target_section="showcase")])
    assert res.is_valid is True
    assert len(res.violations) == 0
    assert any("Rule 3" in p for p in res.passed_rules)

# ── Scorer & Validator Integration Tests ─────────────────────────────────────

def test_scorer_motion_quality_with_rules_validation():
    """SiteBenchmarkScorer integrates validate_motion_rules and heavily penalizes violations."""
    scorer = SiteBenchmarkScorer()

    # 1. Compliant codebase (multi-component with scroll reveal and micro-interactions)
    r_tsx, r_css = generate_scroll_reveal_snippet("Features")
    m_tsx, m_css = generate_micro_interaction_snippet("Pricing")
    compliant_files = {
        "src/Features.tsx": r_tsx,
        "src/Features.css": r_css,
        "src/Pricing.tsx": m_tsx,
        "src/Pricing.css": m_css,
    }
    score_clean, details_clean = scorer.score_motion_quality(compliant_files)
    assert score_clean >= 0.85
    assert "rules_validation" in details_clean
    assert len(details_clean["violations"]) == 0

    # 2. Codebase with hard violation (wheel.preventDefault hijacking)
    violating_files = {
        "src/Hero.tsx": "window.addEventListener('wheel', (e) => { e.preventDefault(); });",
        "src/Hero.css": ".hero:hover { transform: scale(1.1); }",
    }
    score_bad, details_bad = scorer.score_motion_quality(violating_files)
    assert len(details_bad["violations"]) > 0
    assert score_bad < score_clean


def test_project_validator_motion_rules_check():
    """run_motion_rules_check catches infractions in a workspace directory."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        workspace = Path(tmp_dir)

        # Write clean snippet
        p_tsx, p_css = generate_micro_interaction_snippet("Pricing")
        (workspace / "Pricing.tsx").write_text(p_tsx, encoding="utf-8")
        (workspace / "Pricing.css").write_text(p_css, encoding="utf-8")

        passed, errs, warns = run_motion_rules_check(workspace)
        assert passed is True
        assert len(errs) == 0

        # Inject wheel.preventDefault hard violation
        (workspace / "BadHero.tsx").write_text(
            "export function Bad() { window.addEventListener('wheel', (e) => e.preventDefault()); return null; }",
            encoding="utf-8"
        )
        passed_bad, errs_bad, _ = run_motion_rules_check(workspace)
        assert passed_bad is False
        assert any("hijack" in e.lower() or "preventdefault" in e.lower() for e in errs_bad)


def test_validation_result_motion_properties():
    """ValidationResult reflects motion_passed and motion_status in code_passed and passed."""
    vr = ValidationResult(
        typecheck_passed=True,
        build_passed=True,
        lint_passed=True,
        contract_passed=True,
        accessibility_passed=True,
        runtime_passed=True,
        preview_running=True,
        motion_passed=False,
        motion_status="failed",
    )
    assert vr.motion_passed is False
    assert vr.motionPassed is False
    assert vr.motionStatus == "failed"
    assert vr.code_passed is False
    assert vr.passed is False

    d = vr.to_dict()
    assert d["motion_passed"] is False
    assert d["motionPassed"] is False
    assert d["motion_status"] == "failed"

def test_site_benchmark_scorer_penalizes_unverified_packages():
    """SiteBenchmarkScorer applies deductions when unverified external motion libraries are imported."""
    scorer = SiteBenchmarkScorer()

    # Codebase importing unverified GSAP without package.json
    unverified_files = {
        "src/Hero.tsx": "import { gsap } from 'gsap'; export function Hero() { return null; }",
        "src/Hero.css": ".hero { transition: transform 0.2s ease; }",
    }
    score_unverified, details_unverified = scorer.score_motion_quality(unverified_files)
    assert any("unverified external package 'gsap'" in v.lower() for v in details_unverified["violations"])
    assert details_unverified["rules_validation"]["is_valid"] is False

    # Codebase with verified GSAP in package.json
    verified_files = {
        "src/Hero.tsx": "import { gsap } from 'gsap'; export function Hero() { return null; }",
        "src/Hero.css": ".hero { transition: transform 0.2s ease; }",
        "package.json": json.dumps({"dependencies": {"gsap": "^3.12.5"}}),
    }
    score_verified, details_verified = scorer.score_motion_quality(verified_files)
    assert not any("unverified external package 'gsap'" in v.lower() for v in details_verified["violations"])

def compute_sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        while chunk := f.read(65536):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def tokenize(text: str) -> set[str]:
    cleaned = (
        text.lower()
        .replace(".", " ")
        .replace(",", " ")
        .replace(":", " ")
        .replace("-", " ")
        .replace("/", " ")
        .replace("(", " ")
        .replace(")", " ")
    )
    return set(cleaned.split())

    assert actual_sft_sha == sft_meta["sha256"], f"SFT SHA mismatch: {actual_sft_sha} vs {sft_meta['sha256']}"
    assert actual_sft_size == sft_meta["size_bytes"], f"SFT size mismatch: {actual_sft_size} vs {sft_meta['size_bytes']}"
    assert sft_meta["record_count"] == 36

    # Check Eval file hash and size

def test_sft_record_count_and_family_distribution():
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in SFT_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]
    assert len(records) == 36, f"Expected 36 trajectories, got {len(records)}"

    gold_records = []
    repair_records = []
    family_counts = {}

    for item in records:
        assert "task_id" in item
        assert "messages" in item
        assert "metadata" in item

        m_type = item["metadata"].get("motion_type")
        if m_type == "micro_interaction":
            m_type = "micro_interactions"
        family_counts[m_type] = family_counts.get(m_type, 0) + 1

        if item["metadata"].get("trajectory_type") == "repair":
            repair_records.append(item)
        else:
            gold_records.append(item)

    assert len(gold_records) == 30, f"Expected 30 gold trajectories, got {len(gold_records)}"
    assert len(repair_records) == 6, f"Expected 6 repair trajectories, got {len(repair_records)}"

    # Exactly 6 per motion family (5 gold + 1 repair)
    for fam in MOTION_FAMILIES:
        assert family_counts.get(fam) == 6, f"Family {fam} count should be 6, got {family_counts.get(fam)}"


def test_sft_tool_call_contract():
    tool_call_pattern = re.compile(
        r'<tool_call name="write_site">\s*<file path="([^"]+)">([\s\S]*?)</file>\s*<file path="([^"]+)">([\s\S]*?)</file>\s*</tool_call>',
        re.MULTILINE
    )

    records = [json.loads(line) for line in SFT_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]
    for item in records:
        final_assistant_msg = None
        for msg in reversed(item["messages"]):
            if msg["role"] == "assistant":
                final_assistant_msg = msg["content"]
                break

        assert final_assistant_msg is not None, f"Trajectory {item['task_id']} missing assistant message"
        m = tool_call_pattern.search(final_assistant_msg)
        assert m is not None, f"Trajectory {item['task_id']} does not match write_site XML contract"

        file1, code1, file2, code2 = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4)
        exts = {Path(file1).suffix.lower(), Path(file2).suffix.lower()}
        assert exts == {".tsx", ".css"}, f"Trajectory {item['task_id']} must have .tsx and .css files, got {exts}"
        assert len(code1.strip()) > 50, f"Trajectory {item['task_id']} has empty file {file1}"
        assert len(code2.strip()) > 50, f"Trajectory {item['task_id']} has empty file {file2}"

def test_sft_repair_trajectories_structure():
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in SFT_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]
    repair_records = [r for r in records if r["metadata"].get("trajectory_type") == "repair"]
    assert len(repair_records) == 6

    expected_flaws = {
        "motion_repair_scroll_reveal_01": "observer is never disconnected",
        "motion_repair_parallax_02": "setState on every scroll event",
        "motion_repair_horizontal_scroll_03": "wheel.preventDefault()",
        "motion_repair_sticky_story_04": "overflow:hidden",
        "motion_repair_text_reveal_05": "screen readers announce every decorative span",
        "motion_repair_micro_interactions_06": "hover-only",
    }

    for item in repair_records:
        tid = item["task_id"]
        assert tid in expected_flaws
        messages = item["messages"]
        assert len(messages) >= 4, f"Repair trajectory {tid} should have at least 4 turns, got {len(messages)}"

        # Verify multi-turn structure
        roles = [m["role"] for m in messages]
        assert roles[:2] == ["system", "user"]
        assert "assistant" in roles[2:]
        assert "user" in roles[3:]

        # Verify diagnosis turn in user observation
        diag_msg = None
        for m in messages[2:]:
            if m["role"] == "user" and '<observation status="failed">' in m["content"]:
                diag_msg = m["content"]
                break

        assert diag_msg is not None, f"Repair trajectory {tid} missing <observation status=\"failed\"> diagnostic turn"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Motion Rules & Native Library Policy Compliance
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_sft_code_passes_native_motion_policy():
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in SFT_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]

    forbidden_packages = [
        r'from\s+[\'"]gsap[\'"]',
        r'from\s+[\'"]framer-motion[\'"]',
        r'from\s+[\'"]@studio-freight/lenis[\'"]',
        r'require\([\'"]gsap[\'"]\)',
        r'require\([\'"]framer-motion[\'"]\)',
    ]

    for item in records:
        tid = item["task_id"]
        final_assistant_content = ""
        for msg in reversed(item["messages"]):
            if msg["role"] == "assistant":
                final_assistant_content = msg["content"]
                break

        # Zero unverified libraries
        for fp in forbidden_packages:
            assert not re.search(fp, final_assistant_content), (
                f"Trajectory {tid} illegally imports unverified package ({fp})"
            )

        # Prefers-reduced-motion media query present
        assert "prefers-reduced-motion" in final_assistant_content, (
            f"Trajectory {tid} missing prefers-reduced-motion fallback"
        )

        # Zero wheel/touch hijacking
        assert "wheel.preventdefault" not in final_assistant_content.lower(), (
            f"Trajectory {tid} violates zero wheel hijacking rule"
        )
        assert "touchmove.preventdefault" not in final_assistant_content.lower(), (
            f"Trajectory {tid} violates zero touchmove hijacking rule"
        )


def test_sft_motion_family_specific_mechanics():
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in SFT_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]

    for item in records:
        tid = item["task_id"]
        m_type = item["metadata"].get("motion_type")
        content = item["messages"][-1]["content"]

        if m_type == "scroll_reveal":
            assert "IntersectionObserver" in content
            assert ("unobserve" in content or "disconnect" in content)
        elif m_type == "parallax":
            assert "requestAnimationFrame" in content
            assert "passive: true" in content or "passive:true" in content
            assert "cancelAnimationFrame" in content
        elif m_type == "horizontal_scroll":
            assert "requestAnimationFrame" in content
            assert "scroll-snap" in content
            assert "cancelAnimationFrame" in content
        elif m_type == "sticky_story":
            assert "sticky" in content
            assert "IntersectionObserver" in content
            assert "disconnect" in content
        elif m_type == "text_reveal":
            assert "aria-label" in content
            assert "aria-hidden" in content
        elif m_type in ("micro_interaction", "micro_interactions"):
            assert ("focus-visible" in content or "focus-within" in content)
            assert "aria-pressed" in content

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_eval_record_count_and_family_distribution():
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in EVAL_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]
    assert len(records) == 12, f"Expected 12 evaluation records, got {len(records)}"

    eval_families = {}
    brands = set()

    for item in records:
        assert "task_id" in item
        assert "family_id" in item
        assert "category" in item
        assert "motion_type" in item
        assert "brand" in item
        assert "prompt" in item
        assert "messages" in item
        assert "metadata" in item
        assert "checks" in item

        m_type = item["motion_type"]
        if m_type == "micro_interaction":
            m_type = "micro_interactions"
        eval_families[m_type] = eval_families.get(m_type, 0) + 1
        brands.add(item["brand"])

    # Exactly 2 tasks per motion family
    for fam in MOTION_FAMILIES:
        assert eval_families.get(fam) == 2, f"Eval family {fam} count should be 2, got {eval_families.get(fam)}"

    # Exactly 12 distinct brands
    assert len(brands) == 12, f"Expected 12 distinct brands in eval set, got {len(brands)}"


def test_eval_disjointness_and_similarity_threshold():
    sft_records = [json.loads(line) for line in SFT_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]
    eval_records = [json.loads(line) for line in EVAL_PATH_DATA.open(encoding="utf-8")]

    sft_brands = {
        "atelier north",
        "vector cloud",
        "arc audio",
        "field notes",
        "mira studio",
    }

    sft_prompts = []
    for item in sft_records:
        for msg in item["messages"]:
            if msg["role"] == "user":
                sft_prompts.append(msg["content"])

    max_jaccard = 0.0
    for er in eval_records:
        brand = er["brand"].lower()
        assert brand not in sft_brands, f"Eval brand '{brand}' collides with SFT brand"

        e_tok = tokenize(er["prompt"])
        for sp in sft_prompts:
            s_tok = tokenize(sp)
            j = len(e_tok & s_tok) / len(e_tok | s_tok)
            if j > max_jaccard:
                max_jaccard = j

    # Strictly lower than 0.40 requirement
    assert max_jaccard < 0.40, f"Max Jaccard similarity {max_jaccard:.4f} exceeds 0.40 threshold"
    assert max_jaccard < 0.30, f"Max Jaccard similarity {max_jaccard:.4f} should be well decoupled (<0.30)"

    for kw in required_keywords:

import '@testing-library/jest-dom';
import { vi } from 'vitest';
import { act } from '@testing-library/react';

// Expose vi as jest so @testing-library/dom detects fake timers and advances them in waitFor/findBy
(globalThis as any).jest = vi;

// Polyfill File in jsdom environment if missing or unconstructible
if (
  typeof globalThis.File === 'undefined' ||
  !(function () {
    try {
      new (globalThis as any).File([], 't');
      return true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  })()
) {
  try {
    const { File } = require('node:buffer');
    globalThis.File = File;
    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
      (window as any).File = File;
    }
  } catch {}
}

// Polyfill PointerEvent in jsdom environment
if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && typeof window.PointerEvent === 'undefined') {
  class PointerEvent extends (window.MouseEvent || Object) {
    pointerId: number;
    width: number;
    height: number;
    pressure: number;
    pointerType: string;
    isPrimary: boolean;

    constructor(type: string, params: any = {}) {
      super(type, params);
      this.pointerId = params.pointerId ?? 0;
      this.width = params.width ?? 1;
      this.height = params.height ?? 1;
      this.pressure = params.pressure ?? 0;
      this.pointerType = params.pointerType ?? 'mouse';
      this.isPrimary = params.isPrimary ?? true;
    }
  }
  (window as any).PointerEvent = PointerEvent;
  (globalThis as any).PointerEvent = PointerEvent;
}

// Polyfill scrollIntoView in jsdom environment
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  if (typeof window.HTMLElement !== 'undefined' && typeof window.HTMLElement.prototype.scrollIntoView !== 'function') {
    window.HTMLElement.prototype.scrollIntoView = vi.fn();
  }
  if (typeof window.Element !== 'undefined' && typeof window.Element.prototype.scrollIntoView !== 'function') {
    window.Element.prototype.scrollIntoView = vi.fn();
  }
}

// Polyfill writable navigator.clipboard in jsdom environment
let _clipboard: any = {
  writeText: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined),
  readText: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(''),
};
function defineWritableClipboard(target: any) {
  if (!target) return;
  try {
    Object.defineProperty(target, 'clipboard', {
      get() {
        return _clipboard;
      },
      set(val) {
        _clipboard = val;
        if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.navigator) {
          try {
            Object.defineProperty(window.navigator, 'clipboard', {
              value: val,
              writable: true,
              configurable: true,
              enumerable: true,
            });
          } catch {}
        }
        if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined') {
          try {
            Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'clipboard', {
              value: val,
              writable: true,
              configurable: true,
              enumerable: true,
            });
          } catch {}
        }
      },
      configurable: true,
      enumerable: true,
    });
  } catch {}
}

if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.navigator) {
  defineWritableClipboard(window.navigator);
}
if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined') {
  defineWritableClipboard(navigator);
}

const origAdvance = vi.advanceTimersByTime.bind(vi);
vi.advanceTimersByTime = (ms: number) => {
  let result: any;
  act(() => {
    result = origAdvance(ms);
  });
  return result;
};

const origRunAll = vi.runAllTimers.bind(vi);
vi.runAllTimers = () => {
  let result: any;
  act(() => {
    result = origRunAll();
  });
  return result;
};

const origNextTimer = vi.advanceTimersToNextTimer.bind(vi);
vi.advanceTimersToNextTimer = (steps?: number) => {
  let result: any;
  act(() => {
    result = origNextTimer(steps);
  });
  return result;
};

"""
tests/test_validation_and_resolver.py - Unit tests for:
1. resolve_project_path containment resolver (server & agent)
2. ValidationResult blueprint structure, properties, and to_dict

import ast
import dataclasses
import sys
import tempfile
import pytest
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))


def load_definitions(path, names, namespace=None):
    """Load production definitions without starting server/model side effects."""
    if namespace is None:
        namespace = {"Path": Path, "dataclasses": dataclasses}
    tree = ast.parse((ROOT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    nodes = [n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) and n.name in names]
    for node in nodes:
        if hasattr(node, "decorator_list") and not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
            node.decorator_list = []
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(path), "exec"), namespace)
    return namespace


# Load resolvers cleanly without starting GPU/server
sessions_defs = load_definitions("server/sessions.py", ["resolve_project_path"])
server_defs = load_definitions("server/app.py", ["resolve_project_path"])
agent_defs = load_definitions("agent/agent.py", ["resolve_project_path"])

sessions_resolver = sessions_defs["resolve_project_path"]
server_resolver = server_defs["resolve_project_path"]
agent_resolver = agent_defs["resolve_project_path"]
from agent.project_validator import ValidationResult

from server.sessions import Session


# ── 1. resolve_project_path Tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────

@pytest.mark.parametrize("resolver", [sessions_resolver, server_resolver, agent_resolver])
def test_resolver_accepts_valid_relative_paths(resolver):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        root = Path(tmp_dir)
        # Simple relative
        resolved = resolver(root, "src/components/Header.tsx")
        assert resolved == (root / "src/components/Header.tsx").resolve()
        assert str(resolved).startswith(str(root.resolve()))

        # Subdirectory relative
        resolved2 = resolver(root, "styles/main.css")
        assert resolved2 == (root / "styles/main.css").resolve()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("resolver", [sessions_resolver, server_resolver, agent_resolver])
def test_resolver_blocks_traversal(resolver):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        root = Path(tmp_dir)
        escape_payloads = [
            "../../server/app.py",
            "../../../etc/passwd",
            r"..\..\..\Windows\win.ini",
            "foo/../../../../escape.txt",
            "src/components/../../../../sensitive.key",
        ]
        for payload in escape_payloads:
            with pytest.raises(PermissionError, match="outside project root"):
                resolver(root, payload)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("resolver", [sessions_resolver, server_resolver, agent_resolver])
def test_resolver_strips_leading_slashes(resolver):

        root = Path(tmp_dir)
        # Leading slash should not escape to filesystem root
        resolved = resolver(root, "/src/App.tsx")
        assert resolved == (root / "src/App.tsx").resolve()

        resolved_bs = resolver(root, r"\src\App.tsx")

# ── 3. Session revert_to_checkpoint traversal defense ─────────────────────────

def test_session_revert_guards_traversal_payloads():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        session = Session(session_id="1789999999_abcdef", workspace_dir=tmp_dir)
        # Create a checkpoint that contains a malicious relative path
        malicious_checkpoint = {
            "turn_num": 1,
            "timestamp": "2026-09-17 12:00:00",
            "summary": "Malicious checkpoint",
            "files": {
                "../../escaped.txt": "EVIL CONTENT",
                "valid.txt": "SAFE CONTENT",
            },
        }
        session.checkpoints.append(malicious_checkpoint)

        # Reverting should NOT write escaped.txt outside workspace
        outside_file = Path(tmp_dir).parent / "escaped.txt"
        assert not outside_file.exists()

        revert_ok = session.revert_to_checkpoint(1)
        assert revert_ok is True

        # Ensure outside_file was NEVER created
        assert not outside_file.exists()

        # Ensure valid.txt was written safely
        valid_file = Path(tmp_dir) / "valid.txt"
        assert valid_file.exists()
        assert valid_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "SAFE CONTENT"

def test_project_entity_structure_component_and_site():
    """Verify that both component and site generation intents produce the exact same Project entity:
    Project
     ├── workspace/
     ├── Conversation
     ├── Tasks
     ├── Snapshots
     ├── Build state
     └── Preview
    """
    from server.sessions import Project, SessionManager
    sm = SessionManager()

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        # 1. Component Intent Project
        comp_proj = Project(
            session_id="1789777777_112233",
            title="Lumina",
            mode="component",
            prompt="Build Lumina theme toggle",
            workspace_dir=tmp_dir,
            build_state={
                "typecheck_passed": True,
                "build_passed": True,
                "lint_passed": True,
                "runtime_passed": True,
                "errors": [],
                "warnings": [],
                "repair_attempts": 0,
            },
            current_plan=[
                {"task": "Synthesize Lumina", "status": "completed", "file": "Lumina.tsx"},
                {"task": "Verify types & syntax", "status": "completed"},
                {"task": "Bundle preview runner", "status": "completed"},

        assert comp_proj.workspace_dir == Path(tmp_dir)
        (Path(tmp_dir) / "Lumina.tsx").write_text("export const Lumina = () => <div>Lumina</div>;", encoding="utf-8")
        assert "Lumina.tsx" in comp_proj.get_current_files()

        # 1b. Conversation
        comp_proj.history.append({"role": "user", "content": "Build Lumina theme toggle"})
        comp_proj.history.append({"role": "assistant", "turn_id": 1, "summary": "## What I did\n- Created Lumina"})
        assert len(comp_proj.history) == 2

        # 1c. Tasks
        assert len(comp_proj.current_plan) == 3
        assert comp_proj.current_plan[0]["task"] == "Synthesize Lumina"

        # 1d. Snapshots
        chk_id = comp_proj.create_checkpoint("Initial component Lumina")
        assert chk_id == 1
        assert len(comp_proj.checkpoints) == 1
        assert "Lumina.tsx" in comp_proj.checkpoints[0]["files"]

        # 1e. Build state
        assert comp_proj.build_state["typecheck_passed"] is True
        assert comp_proj.build_state["repair_attempts"] == 0

        # 1f. Preview
        assert comp_proj.preview["url"] == "/preview/1789777777_112233"
        assert comp_proj.preview["symbol"] == "Lumina"

        # Serialization check
        comp_dict = comp_proj.to_dict()
        assert "workspace_dir" in comp_dict
        assert "history" in comp_dict
        assert "current_plan" in comp_dict
        assert "checkpoints" in comp_dict
        assert "build_state" in comp_dict
        assert "preview" in comp_dict

        # 2. Site Intent Project (produces the exact same schema)
        site_proj = Project(
            session_id="1789666666_445566",
            title="Portfolio",
            mode="site",
            prompt="Build dark developer portfolio",
            build_state={
                "typecheck_passed": True,
                "build_passed": True,
                "lint_passed": True,
                "runtime_passed": True,
                "errors": [],
                "warnings": [],
                "repair_attempts": 1,
            },
            current_plan=[
                {"task": "Section: header", "status": "completed"},
                {"task": "Section: hero", "status": "completed"},
                {"task": "Section: footer", "status": "completed"},
            ],
        )

        site_dict = site_proj.to_dict()
        # Ensure identical top-level keys
        assert set(comp_dict.keys()) == set(site_dict.keys())
        assert comp_dict["mode"] == "component"
        assert site_dict["mode"] == "site"

"""Regressions for model ownership, authentication and generated-content checks."""
import ast
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import queue
import re
import subprocess
import threading

from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import Mock

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def load_definitions(path, names, namespace):
    """Load production definitions without starting server/model side effects."""
    tree = ast.parse((ROOT / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    nodes = [n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) and n.name in names]
    for node in nodes:
        if hasattr(node, "decorator_list"):
            node.decorator_list = []
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(path), "exec"), namespace)
    return namespace


def test_timeout_retains_model_ownership_until_generation_exits():
    started, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
    calls = []
    real_thread = threading.Thread

    class ImmediateTimeoutThread(real_thread):
        def join(self, timeout=None):
            # Simulate expiry without waiting forty minutes.
            if timeout is not None:
                started.wait(2)
                return
            return super().join()

    def generate(task, events):
        calls.append(task["task_id"])
        if task["task_id"] == "first":
            started.set()
            assert release.wait(5)

    tasks = queue.Queue()
    for task in ({"task_id": "first"}, {"task_id": "second"}, None):
        tasks.put(task)
    ns = dict(_generation_queue=tasks, task_queues={}, cancelled_tasks=set(),
              _runner=SimpleNamespace(stop_check=None), _runner_lock=threading.Lock(),
              _model_status="ready", _current_task=None,
              threading=SimpleNamespace(Thread=ImmediateTimeoutThread),
              _run_generation=generate, _run_site_generation=generate,
              _run_session_edit_turn=generate)
    load_definitions("server/app.py", {"_worker"}, ns)
    worker = real_thread(target=ns["_worker"], daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    try:
        assert started.wait(2)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 2
        while "first" not in ns["cancelled_tasks"] and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(.01)
        assert "first" in ns["cancelled_tasks"]
        assert ns["_model_status"] == "busy"
        assert ns["_current_task"]["task_id"] == "first"
        assert ns["_runner_lock"].locked()
        assert calls == ["first"]
    finally:
        release.set()
        worker.join(3)
    assert not worker.is_alive()
    assert calls == ["first", "second"]
    assert ns["_runner"].stop_check is None

def test_generation_moves_to_embedding_device_and_stops(monkeypatch):
    import sys

    ns = dict(DEFAULT_INFERENCE_MAX_SEQ_LENGTH=8192, DEFAULT_MAX_NEW_TOKENS=4096,

            return self["input_ids"]
        def to(self, device):

            return self

    runner.tokenizer.eos_token_id = 0

        runner.generate_turn(0, [], "Demo", max_new_tokens=16)
    runner.stop_check = lambda: True
    with pytest.raises(InterruptedError):
        runner.generate_turn(0, [], "Demo", max_new_tokens=4)
    cancelled = [False]
    runner.stop_check = lambda: cancelled[0]
    def cancel_during_generate(**kwargs):
        cancelled[0] = True

        return torch.tensor([[1, 2, 3]])
    runner.model.generate.side_effect = cancel_during_generate
    with pytest.raises(InterruptedError):
        runner.generate_turn(0, [], "Demo", max_new_tokens=4)


def test_dynamic_context_headroom_clamping():
    import sys
    import torch
    ns = dict(DEFAULT_INFERENCE_MAX_SEQ_LENGTH=8192, DEFAULT_MAX_NEW_TOKENS=4096,
              List=list, Dict=dict, format_chatml=lambda *a, **k: "prompt", re=re)
    load_definitions("agent/agent.py", {"AgentModelRunner"}, ns)
    cls = ns["AgentModelRunner"]
    runner = cls.__new__(cls)
    runner.is_mock = False
    runner.stop_check = None
    runner.max_seq_length = 50

    class Inputs(dict):
        @property
        def input_ids(self):
            return self["input_ids"]
        def to(self, device):
            return self

    # Input length is 30, max_seq_length is 50. Request 40 new tokens (30 + 40 > 50).
    # With headroom, it should clamp max_new_tokens to fit within 50 without raising ValueError.
    runner.tokenizer = Mock(return_value=Inputs(input_ids=torch.ones(1, 30, dtype=torch.long), attention_mask=torch.ones(1, 30)))
    runner.tokenizer.eos_token_id = 0
    runner.tokenizer.decode.return_value = "done"
    runner.model = Mock()
    runner.model.get_input_embeddings.return_value.weight = torch.zeros(1)
    
    captured_kwargs = {}
    def mock_gen(**kwargs):
        captured_kwargs.update(kwargs)
        return torch.ones(1, 35, dtype=torch.long)
    runner.model.generate.side_effect = mock_gen

    out = runner.generate_turn(0, [], "Demo", max_new_tokens=40)
    assert out == "done"
    # Verify max_new_tokens was clamped to available budget (50 - 30 - margin <= 20)
    assert captured_kwargs["max_new_tokens"] < 40
    assert captured_kwargs["max_new_tokens"] <= 20

def test_allocate_port_sequential():

def test_allocate_port_skips_bound_socket():
    """Verify that allocatePort detects and skips an OS-bound port."""
    pm = PreviewManager(base_port=5180, max_port=5190)

    # Bind port 5180 with a real socket to simulate an external process
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    try:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 5180))
        s.listen(1)

        # allocatePort should detect that 5180 is unavailable and skip to 5181
        next_port = pm.allocatePort()
        assert next_port != 5180
        assert next_port >= 5181
    finally:
        s.close()

    assert "(cwd: /workspace)" in log

def test_command_completed_dual_presentation():

    # Success

        type=AgentEventType.COMMAND_COMPLETED,
        data={"command": "npm run build", "exit_code": 0, "duration_ms": 820.0},
    )
    assert "✓ Build passed" in evt_ok.to_chat_message()
    assert "820" in evt_ok.to_chat_message()
    assert "[Command] Exited with code 0: npm run build" in evt_ok.to_log_line()

    # Failure
    evt_fail = AgentEvent(
        type=AgentEventType.COMMAND_COMPLETED,
        data={"command": "npm run build", "exit_code": 1, "duration_ms": 300.0},
    )
    assert "✗ `npm run build` failed (exit code 1)" in evt_fail.to_chat_message()

def test_event_bus_subscription_and_dispatch():
    """Verify that published events reach all subscribers for a given task_id."""
    bus = EventBus()
    task_id = "task-test-123"

    sub1 = bus.subscribe(task_id)
    sub2 = bus.subscribe(task_id)

    bus.publish(task_id, AgentEvent(
        type=AgentEventType.COMMAND_STARTED,
        data={"command": "npm run build"},
    ))

    msg1 = sub1.get(timeout=1)
    msg2 = sub2.get(timeout=1)

    assert msg1["type"] == "command.started"
    assert msg2["type"] == "command.started"
    assert msg1["chat"] == msg2["chat"]

    # Late subscriber replay
    sub3 = bus.subscribe(task_id)
    msg3 = sub3.get(timeout=1)
    assert msg3["type"] == "command.started"

    # Unsubscribe
    bus.unsubscribe(task_id, sub1)
    bus.clear_task(task_id)

def test_token_budget_enforcement_and_surplus_reallocation():

        selected_files=3000,
        related_files=1600,
        recent_conversation=900,
        build_diagnostics=700,
        reserve=392,
    )
    builder = ContextBuilder(budget=budget)

    # Large target files that test budget limits
    large_ts = "import React from 'react';\n" + "\n".join(f"const item{i} = {i};" for i in range(1500))
    files = {
        "src/components/BigComponent.tsx": large_ts,

    }

    built = builder.build_context(
        session=session,
        new_instruction="Update BigComponent with new styling",
        target_files=[("src/components/BigComponent.tsx", large_ts)],
        diagnostics=None,  # 0 tokens used -> surplus flows to selected_files
    )

    # 1. Total tokens must never exceed total budget
    assert built.token_usage.total <= budget.total

    # 2. Surplus was reallocated: diagnostics was 0, so selected_files received a surplus boost
    assert built.token_usage.build_diagnostics == 0
    assert built.token_usage.selected_files > 0

def test_monotonic_sequence_numbers():

    e1 = bus.publish("t1", AgentEvent(type=AgentEventType.AGENT_STATUS, data={"status": "Planning"}), project_id=pid)
    e2 = bus.publish("t1", AgentEvent(type=AgentEventType.COMMAND_STARTED, data={"command": "npm run build"}), project_id=pid)
    e3 = bus.publish("t1", AgentEvent(type=AgentEventType.BUILD_RESULT, data={"passed": True}), project_id=pid)

    assert e1["eventId"] == 1
    assert e1["project_id"] == pid

    assert e2["seq"] == 2
    assert e2["eventId"] == 2

    assert e3["seq"] == 3
    assert e3["eventId"] == 3

    assert item2["type"] == "preview.ready"
    assert item2["url"] == "http://127.0.0.1:5173"

    bus.unsubscribe_project(pid, proj_q)


def test_dispatch_task_start_creates_queued_task():
    """Verifies _dispatch_task_start queues task and emits task.queued event."""
    session = session_manager.create_session(title="WSTestSite", mode="site", prompt="Initial prompt")
    res = _dispatch_task_start(session.session_id, "Add a hero section", mode="site")

    assert res["status"] == "queued"
    assert res["session_id"] == session.session_id
    assert "task_id" in res
    _dispatch_task_cancel(session.session_id)


def test_dispatch_task_cancel():
    """Verifies _dispatch_task_cancel cancels tasks and emits task.failed (cancelled)."""
    session = session_manager.create_session(title="CancelTestSite", mode="site", prompt="Prompt")
    res = _dispatch_task_start(session.session_id, "Add navbar")

    cancel_res = _dispatch_task_cancel(session.session_id, reason="user_cancelled")
    assert cancel_res["status"] == "cancelled"
    assert cancel_res["project_id"] == session.session_id


def test_dispatch_prompt_queue():
    """Verifies _dispatch_prompt_queue stores queued prompt and updates session."""
    session = session_manager.create_session(title="QueueTestSite", mode="site", prompt="Prompt")
    q_res = _dispatch_prompt_queue(session.session_id, "Make colors dark mode")

    assert q_res["status"] in ("prompt_queued", "queued")
    assert q_res["queue_depth"] >= 1
    s_loaded = session_manager.get_session(session.session_id)
    assert any(
        p == "Make colors dark mode" or (isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("prompt") == "Make colors dark mode")
        for p in s_loaded.queued_prompts
    )


def test_dispatch_preview_selection():

    sel_data = {
        "component": "Hero",
        "elementId": "hero-headline",
        "selector": ".hero__title",
        "coordinates": {"x": 120, "y": 300},
    }
    sel_res = _dispatch_preview_selection(session.session_id, sel_data)

    s_loaded = session_manager.get_session(session.session_id)
    assert s_loaded.preview_selection["component"] == "Hero"
    assert s_loaded.preview_selection["elementId"] == "hero-headline"


def test_live_project_websocket_endpoint():
    """
    Spins up the Flask test server on an ephemeral port and connects via websockets
    to /ws/projects/:projectId, testing connection.ready, bidirectional messaging,
    and sequence replay.
    """
    port = 5092
    server_url = f"ws://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server_ready = threading.Event()

    def run_server():
        server_ready.set()
        app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=port, debug=False, threaded=True)

    server_thread = threading.Thread(target=run_server, daemon=True)
    server_thread.start()
    server_ready.wait()
    time.sleep(0.8)

    session = session_manager.create_session(title="LiveWSSite", mode="site", prompt="Test prompt")
    proj_id = session.session_id

    async def run_client():
        async def recv_json(timeout=3.0):
            raw = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.recv(), timeout=timeout)
            return json.loads(raw)

        # 1. Connect to /ws/projects/:projectId
        async with websockets.connect(f"{server_url}/ws/projects/{proj_id}") as ws:
            # Initial greeting
            msg1 = await recv_json()
            assert msg1["type"] == "connection.ready"
            assert msg1["project_id"] == proj_id

            # Idle receive timeouts must keep the upgraded connection alive.
            await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
            await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "ping"}))
            assert (await recv_json())["type"] == "pong"

            # 2. Client sends preview.selection
            await ws.send(json.dumps({
                "type": "preview.selection",
                "component": "Navbar",
                "elementId": "nav-link-1",
            }))

            # Expect preview.selection_received AND activity.updated (in any order)
            msgs_received = set()
            for _ in range(2):
                m = await recv_json()
                msgs_received.add(m["type"])
            assert "preview.selection_received" in msgs_received
            assert "activity.updated" in msgs_received

            # 3. Client sends prompt.queue
            await ws.send(json.dumps({
                "type": "prompt.queue",
                "prompt": "Add subtle drop shadow to Navbar",
            }))

            # Expect prompt.queued AND activity.started (in any order)
            q_msgs = set()
            for _ in range(2):
                m = await recv_json()
                q_msgs.add(m["type"])
            assert "prompt.queued" in q_msgs
            assert "activity.started" in q_msgs

            # 4. Client sends task.cancel
            await ws.send(json.dumps({
                "type": "task.cancel",
                "reason": "testing_cancel",
            }))

            # Expect task.cancelled AND task.failed (in any order)
            cancel_msgs = set()
            for _ in range(2):
                m = await recv_json()
                cancel_msgs.add(m["type"])
            assert "task.cancelled" in cancel_msgs
            assert "task.failed" in cancel_msgs

    asyncio.run(run_client())


def test_task_started_and_cancelled_event_types():
    """Verifies TASK_STARTED and TASK_CANCELLED event types and emitter helpers."""
    assert AgentEventType.TASK_STARTED == "task.started"
    assert AgentEventType.TASK_CANCELLED == "task.cancelled"

    bus = EventBus()
    pid = "proj_types_test"
    tid = "task_types_123"

    emitter = TaskEventEmitter(task_id=tid, project_id=pid, bus=bus)
    proj_q = bus.subscribe_project(pid)

    s_evt = emitter.task_started(mode="site")
    c_evt = emitter.task_cancelled(reason="user_abort")

    assert s_evt["seq"] == 1
    assert s_evt["type"] == "task.started"
    assert s_evt["project_id"] == pid

    assert c_evt["seq"] == 2
    assert c_evt["type"] == "task.cancelled"
    assert c_evt["reason"] == "user_abort"

    bus.unsubscribe_project(pid, proj_q)


def test_rest_cancel_broadcasts_to_project_channel():
    """Verifies that calling REST /api/cancel/<task_id> broadcasts task.cancelled to the project channel."""
    from server.app import event_bus
    client = app.test_client()

    pid = "proj_rest_cancel_test"
    tid = "task_rest_cancel_999"

    # Bind task to project and subscribe to project channel
    event_bus.bind_task_to_project(tid, pid)
    proj_q = event_bus.subscribe_project(pid)

    try:
        resp = client.post(f"/api/cancel/{tid}")
        assert resp.status_code == 200

        # Verify project subscriber receives task.cancelled
        events = []
        while not proj_q.empty():
            events.append(proj_q.get_nowait())

        types = [e.get("type") for e in events]
        assert "task.cancelled" in types, f"Expected task.cancelled on project channel, got: {types}"
    finally:
        event_bus.unsubscribe_project(pid, proj_q)


def test_frontend_websocket_suite():
    """Executes the frontend Vite proxy and WebSocket integration tests via tsx."""
    import subprocess
    script_path = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "scripts" / "test_project_websocket_frontend.mjs"
    assert script_path.exists()

    res = subprocess.run(
        ["npx", "--yes", "tsx", str(script_path)],
        cwd=str(script_path.parent.parent),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        shell=True,
    )
    assert res.returncode == 0, f"Frontend WebSocket test failed:\nSTDOUT:\n{res.stdout}\nSTDERR:\n{res.stderr}"
    assert "ALL FRONTEND WEBSOCKET MIGRATION TESTS PASSED!" in res.stdout

import React, { useState } from 'react';
import './Menu.css';

interface MenuItem {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  category: 'bread' | 'viennoiserie' | 'patisserie' | 'cafe';
  price: string;
  description: string;
  badge?: string;
  tag: string;
}

const MENU_ITEMS: MenuItem[] = [
  {
    id: '1',
    name: 'Artisan Country Levain Boule',
    category: 'bread',
    price: '$9.50',
    description: '48-hour slow cold fermented rustic sourdough with a deeply caramelized, blistered crust and custard-like crumb.',
    badge: 'Signature',
    tag: '100% Organic Heritage Flour'
  },
  {
    id: '2',
    name: 'Almond Twice-Baked Croissant',
    category: 'viennoiserie',
    price: '$5.25',
    description: 'Flaky pure butter croissant filled with rich almond frangipane cream and topped with toasted sliced almonds.',
    badge: 'Bestseller',
    tag: 'French Normandy Butter'
  },
  {
    id: '3',
    name: 'Pain au Chocolat',
    category: 'viennoiserie',
    price: '$4.75',
    description: 'Golden honeycomb laminated pastry folded around two generous batons of rich Valrhona 70% dark chocolate.',
    tag: 'Valrhona 70%'
  },
  {
    id: '4',
    name: 'Classic Baguette de Tradition',
    category: 'bread',
    price: '$4.25',
    description: 'Hand-shaped Parisian classic with a thin, crackling crust, creamy open crumb, and hint of wild ferment sour.',
    badge: 'Baked at 6 AM',
    tag: 'Wild Sourdough Starter'
  },
  {
    id: '5',
    name: 'Bordeaux Vanilla Canelé',
    category: 'patisserie',
    price: '$4.00',
    description: 'Baked in traditional copper molds for a caramelized, crunchy beeswax shell with a moist rum custard heart.',
    tag: 'Madagascar Vanilla'
  },
  {
    id: '6',
    name: 'Cardamom Morning Bun',
    category: 'viennoiserie',
    price: '$4.50',
    description: 'Spiral croissant dough tossed in coarse sugar, Ceylon cinnamon, and fresh cracked green cardamom seeds.',
    badge: 'Staff Favorite',
    tag: 'Stone Ground Spices'
  },
  {
    id: '7',
    name: 'Seasonal Fruit & Mascarpone Tart',
    category: 'patisserie',
    price: '$6.50',
    description: 'Crisp sablé breton crust layered with whipped vanilla mascarpone and glazed local orchard berries.',
    tag: 'Local Farm Fresh'
  },
  {
    id: '8',
    name: 'Cortado & Oat Flat White',
    category: 'cafe',
    price: '$4.50',
    description: 'Double shot of single-origin Ethiopian roast espresso with silky textured steamed milk or minor figures oat milk.',
    tag: 'Single-Origin Roast'
  }
];

export function Menu() {
  const [activeCategory, setActiveCategory] = useState<string>('all');

  const filteredItems = activeCategory === 'all'
    ? MENU_ITEMS
    : MENU_ITEMS.filter(item => item.category === activeCategory);

  return (
    <section className="menu-section" id="menu" aria-label="Bakery Menu">
      <div className="menu-section__container">
        <div className="menu-section__header">
          <span className="menu-section__eyebrow">Fresh Out of the Hearth</span>
          <h2 className="menu-section__title">Daily Artisanal Menu</h2>
          <p className="menu-section__subtitle">
            All our breads and pastries are made by hand daily in small batches using French Normandy butter, organic stone-milled grains, and 48-hour cold proofing.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div className="menu-section__filters" role="tablist" aria-label="Menu categories">
          {[
            { key: 'all', label: 'All Items' },
            { key: 'bread', label: 'Hearth Breads' },
            { key: 'viennoiserie', label: 'Viennoiserie' },
            { key: 'patisserie', label: 'Pâtisserie' },
            { key: 'cafe', label: 'Café & Drinks' }
          ].map(tab => (
            <button
              key={tab.key}
              role="tab"
              aria-selected={activeCategory === tab.key}
              className={`menu-filter-btn ${activeCategory === tab.key ? 'menu-filter-btn--active' : ''}`}
              onClick={() => setActiveCategory(tab.key)}
            >
              {tab.label}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>

        <div className="menu-section__grid">
          {filteredItems.map(item => (
            <div className="menu-card" key={item.id}>
              <div className="menu-card__top">
                <span className="menu-card__tag">{item.tag}</span>
                {item.badge && <span className="menu-card__badge">{item.badge}</span>}
              </div>
              <div className="menu-card__header">
                <h3 className="menu-card__name">{item.name}</h3>
                <span className="menu-card__price">{item.price}</span>
              </div>
              <p className="menu-card__description">{item.description}</p>
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>

        <div className="menu-section__notice">
          <p>
            🌾 <strong>Allergies &amp; Dietary:</strong> Vegan, nut-free, and seeded options available upon request. Ask our baristas and bakers for today's seasonal baker's specials.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

export default Menu;

/* Menu.css - Artisanal Bakery Menu Styles */
.menu-section {
  width: 100%;

}

}

}

}

  background: #292524;
  color: #ffffff;
}

.menu-section__grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr));

}

.menu-card {
  background: #fdfbf7;

}

}

  align-items: center;

  margin-bottom: 0.85rem;
}

.menu-card__tag {
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: #78716c;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
}

.menu-card__badge {
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  background: rgba(194, 65, 12, 0.1);
  color: var(--accent-color, #c2410c);
  padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem;
  border-radius: 9999px;
}

.menu-card__header {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 1rem;
  margin-bottom: 0.65rem;
}

.menu-card__name {
  font-family: var(--font-heading, 'Fraunces', serif);

.menu-card__description {

}

.menu-section__notice {

@media (max-width: 640px) {

import React, { useState } from 'react';
import './Contact.css';

export default function Contact() {
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false);

  const handleSubmit = (e: React.FormEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    setSubmitted(true);
  };

  return (
    <section id="contact" className="contact" aria-label="Contact and Visit Us">
      <div className="contact__container">
        <div className="contact__header">
          <span className="contact__eyebrow">Visit &amp; Connect</span>
          <h2 className="contact__title">Join Us at the Counter</h2>
          <p className="contact__subtitle">
            Whether ordering custom pastry boxes for your weekend gathering or simply dropping in for a morning baguette, we would love to welcome you.
          </p>
        </div>

        <div className="contact__content-grid">
          <div className="contact__info-card">
            <h3 className="contact__info-heading">Bakery &amp; Café Hours</h3>
            
            <div className="contact__info-row">
              <span className="contact__info-icon">🕒</span>
              <div>
                <strong>Baking Schedule</strong>
                <p>Tuesday – Saturday: 6:30 AM – 4:00 PM</p>
                <p>Sunday: 7:00 AM – 2:00 PM</p>
                <p className="contact__info-sub">Monday: Closed for levain refreshment &amp; milling</p>
              </div>
            </div>

            <div className="contact__info-row">
              <span className="contact__info-icon">📍</span>
              <div>
                <strong>Location</strong>
                <p>428 Heritage Boulevard, Suite 100</p>
                <p>Old Mill Arts District</p>
              </div>
            </div>

            <div className="contact__info-row">
              <span className="contact__info-icon">📞</span>
              <div>
                <strong>Phone &amp; Preorders</strong>
                <p>(555) 742-8392</p>
                <p className="contact__info-sub">For catering &amp; event loaves, order 48h in advance</p>
              </div>
            </div>

            <div className="contact__info-row">
              <span className="contact__info-icon">✉️</span>
              <div>
                <strong>Email</strong>
                <p>bonjour@lumierebakery.com</p>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>

          <div className="contact__form-card">
            <h3 className="contact__form-title">Send a Message or Catering Request</h3>
            
            {submitted ? (
              <div className="contact__success-message">
                <h4>Merci Beaucoup!</h4>
                <p>Your message has reached our head baker. We will respond within 24 hours.</p>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className="contact__form-submit"
                  onClick={() => setSubmitted(false)}
                  style={{ marginTop: '1.5rem' }}
                >
                  Send Another Inquiry
                </button>
              </div>
            ) : (
              <form className="contact__form" onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
                <div className="contact__form-row">
                  <div className="contact__form-group">
                    <label htmlFor="name" className="contact__form-label">Full Name</label>
                    <input type="text" id="name" className="contact__form-input" placeholder="Claire Delacroix" required />
                  </div>
                  <div className="contact__form-group">
                    <label htmlFor="email" className="contact__form-label">Email Address</label>
                    <input type="email" id="email" className="contact__form-input" placeholder="claire@example.com" required />
                  </div>
                </div>

                <div className="contact__form-group">
                  <label htmlFor="subject" className="contact__form-label">Inquiry Type</label>
                  <select id="subject" className="contact__form-input">
                    <option value="general">General Question</option>
                    <option value="catering">Special Event / Pastry Catering</option>
                    <option value="wholesale">Wholesale Sourdough Inquiries</option>
                    <option value="feedback">Feedback for our Bakers</option>
                  </select>
                </div>

                <div className="contact__form-group">
                  <label htmlFor="message" className="contact__form-label">Message</label>
                  <textarea
                    id="message"
                    className="contact__form-textarea"
                    rows={4}
                    placeholder="Tell us what you are planning or inquiring about..."
                    required
                  ></textarea>
                </div>

                <button type="submit" className="contact__form-submit">
                  Send Message &rarr;
                </button>
              </form>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

import './Header.css';

export function Header() {
  const [isDrawerOpen, setIsDrawerOpen] = useState(false);

  return (
    <header className="header" data-scroll="sticky-top">
      <div className="header__inner">
        <a href="#" className="header__logo" aria-label="Kohī Lab Home">
          Kōhī Lab
        </a>
        <nav className="header__nav">
          <ul className="header__list">
            <li className="header__item">
              <a href="#hero" className="header__link">Home</a>
            </li>
            <li className="header__item">
              <a href="#features" className="header__link">Features</a>
            </li>
            <li className="header__item">
              <a href="#contact" className="header__link">Contact</a>
            </li>
          </ul>
        </nav>
        <div className="header__actions">
          <a href="mailto:hello@kohilab.com" className="header__btn">Say Hi</a>
          <button
            type="button"
            className="header__toggle"
            aria-label="Toggle Menu"
            onClick={() => setIsDrawerOpen(!isDrawerOpen)}
          >
            <span className="bar bar--top"></span>
            <span className="bar bar--mid"></span>
            <span className="bar bar--bot"></span>
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
      {isDrawerOpen && (
        <div className="header__drawer">
          <button
            type="button"
            className="header__close"
            aria-label="Close Menu"
            onClick={() => setIsDrawerOpen(false)}
          >
            <span className="bar bar--top"></span>
            <span className="bar bar--mid"></span>
            <span className="bar bar--bot"></span>

          <ul className="header__list">

            </li>
            <li className="header__item">
              <a href="#contact" className="header__link">Contact</a>
            </li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      )}
    </header>
  );
}

                </svg>

                <span className="sa-contact__card-meta">Mon – Fri, 9am – 6pm EST</span>
              </div>
            </div>

            <div className="sa-contact__card">
              <div className="sa-contact__icon-wrap">
                <svg width="22" height="22" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">

                    id="contact-message"
