`````tsx
                    placeholder="Describe your deployment environment, scale requirements, or questions..."
                    value={formData.message}
                    onChange={(e) => setFormData({ ...formData, message: e.target.value })}
                    required
                  />
                </div>
                <button type="submit" className="sa-contact__btn sa-contact__btn--submit">Submit Inquiry &rarr;</button>
              </form>
`````

- **Fence**: 5 backticks
- **Description**: Jinja2 chat template for Qwen2.5-Coder formatting system instructions, user prompts, tool calls, and observations.

`````text
{%- if tools %}
    {{- '<|im_start|>system\n' }}
    {%- if messages[0]['role'] == 'system' %}
        {{- messages[0]['content'] }}
    {%- else %}
        {{- 'You are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.' }}
    {%- endif %}
    {{- "\n\n# Tools\n\nYou may call one or more functions to assist with the user query.\n\nYou are provided with function signatures within <tools></tools> XML tags:\n<tools>" }}
    {%- for tool in tools %}
        {{- "\n" }}
        {{- tool | tojson }}
    {%- endfor %}
    {{- "\n</tools>\n\nFor each function call, return a json object with function name and arguments within <tool_call></tool_call> XML tags:\n<tool_call>\n{\"name\": <function-name>, \"arguments\": <args-json-object>}\n</tool_call><|im_end|>\n" }}
{%- else %}
    {%- if messages[0]['role'] == 'system' %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>system\n' + messages[0]['content'] + '<|im_end|>\n' }}
    {%- else %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>system\nYou are Qwen, created by Alibaba Cloud. You are a helpful assistant.<|im_end|>\n' }}
    {%- endif %}
{%- endif %}
{%- for message in messages %}
    {%- if (message.role == "user") or (message.role == "system" and not loop.first) or (message.role == "assistant" and not message.tool_calls) %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>' + message.role + '\n' + message.content + '<|im_end|>' + '\n' }}
    {%- elif message.role == "assistant" %}
        {{- '<|im_start|>' + message.role }}
        {%- if message.content %}
            {{- '\n' + message.content }}
        {%- endif %}
        {%- for tool_call in message.tool_calls %}
            {%- if tool_call.function is defined %}
                {%- set tool_call = tool_call.function %}
            {%- endif %}
            {{- '\n<tool_call>\n{"name": "' }}
            {{- tool_call.name }}
            {{- '", "arguments": ' }}
            {{- tool_call.arguments | tojson }}
            {{- '}\n</tool_call>' }}
        {%- endfor %}
        {{- '<|im_end|>\n' }}
    {%- elif message.role == "tool" %}
        {%- if (loop.index0 == 0) or (messages[loop.index0 - 1].role != "tool") %}
            {{- '<|im_start|>user' }}
        {%- endif %}
        {{- '\n<tool_response>\n' }}
        {{- message.content }}
        {{- '\n</tool_response>' }}
        {%- if loop.last or (messages[loop.index0 + 1].role != "tool") %}
            {{- '<|im_end|>\n' }}
        {%- endif %}
    {%- endif %}
{%- endfor %}
{%- if add_generation_prompt %}
    {{- '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}
{%- endif %}
`````

- **Fence**: 5 backticks
- **Description**: Model card documenting fine-tuning details and base model lineage.

`````markdown
---
base_model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct
library_name: peft
pipeline_tag: text-generation
tags: [lora, react, typescript]
---

# ReactAgent LoRA

Adapter for React, TypeScript and CSS generation with compiler/test feedback. Generated code needs review, particularly interactive behavior and complex generic types.

## Verified export identity (September 15, 2026)

The local adapter weights match `agent_lora_output/checkpoint-46/adapter_model.safetensors` byte for byte:

```text
SHA256 82cc3d7686238c2ae2400a710eee423cd0f0baa2088f2cee255e53c1fb0dedf3
```

The export records rank 16, alpha 16, **dropout 0.0**, targeting `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_proj`, `up_proj`, `down_proj`. The matching checkpoint records 46 steps, one epoch, batch size 1, and no validation metric or best checkpoint. This differs from the historical 96-step run below. Its exact training dataset snapshot and hardware were not preserved in a manifest and cannot be established from weights alone.

The adapter references `./base-model` (Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct). Loading requires base and adapter weights, which may be excluded from Git. CPU inference uses Transformers float32; CUDA prefers Unsloth. CPU execution requires enough RAM for the base model.

## Historical training and evaluation

[PROJECT_JOURNEY.md](../docs/PROJECT_JOURNEY.md) documents an older run: 146 trajectories, response-only loss masking, three epochs, learning rate 1e-4, 96 steps, NVIDIA RTX 4050, and best validation loss 0.3503. Its dropout=0.05 statement is historical; it does not describe the current export configuration.

The log reports 153 held-out tasks, up to five agent turns, and 16.17 hours elapsed:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| First-turn passes | 60/153 (39.2%) |
| Additional passes after correction | 18/153 (11.8 percentage points) |
| Final passes | 78/153 (51.0%) |
| TSC + render | 30/42 (71.4%) |
| TSC + accessibility | 3/4 (75.0%) |
| TSC + interaction | 21/58 (36.2%) |
| TSC only | 24/49 (49.0%) |

These are historical log-reported results, **not a verified benchmark of checkpoint-46**. The current `docs/agent_results.json` and `docs/eval_results.json` contain mock runs of one and two tasks respectively. They cannot substantiate those scores. No fresh GPU benchmark was performed for this card.

## Limitations

The historical analysis groups 33/75 failures as unknown/multiple TypeScript errors and 8/75 as parse/syntax errors, with truncated output among the reported causes. Interactive state, event handling and ARIA targeting remain weak areas. Increasing the generation budget addresses a source of truncation; it does not establish better quality or solve generic-type reasoning.

Runtime defaults are an 8192-token context and 4096-token generation budget, configurable with `SLM_INFERENCE_MAX_SEQ_LENGTH` and `SLM_MAX_NEW_TOKENS`. Longer generations cost memory and latency. Re-evaluate the exact adapter and record its hash before making new quality claims.

## Evaluation

From the repository root with weights and Python/npm dependencies installed:

```sh
python agent/agent.py --model ./my-react-agent-lora --eval-set data/eval/react_ts_css_eval_set_combined.jsonl --max-turns 5 --no-best-of-2 --max-new-tokens 768 --max-seq-len 4096 --output docs/current_adapter_eval.json
```

This retains the historical token budget for comparison. Evaluate separately with `--max-new-tokens 4096 --max-seq-len 8192` to measure the runtime change. Preserve both outputs with the adapter and dataset hashes. No dataset licensing audit is recorded in the available training metadata.
`````

# Qwen3-4B
<a href="https://chat.qwen.ai/" target="_blank" style="margin: 2px;">
    <img alt="Chat" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%92%9C%EF%B8%8F%20Qwen%20Chat%20-536af5" style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle;"/>
</a>

## Qwen3 Highlights

Qwen3 is the latest generation of large language models in Qwen series, offering a comprehensive suite of dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. Built upon extensive training, Qwen3 delivers groundbreaking advancements in reasoning, instruction-following, agent capabilities, and multilingual support, with the following key features:

- **Uniquely support of seamless switching between thinking mode** (for complex logical reasoning, math, and coding) and **non-thinking mode** (for efficient, general-purpose dialogue) **within single model**, ensuring optimal performance across various scenarios.
- **Significantly enhancement in its reasoning capabilities**, surpassing previous QwQ (in thinking mode) and Qwen2.5 instruct models (in non-thinking mode) on mathematics, code generation, and commonsense logical reasoning.
- **Superior human preference alignment**, excelling in creative writing, role-playing, multi-turn dialogues, and instruction following, to deliver a more natural, engaging, and immersive conversational experience.
- **Expertise in agent capabilities**, enabling precise integration with external tools in both thinking and unthinking modes and achieving leading performance among open-source models in complex agent-based tasks.
- **Support of 100+ languages and dialects** with strong capabilities for **multilingual instruction following** and **translation**.

## Model Overview

**Qwen3-4B** has the following features:
- Type: Causal Language Models
- Training Stage: Pretraining & Post-training
- Number of Parameters: 4.0B
- Number of Paramaters (Non-Embedding): 3.6B
- Number of Layers: 36
- Number of Attention Heads (GQA): 32 for Q and 8 for KV
- Context Length: 32,768 natively and [131,072 tokens with YaRN](#processing-long-texts). 

For more details, including benchmark evaluation, hardware requirements, and inference performance, please refer to our [blog](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen3/), [GitHub](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3), and [Documentation](https://qwen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/).

> [!TIP]
> If you encounter significant endless repetitions, please refer to the [Best Practices](#best-practices) section for optimal sampling parameters, and set the ``presence_penalty`` to 1.5.

## Quickstart

The code of Qwen3 has been in the latest Hugging Face `transformers` and we advise you to use the latest version of `transformers`.

With `transformers<4.51.0`, you will encounter the following error:
```
KeyError: 'qwen3'
```

The following contains a code snippet illustrating how to use the model generate content based on given inputs. 
```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

model_name = "Qwen/Qwen3-4B"

# load the tokenizer and the model
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    model_name,
    torch_dtype="auto",
    device_map="auto"
)

# prepare the model input
prompt = "Give me a short introduction to large language model."
messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": prompt}
]
text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=False,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    enable_thinking=True # Switches between thinking and non-thinking modes. Default is True.
)
model_inputs = tokenizer([text], return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)

# conduct text completion
generated_ids = model.generate(
    **model_inputs,
    max_new_tokens=32768
)
output_ids = generated_ids[0][len(model_inputs.input_ids[0]):].tolist() 

# parsing thinking content
try:
    # rindex finding 151668 (</think>)
    index = len(output_ids) - output_ids[::-1].index(151668)
except ValueError:
    index = 0

thinking_content = tokenizer.decode(output_ids[:index], skip_special_tokens=True).strip("\n")
content = tokenizer.decode(output_ids[index:], skip_special_tokens=True).strip("\n")

print("thinking content:", thinking_content)
print("content:", content)
```

For deployment, you can use `sglang>=0.4.6.post1` or `vllm>=0.8.5` or to create an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint:
- SGLang:
    ```shell
    python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-4B --reasoning-parser qwen3
    ```
- vLLM:
    ```shell
    vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B --enable-reasoning --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1
    ```

For local use, applications such as Ollama, LMStudio, MLX-LM, llama.cpp, and KTransformers have also supported Qwen3.

## Switching Between Thinking and Non-Thinking Mode

> [!TIP]
> The `enable_thinking` switch is also available in APIs created by SGLang and vLLM. 
> Please refer to our documentation for [SGLang](https://qwen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/deployment/sglang.html#thinking-non-thinking-modes) and [vLLM](https://qwen.readthedocs.io/en/latest/deployment/vllm.html#thinking-non-thinking-modes) users.

### `enable_thinking=True`

By default, Qwen3 has thinking capabilities enabled, similar to QwQ-32B. This means the model will use its reasoning abilities to enhance the quality of generated responses. For example, when explicitly setting `enable_thinking=True` or leaving it as the default value in `tokenizer.apply_chat_template`, the model will engage its thinking mode.

```python
text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=False,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    enable_thinking=True  # True is the default value for enable_thinking
)
```

In this mode, the model will generate think content wrapped in a `<think>...</think>` block, followed by the final response.

> [!NOTE]
> For thinking mode, use `Temperature=0.6`, `TopP=0.95`, `TopK=20`, and `MinP=0` (the default setting in `generation_config.json`). **DO NOT use greedy decoding**, as it can lead to performance degradation and endless repetitions. For more detailed guidance, please refer to the [Best Practices](#best-practices) section.


### `enable_thinking=False`

We provide a hard switch to strictly disable the model's thinking behavior, aligning its functionality with the previous Qwen2.5-Instruct models. This mode is particularly useful in scenarios where disabling thinking is essential for enhancing efficiency.

```python
text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    tokenize=False,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    enable_thinking=False  # Setting enable_thinking=False disables thinking mode
)
```

In this mode, the model will not generate any think content and will not include a `<think>...</think>` block.

> [!NOTE]
> For non-thinking mode, we suggest using `Temperature=0.7`, `TopP=0.8`, `TopK=20`, and `MinP=0`. For more detailed guidance, please refer to the [Best Practices](#best-practices) section.

### Advanced Usage: Switching Between Thinking and Non-Thinking Modes via User Input

We provide a soft switch mechanism that allows users to dynamically control the model's behavior when `enable_thinking=True`. Specifically, you can add `/think` and `/no_think` to user prompts or system messages to switch the model's thinking mode from turn to turn. The model will follow the most recent instruction in multi-turn conversations.

Here is an example of a multi-turn conversation:

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

class QwenChatbot:
    def __init__(self, model_name="Qwen/Qwen3-4B"):
        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
        self.model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)
        self.history = []

    def generate_response(self, user_input):
        messages = self.history + [{"role": "user", "content": user_input}]

        text = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            messages,
            tokenize=False,
            add_generation_prompt=True
        )

        inputs = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")
        response_ids = self.model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=32768)[0][len(inputs.input_ids[0]):].tolist()
        response = self.tokenizer.decode(response_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)

        # Update history
        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_input})
        self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response})

        return response

# Example Usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    chatbot = QwenChatbot()

    # First input (without /think or /no_think tags, thinking mode is enabled by default)
    user_input_1 = "How many r's in strawberries?"
    print(f"User: {user_input_1}")
    response_1 = chatbot.generate_response(user_input_1)
    print(f"Bot: {response_1}")
    print("----------------------")

    # Second input with /no_think
    user_input_2 = "Then, how many r's in blueberries? /no_think"
    print(f"User: {user_input_2}")
    response_2 = chatbot.generate_response(user_input_2)
    print(f"Bot: {response_2}") 
    print("----------------------")

    # Third input with /think
    user_input_3 = "Really? /think"
    print(f"User: {user_input_3}")
    response_3 = chatbot.generate_response(user_input_3)
    print(f"Bot: {response_3}")
```

> [!NOTE]
> For API compatibility, when `enable_thinking=True`, regardless of whether the user uses `/think` or `/no_think`, the model will always output a block wrapped in `<think>...</think>`. However, the content inside this block may be empty if thinking is disabled.
> When `enable_thinking=False`, the soft switches are not valid. Regardless of any `/think` or `/no_think` tags input by the user, the model will not generate think content and will not include a `<think>...</think>` block.

## Agentic Use

Qwen3 excels in tool calling capabilities. We recommend using [Qwen-Agent](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Agent) to make the best use of agentic ability of Qwen3. Qwen-Agent encapsulates tool-calling templates and tool-calling parsers internally, greatly reducing coding complexity.

To define the available tools, you can use the MCP configuration file, use the integrated tool of Qwen-Agent, or integrate other tools by yourself.
```python
from qwen_agent.agents import Assistant

# Define LLM
llm_cfg = {
    'model': 'Qwen3-4B',

    # Use the endpoint provided by Alibaba Model Studio:
    # 'model_type': 'qwen_dashscope',
    # 'api_key': os.getenv('DASHSCOPE_API_KEY'),

    # Use a custom endpoint compatible with OpenAI API:
    'model_server': 'http://localhost:8000/v1',  # api_base
    'api_key': 'EMPTY',

    # Other parameters:
    # 'generate_cfg': {
    #         # Add: When the response content is `<think>this is the thought</think>this is the answer;
    #         # Do not add: When the response has been separated by reasoning_content and content.
    #         'thought_in_content': True,
    #     },
}

# Define Tools
tools = [
    {'mcpServers': {  # You can specify the MCP configuration file
            'time': {
                'command': 'uvx',
                'args': ['mcp-server-time', '--local-timezone=Asia/Shanghai']
            },
            "fetch": {
                "command": "uvx",
                "args": ["mcp-server-fetch"]
            }
        }
    },
  'code_interpreter',  # Built-in tools
]

# Define Agent
bot = Assistant(llm=llm_cfg, function_list=tools)

# Streaming generation
messages = [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/ Introduce the latest developments of Qwen'}]
for responses in bot.run(messages=messages):
    pass
print(responses)
```

## Processing Long Texts

Qwen3 natively supports context lengths of up to 32,768 tokens. For conversations where the total length (including both input and output) significantly exceeds this limit, we recommend using RoPE scaling techniques to handle long texts effectively. We have validated the model's performance on context lengths of up to 131,072 tokens using the [YaRN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00071) method.

YaRN is currently supported by several inference frameworks, e.g., `transformers` and `llama.cpp` for local use, `vllm` and `sglang` for deployment. In general, there are two approaches to enabling YaRN for supported frameworks:

- Modifying the model files:
  In the `config.json` file, add the `rope_scaling` fields:
    ```json
    {
        ...,
        "rope_scaling": {
            "rope_type": "yarn",
            "factor": 4.0,
            "original_max_position_embeddings": 32768
        }
    }
    ```
  For `llama.cpp`, you need to regenerate the GGUF file after the modification.

- Passing command line arguments:

  For `vllm`, you can use
    ```shell
    vllm serve ... --rope-scaling '{"rope_type":"yarn","factor":4.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":32768}' --max-model-len 131072  
    ```

  For `sglang`, you can use
    ```shell
    python -m sglang.launch_server ... --json-model-override-args '{"rope_scaling":{"rope_type":"yarn","factor":4.0,"original_max_position_embeddings":32768}}'
    ```

  For `llama-server` from `llama.cpp`, you can use
    ```shell
    llama-server ... --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4 --yarn-orig-ctx 32768
    ```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If you encounter the following warning
> ```
> Unrecognized keys in `rope_scaling` for 'rope_type'='yarn': {'original_max_position_embeddings'}
> ```
> please upgrade `transformers>=4.51.0`.

> [!NOTE]
> All the notable open-source frameworks implement static YaRN, which means the scaling factor remains constant regardless of input length, **potentially impacting performance on shorter texts.**
> We advise adding the `rope_scaling` configuration only when processing long contexts is required. 
> It is also recommended to modify the `factor` as needed. For example, if the typical context length for your application is 65,536 tokens, it would be better to set `factor` as 2.0. 

> [!NOTE]
> The default `max_position_embeddings` in `config.json` is set to 40,960. This allocation includes reserving 32,768 tokens for outputs and 8,192 tokens for typical prompts, which is sufficient for most scenarios involving short text processing. If the average context length does not exceed 32,768 tokens, we do not recommend enabling YaRN in this scenario, as it may potentially degrade model performance.

> [!TIP]
> The endpoint provided by Alibaba Model Studio supports dynamic YaRN by default and no extra configuration is needed.

## Best Practices

To achieve optimal performance, we recommend the following settings:

1. **Sampling Parameters**:
   - For thinking mode (`enable_thinking=True`), use `Temperature=0.6`, `TopP=0.95`, `TopK=20`, and `MinP=0`. **DO NOT use greedy decoding**, as it can lead to performance degradation and endless repetitions.
   - For non-thinking mode (`enable_thinking=False`), we suggest using `Temperature=0.7`, `TopP=0.8`, `TopK=20`, and `MinP=0`.
   - For supported frameworks, you can adjust the `presence_penalty` parameter between 0 and 2 to reduce endless repetitions. However, using a higher value may occasionally result in language mixing and a slight decrease in model performance.

2. **Adequate Output Length**: We recommend using an output length of 32,768 tokens for most queries. For benchmarking on highly complex problems, such as those found in math and programming competitions, we suggest setting the max output length to 38,912 tokens. This provides the model with sufficient space to generate detailed and comprehensive responses, thereby enhancing its overall performance.

3. **Standardize Output Format**: We recommend using prompts to standardize model outputs when benchmarking.
   - **Math Problems**: Include "Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}." in the prompt.
   - **Multiple-Choice Questions**: Add the following JSON structure to the prompt to standardize responses: "Please show your choice in the `answer` field with only the choice letter, e.g., `"answer": "C"`."

4. **No Thinking Content in History**: In multi-turn conversations, the historical model output should only include the final output part and does not need to include the thinking content. It is implemented in the provided chat template in Jinja2. However, for frameworks that do not directly use the Jinja2 chat template, it is up to the developers to ensure that the best practice is followed.

`````python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

scripts/verify_claims.py — Automated Source Claim Verification Engine

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, List, Optional, Tuple

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


# ── Color & Formatting Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _colorize(text: str, color_code: str) -> str:
    # Check if ANSI supported or NO_COLOR
    if os.environ.get("NO_COLOR") or not sys.stdout.isatty():
        return text
    return f"\033[{color_code}m{text}\033[0m"

def c_pass(text: str) -> str: return _colorize(text, "32;1") # Bright Green
def c_fail(text: str) -> str: return _colorize(text, "31;1") # Bright Red
def c_info(text: str) -> str: return _colorize(text, "36")   # Cyan
def c_bold(text: str) -> str: return _colorize(text, "1")    # Bold


# ── WCAG Contrast Calculator ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def srgb_luminance(hex_str: str) -> float:
    """Calculates relative luminance for an sRGB hex code per WCAG 2.1."""
    hex_clean = hex_str.strip().lstrip("#")
    if len(hex_clean) == 3:
        hex_clean = "".join(c * 2 for c in hex_clean)
    r = int(hex_clean[0:2], 16) / 255.0
    g = int(hex_clean[2:4], 16) / 255.0
    b = int(hex_clean[4:6], 16) / 255.0

    def adjust(v: float) -> float:
        return v / 12.92 if v <= 0.04045 else math.pow((v + 0.055) / 1.055, 2.4)

    return 0.2126 * adjust(r) + 0.7152 * adjust(g) + 0.0722 * adjust(b)

def contrast_ratio(hex1: str, hex2: str) -> float:
    """Computes contrast ratio between two hex colors (1.0 to 21.0)."""
    l1 = srgb_luminance(hex1)
    l2 = srgb_luminance(hex2)
    lighter = max(l1, l2)
    darker = min(l1, l2)
    return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)


# ── Assertion Primitives ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def read_file(rel_path: str) -> Tuple[Path, str]:
    p = BASE_DIR / rel_path
    if not p.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {p}")
    return p, p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

def assert_function_exists(rel_path: str, func_name: str) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    p, content = read_file(rel_path)
    pattern = rf'(?:def\s+{re.escape(func_name)}\s*\(|function\s+{re.escape(func_name)}\s*\(|(?:const|let|var)\s+{re.escape(func_name)}\s*=)'
    matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content))
    if matches:
        line_no = content[:matches[0].start()].count("\n") + 1
        return True, f"Found '{func_name}' at {rel_path}:{line_no}"
    return False, f"Function '{func_name}' NOT found in {rel_path}"

def assert_string_contains(rel_path: str, pattern: str, is_regex: bool = False) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    p, content = read_file(rel_path)
    if is_regex:
        matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content))
        if matches:
            line_no = content[:matches[0].start()].count("\n") + 1
            return True, f"Found match for pattern /{pattern}/ at {rel_path}:{line_no}"
        return False, f"Regex pattern /{pattern}/ not found in {rel_path}"
    else:
        idx = content.find(pattern)
        if idx != -1:
            line_no = content[:idx].count("\n") + 1
            return True, f"Found '{pattern}' at {rel_path}:{line_no}"
        return False, f"String '{pattern}' not found in {rel_path}"

def assert_string_absent(rel_path: str, pattern: str, is_regex: bool = False) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    p, content = read_file(rel_path)
    if is_regex:
        matches = list(re.finditer(pattern, content))
        if matches:
            line_no = content[:matches[0].start()].count("\n") + 1
            return False, f"Forbidden pattern /{pattern}/ was found at {rel_path}:{line_no}"
        return True, f"Verified /{pattern}/ is absent from {rel_path}"
    else:
        idx = content.find(pattern)
        if idx != -1:
            line_no = content[:idx].count("\n") + 1
            return False, f"Forbidden string '{pattern}' was found at {rel_path}:{line_no}"
        return True, f"Verified '{pattern}' is absent from {rel_path}"

def assert_occurrence_count(
    rel_path: str,
    pattern: str,
    min_count: Optional[int] = None,
    max_count: Optional[int] = None,
    exact_count: Optional[int] = None
) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    p, content = read_file(rel_path)
    matches = re.findall(pattern, content)
    count = len(matches)

    if exact_count is not None:
        if count == exact_count:
            return True, f"Occurrence count of /{pattern}/ in {rel_path} is exactly {count}"
        return False, f"Expected exactly {exact_count} occurrences of /{pattern}/ in {rel_path}, but found {count}"

    if min_count is not None and count < min_count:
        return False, f"Found {count} occurrences of /{pattern}/ in {rel_path}, below required minimum of {min_count}"

    if max_count is not None and count > max_count:
        return False, f"Found {count} occurrences of /{pattern}/ in {rel_path}, exceeding allowed maximum of {max_count}"

    bounds_desc = []
    if min_count is not None: bounds_desc.append(f">={min_count}")
    if max_count is not None: bounds_desc.append(f"<={max_count}")
    return True, f"Occurrence count of /{pattern}/ in {rel_path} is {count} ({', '.join(bounds_desc)})"

            claim_id="P6.6",

            verify_fn=lambda: assert_occurrence_count("web_ui_static/index.html", r'@media\b', min_count=3)
        ),
        Claim(
            phase=6,
            claim_id="P6.7",
            description="`server/app.py` exposes `/api/task/<task_id>/status` and `/api/generation/<task_id>/status`",
            verify_fn=lambda: (
                assert_string_contains("server/app.py", '@app.route("/api/task/<task_id>/status"') and
                assert_string_contains("server/app.py", '@app.route("/api/generation/<task_id>/status"')
            )
        ),
    ]
    return claims


# ── Verification Runner ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def run_claims(claims: List[Claim]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    passed = 0
    failed = 0

    # Group by phase
    phases = sorted(list(set(c.phase for c in claims)))
    for phase in phases:
        phase_claims = [c for c in claims if c.phase == phase]
        print(f"\n{c_bold(f'=== Phase {phase} Claims Verification ({len(phase_claims)} checks) ===')}")
        for c in phase_claims:
            try:
                ok, msg = c.verify_fn()
                if ok:
                    passed += 1
                    print(f"  {c_pass('[PASS]')} {c_bold(c.claim_id)}: {c.description}")
                    print(f"         {c_info(msg)}")
                else:
                    failed += 1
                    print(f"  {c_fail('[FAIL]')} {c_bold(c.claim_id)}: {c.description}")
                    print(f"         {c_fail(f'ERROR: {msg}')}")
            except Exception as e:
                failed += 1
                print(f"  {c_fail('[FAIL]')} {c_bold(c.claim_id)}: {c.description}")
                print(f"         {c_fail(f'EXCEPTION: {e}')}")

    return passed, failed


# ── Self-Test Engine ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def run_self_test() -> bool:
    print(c_bold("\n=== Running verify_claims.py Self-Test (Proving False Claims Are Caught) ==="))
    all_ok = True

    # Test 1: Bogus function claim
    bogus_func = "def totally_fake_function_that_does_not_exist"
    ok, msg = assert_function_exists("agent/site_brief.py", "totally_fake_function_that_does_not_exist")
    if not ok:
        print(f"  {c_pass('[PASS]')} Correctly caught false function claim: {msg}")
    else:
        print(f"  {c_fail('[FAIL]')} Failed to catch false function claim!")
        all_ok = False

    # Test 2: Bogus aria-label count (523 claimed vs 83 actual)
    ok, msg = assert_occurrence_count("web_ui_static/index.html", r'aria-label=', exact_count=523)
    if not ok:
        print(f"  {c_pass('[PASS]')} Correctly caught bogus aria-label count claim (523 claimed): {msg}")
    else:
        print(f"  {c_fail('[FAIL]')} Failed to catch bogus aria-label claim!")
        all_ok = False

    # Test 3: Bogus string absence claim (asserting a present string is absent)
    ok, msg = assert_string_absent("agent/site_brief.py", "def extract_explicit_sections")
    if not ok:
        print(f"  {c_pass('[PASS]')} Correctly caught false string absence claim: {msg}")
    else:
        print(f"  {c_fail('[FAIL]')} Failed to catch false string absence claim!")
        all_ok = False

    # Test 4: WCAG contrast ratio accuracy
    # #71717a on #09090b is ~3.5:1 (failing AA)
    ratio_fail = contrast_ratio("#71717a", "#09090b")
    # #a8a29e on #09090b is ~8.29:1 (passing AA)
    ratio_pass = contrast_ratio("#a8a29e", "#09090b")
    if ratio_fail < 4.5 and ratio_pass >= 4.5:
        print(f"  {c_pass('[PASS]')} WCAG calculator verified: #71717a={ratio_fail:.2f}:1 (<4.5), #a8a29e={ratio_pass:.2f}:1 (>=4.5)")
    else:
        print(f"  {c_fail('[FAIL]')} WCAG contrast calculation unexpected: fail={ratio_fail}, pass={ratio_pass}")
        all_ok = False

    return all_ok


# ── CLI Interface ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="verify_claims.py: Source-Grounded Claim Verification Engine for ReactAgent SLM",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
    )
    parser.add_argument("--phase", type=int, choices=[0, 1, 2, 4, 6], help="Verify claims for a specific phase")
    parser.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true", help="Run negative self-tests to prove false claims are caught")

    # Ad-hoc inspection flags
    parser.add_argument("--file", type=str, help="Relative path to file for ad-hoc check")
    parser.add_argument("--contains", type=str, help="Assert file contains this string")
    parser.add_argument("--not-contains", type=str, help="Assert file does NOT contain this string")
    parser.add_argument("--func", type=str, help="Assert function is defined in file")
    parser.add_argument("--count-regex", type=str, help="Regex to count occurrences in file")
    parser.add_argument("--min", type=int, help="Minimum count for --count-regex")
    parser.add_argument("--max", type=int, help="Maximum count for --count-regex")
    parser.add_argument("--exact", type=int, help="Exact count for --count-regex")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Self-test mode
    if args.self_test:
        ok = run_self_test()
        sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

    # Ad-hoc mode
    if args.file:
        if not (args.contains or args.not_contains or args.func or args.count_regex):
            print(c_fail("Error: Specify --contains, --not-contains, --func, or --count-regex with --file"))
            sys.exit(1)

        success = True
        if args.func:
            ok, msg = assert_function_exists(args.file, args.func)
            print(f"[{c_pass('PASS') if ok else c_fail('FAIL')}] {msg}")
            if not ok: success = False

        if args.contains:
            ok, msg = assert_string_contains(args.file, args.contains)
            print(f"[{c_pass('PASS') if ok else c_fail('FAIL')}] {msg}")
            if not ok: success = False

        if args.not_contains:
            ok, msg = assert_string_absent(args.file, args.not_contains)
            print(f"[{c_pass('PASS') if ok else c_fail('FAIL')}] {msg}")
            if not ok: success = False

        if args.count_regex:
            ok, msg = assert_occurrence_count(args.file, args.count_regex, min_count=args.min, max_count=args.max, exact_count=args.exact)
            print(f"[{c_pass('PASS') if ok else c_fail('FAIL')}] {msg}")
            if not ok: success = False

        sys.exit(0 if success else 1)

    # Standard Phase Verification mode
    claims = get_all_claims()
    if args.phase is not None:
        claims = [c for c in claims if c.phase == args.phase]

    print(c_bold("=================================================================="))
    print(c_bold(" ReactAgent SLM — Source-Grounded Claim Verification Engine"))
    print(c_bold("=================================================================="))
    print(f"Workspace Root: {BASE_DIR}")
    print(f"Targeting: {'Phase ' + str(args.phase) if args.phase is not None else 'All Confirmed Phases (0, 1, 2, 4, 6)'}")

    passed, failed = run_claims(claims)

    total = passed + failed
    print("\n" + c_bold("--- Claim Verification Summary ---"))
    print(f"Total Claims Tested: {total}")
    print(f"Passed: {c_pass(str(passed))}")
    print(f"Failed: {c_fail(str(failed)) if failed > 0 else '0'}")

    if failed > 0:
        print(c_fail(f"\nFAILED: {failed} claims could not be verified against the actual source code."))
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print(c_pass(f"\nSUCCESS: All {passed}/{total} claims independently verified against source code."))
        sys.exit(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
`````

- **Fence**: 5 backticks
- **Description**: Script compiling sealed held-out benchmark splits.

`````python
"""
Builds the sealed final benchmark and development benchmark splits.

1. Sealed Final Benchmark (153 tasks):
   - Canonical held-out benchmark derived from react_ts_css_eval_set_combined.jsonl
   - Enriched with stable task_id (bench_final_001..bench_final_153), family_id, and symbol
   - Sealed with cryptographic SHA-256 manifest: data/eval/sealed_final_benchmark_manifest.json

2. Development Benchmark (150 tasks):
   - Daily development benchmark derived from star_task_bank.jsonl
   - Enriched with dev_task_001..dev_task_150, dev_family_*, category, check, test_code
   - Strictly held out and disjoint from the sealed benchmark across all 6 checks
"""

import datetime
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
from typing import Tuple

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR))

from training.leakage_guard import (
    extract_symbols,
    audit_dataset_against_benchmark,
    SEALED_BENCHMARK_PATH,
    SEALED_MANIFEST_PATH,
    DEV_BENCHMARK_PATH,
    LEGACY_BENCHMARK_PATH,
)


def derive_component_symbol(prompt: str) -> str:
    """Extract the primary component symbol or hook name from the prompt."""
    # Look for backtick component name
    bt_matches = re.findall(r"`([A-Za-z0-9_]+)`", prompt)
    for m in bt_matches:
        if m.startswith("use") or (m[0].isupper() and not m.startswith("CSS")):
            return m
    # Look for PascalCase words
    pascal = re.findall(r"\b[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]+(?:[A-Z][a-z0-9]+)+\b", prompt)
    if pascal:
        return pascal[0]
    return "Component"


def build_sealed_benchmark() -> Tuple[Path, Path]:
    """Create data/eval/sealed_final_benchmark.jsonl and its manifest."""
    source_file = LEGACY_BENCHMARK_PATH
    if not source_file.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Source benchmark not found: {source_file}")

    target_file = SEALED_BENCHMARK_PATH
    target_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    items = []
    task_hashes = {}

    with open(source_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for idx, line in enumerate(f, 1):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            row = json.loads(line)
            task_id = f"bench_final_{idx:03d}"
            symbol = derive_component_symbol(row["prompt"])
            family_id = f"family_{symbol.lower()}"

            entry = {
                "task_id": task_id,
                "family_id": family_id,
                "symbol": symbol,
                "check": row.get("check", "tsc_and_render"),
                "prompt": row["prompt"].strip(),
                "test_code": row.get("test_code", ""),
            }
            items.append(entry)
            p_hash = hashlib.sha256(entry["prompt"].encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
            task_hashes[task_id] = p_hash

    # Write sealed benchmark lines
    with open(target_file, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        for item in items:
            f.write(json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    # Compute SHA-256
    sha = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(target_file, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            sha.update(chunk)
    file_hash = sha.hexdigest()

    manifest = {
        "status": "sealed",
        "benchmark_file": "data/eval/sealed_final_benchmark.jsonl",
        "task_count": len(items),
        "sha256": file_hash,
        "sealed_at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "purpose": "Authoritative held-out benchmark evaluated strictly at major checkpoints.",
        "leakage_checks_enforced": [
            "exact_prompt_matching",
            "normalized_matching",
            "symbol_overlap",
            "token_similarity",
            "family_level_holdout",
            "semantic_similarity_checks",
        ],
        "task_hashes": task_hashes,
    }

    with open(SEALED_MANIFEST_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

    print(f"Created sealed final benchmark: {target_file} ({len(items)} tasks, SHA: {file_hash[:12]}...)")
    print(f"Created manifest: {SEALED_MANIFEST_PATH}")
    return target_file, SEALED_MANIFEST_PATH


def build_dev_benchmark() -> Path:
    """Create data/eval/dev_benchmark.jsonl from clean non-leaking tasks."""
    star_file = BASE_DIR / "data" / "star_task_bank.jsonl"
    web_file = BASE_DIR / "data" / "website_task_bank.jsonl"
    if not star_file.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Star task bank not found: {star_file}")

    target_file = DEV_BENCHMARK_PATH
    target_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Load sealed benchmark prompts to filter out any semantic overlaps
    from training.leakage_guard import (
        compute_semantic_similarity,
        compute_token_jaccard,
        extract_symbols,
    )
    sealed = []
    if SEALED_BENCHMARK_PATH.exists():
        sealed = [json.loads(l) for l in open(SEALED_BENCHMARK_PATH, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]

    items = []
    skipped_count = 0
    with open(star_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for idx, line in enumerate(f, 1):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            row = json.loads(line)
            prompt = row["prompt"].strip()

            # Filter against sealed benchmark if semantic similarity is high
            is_leaky = any(
                compute_semantic_similarity(prompt, s["prompt"]) >= 0.58
                or compute_token_jaccard(prompt, s["prompt"]) >= 0.45
                for s in sealed
            )
            if is_leaky:
                skipped_count += 1
                continue

            symbol = row.get("symbol") or derive_component_symbol(prompt)
            family_id = f"dev_family_{symbol.lower()}"
            task_id = f"dev_task_{len(items) + 1:03d}"

            items.append({
                "task_id": task_id,
                "family_id": family_id,
                "symbol": symbol,
                "category": row.get("category", "general"),
                "check": row.get("check", "tsc_render_interact"),
                "prompt": prompt,
                "test_code": row.get("test_code", ""),
            })

    # Backfill with clean tasks from website_task_bank if needed to reach 150 tasks
    if len(items) < 150 and web_file.exists():
        with open(web_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                if len(items) >= 150:
                    break
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                row = json.loads(line)
                prompt = row["prompt"].strip()
                if any(
                    compute_semantic_similarity(prompt, s["prompt"]) >= 0.50
                    or compute_token_jaccard(prompt, s["prompt"]) >= 0.35
                    for s in sealed
                ):
                    continue
                symbol = row.get("symbol") or derive_component_symbol(prompt)
                task_id = f"dev_task_{len(items) + 1:03d}"
                items.append({
                    "task_id": task_id,
                    "family_id": f"dev_family_{symbol.lower()}",
                    "symbol": symbol,
                    "category": row.get("category", "layout"),
                    "check": row.get("check", "tsc_and_render"),
                    "prompt": prompt,
                    "test_code": row.get("test_code", ""),
                })

    with open(target_file, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        for item in items:
            f.write(json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    print(f"Created development benchmark: {target_file} ({len(items)} tasks, filtered {skipped_count} near-leaks)")
    return target_file


def main():
    build_sealed_benchmark()
    dev_path = build_dev_benchmark()

    # Audit dev benchmark against sealed benchmark across all 6 checks
    print("\nAuditing Development Benchmark against Sealed Final Benchmark...")
    report = audit_dataset_against_benchmark(
        dataset_path=str(dev_path),
        benchmark_path=str(SEALED_BENCHMARK_PATH),
        manifest_path=str(SEALED_MANIFEST_PATH),
    )
    print(f"Dev Benchmark Disjointness: {'PASSED (0 leaks)' if report.is_clean else 'FAILED'}")
    print(f"Total dev tasks: {report.total_candidate_samples}")
    print(f"Peak token similarity: {report.peak_token_similarity:.3f} (threshold: {report.token_threshold})")
    print(f"Peak semantic similarity: {report.peak_semantic_similarity:.3f} (threshold: {report.semantic_threshold})")
    if not report.is_clean:
        print(f"Violations detected: {report.breakdown}")
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from typing import Tuple
    main()
`````

`````python
"""Measure the real initial site request without loading a model or generating code."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import uuid
from tokenizers import Tokenizer

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT/'agent'))
from agent import run_site_agent_on_example
from agent_protocol import format_chatml
from site_brief import generate_content_brief, brief_to_xml


class Captured(BaseException):
    pass


class CaptureRunner:
    history = None
    def generate_turn(self, **kwargs):
        self.history = kwargs['history']
        raise Captured()


def main():
    prompt = json.loads((ROOT/'sessions/1789582016_b4b7d5.json').read_text(encoding='utf8'))['prompt']
    brief = generate_content_brief(prompt, provider='heuristic', resolve_images=False)
    runner = CaptureRunner()
    workspace = ROOT/'experiments'/'context-checks'/uuid.uuid4().hex
    try:
        run_site_agent_on_example(0,prompt,'NexaFlow',brief_to_xml(brief),brief['sections'],runner,workspace,
                                  brief=brief,style_spec=brief.get('style_spec'),
                                  custom_section_instructions=brief.get('custom_section_instructions'),
                                  strategy='freeform')
    except Captured:
        pass
    tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file(str(ROOT/'base-model/tokenizer.json'))
    count = len(tokenizer.encode(format_chatml(runner.history,add_generation_prompt=True)).ids)
    result = {'initial_prompt_tokens':count,'context_limit':8192,'requested_output_tokens':4096,
              'fits':count+4096<=8192,'sections':brief['sections'],
              'scope':'Exact initial request only; later history must also fit after compaction.'}
    (ROOT/'experiments'/'site-context-check.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2),encoding='utf8')
    print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
    return 0 if result['fits'] else 1


if __name__=='__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
`````

`````python
"""One deterministic held-out hero probe; never substitutes for visual evaluation."""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "agent"))
from agent import AgentModelRunner
from agent_protocol import SITE_AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, parse_agent_output, WriteSiteAction
from site_quality import prepare_site_quality
from evaluate import run_command


def evaluate(model_path, output):
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prompt = ('Build only the Hero section for Vela, a fictional developer workspace. '
              'Headline: Give your ideas form. Use a two-column layout, a working anchor CTA '
              'to #workflow, and the supplied 3D PremiumScene component. '
              'Write src/components/Hero.tsx and Hero.css. Export default function Hero. '
              'Do not invent metrics or customers. Support 375px screens and reduced motion.')
    instructions, _ = prepare_site_quality(prompt, output)
    runner = AgentModelRunner(str(model_path), max_seq_length=8192)
    start = time.monotonic()
    response = runner.generate_turn(0, [{"role": "system", "content": SITE_AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
                                      {"role": "user", "content": prompt + "\n" + instructions}],
                                    "Hero", max_new_tokens=2048, temperature=0)
    (output / "response.txt").write_text(response, encoding="utf-8")
    turn = parse_agent_output(response)
    files = dict(turn.action.files) if isinstance(turn.action, WriteSiteAction) else {}
    allowed = {"src/components/Hero.tsx", "src/components/Hero.css"}
    for name, content in files.items():
        if name in allowed:
            target = output / name
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    code = files.get("src/components/Hero.tsx", "")
    css = files.get("src/components/Hero.css", "")
    compiled = False
    diagnostics = "No expected Hero.tsx generated"
    if code:
        result = run_command(["npx", "tsc", "--noEmit", "--jsx", "react-jsx", "--target", "ES2022",
                              "--moduleResolution", "bundler", "--esModuleInterop", "--skipLibCheck",
                              str((output / "src/components/Hero.tsx").resolve()), "css.d.ts"], cwd=ROOT)
        compiled = result.returncode == 0
        diagnostics = result.stdout + result.stderr
    weights = model_path / "adapter_model.safetensors"
    report = {"model": str(model_path), "adapter_sha256": hashlib.sha256(weights.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),

              "has_responsive_rule": "@media" in css, "diagnostics": diagnostics,
              "visual_quality": "Not measured by this probe; render and review separately."}
    report['closed_envelope'] = response.count('</file>') == 2 and response.count('</tool_call>') == 1
    report['probe_pass'] = compiled and allowed <= set(files) and report['closed_envelope']
    if compiled and allowed <= set(files):
        (output / "package.json").write_text(json.dumps({"private": True, "type": "module", "scripts": {"dev": "vite"}}), encoding="utf-8")
        (output / "index.html").write_text('<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="UTF-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Vela probe</title></head><body><div id="root"></div><script type="module" src="/main.tsx"></script></body></html>', encoding="utf-8")

        from visual_judge import take_screenshot
        screenshot = take_screenshot(output.resolve(), output_path=(output / "probe.webp").resolve())
        report["screenshot"] = str(screenshot) if screenshot else None
    (output / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
`````

`````python
def evaluate(model, output):
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    runner = AgentModelRunner(str(model), max_seq_length=8192)
    results=[]
    for index,(name,(brief,test)) in enumerate(CASES.items()):
        destination=output/name
        destination.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        prompt=brief+f' Write exactly src/components/{name}.tsx and src/components/{name}.css. Export default function {name}. Return complete closed file tags without markdown fences.'
        started=time.monotonic()
        response=runner.generate_turn(index,[{'role':'system','content':SITE_AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT},{'role':'user','content':prompt}],name,max_new_tokens=2048,temperature=0)
        (destination/'response.txt').write_text(response,encoding='utf-8')
        action=parse_agent_output(response).action
        files=dict(action.files) if isinstance(action,WriteSiteAction) else {}
        expected={f'src/components/{name}.tsx',f'src/components/{name}.css'}
        for path,code in files.items():
            if path in expected:
                target=destination/path;target.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
                target.write_text(code,encoding='utf-8')
        row={'section':name,'prompt':prompt,'elapsed_seconds':round(time.monotonic()-started,2),
             'expected_files':expected==set(files),'closed_file_tags':response.count('</file>')==2,
             'typecheck':False,'interaction_tests':False}
        if expected<=set(files):
            test_file=destination/'generated.test.tsx'
            test_file.write_text("import React from 'react';import {it,expect} from 'vitest';import {render,screen} from '@testing-library/react';import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';import Component from './src/components/"+name+"';\n"+test,encoding='utf-8')
            compile_result=run_command(['npx','tsc','--noEmit','--jsx','react-jsx','--target','ES2022','--module','ESNext','--moduleResolution','bundler','--esModuleInterop','--skipLibCheck',str(destination/'src/components'/f'{name}.tsx'),'css.d.ts'],cwd=ROOT)
            row['typecheck']=compile_result.returncode==0
            (destination/'typecheck.txt').write_text(compile_result.stdout+compile_result.stderr,encoding='utf-8')
            result=run_command(['npx','vitest','run',str(test_file),'--config','vitest.config.ts'],cwd=ROOT)
            row['interaction_tests']=result.returncode==0
            (destination/'tests.txt').write_text(result.stdout+result.stderr,encoding='utf-8')
        results.append(row)
        report={'model':str(model),'adapter_sha256':hashlib.sha256((model/'adapter_model.safetensors').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'max_new_tokens':2048,'temperature':0,'cases':results,'scope':'One-shot section tests only; no visual score or full-site claim.'}
        (output/'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n',encoding='utf-8')
        print(json.dumps(row),flush=True)


if __name__=='__main__':
`````

- **Description**: Node.js CSS validator using PostCSS to verify syntax and custom property usage.

`````javascript
const fs = require('node:fs');
const postcss = require('postcss');
try {
  const root = postcss.parse(fs.readFileSync(0, 'utf8'));
  const sharedSelectors = [];
  root.walkRules(rule => {
    let parent = rule.parent;
    while (parent) {
      if (parent.type === 'atrule' && /^(scope|.*keyframes)$/i.test(parent.name)) return;
      parent = parent.parent;
    }
    for (const selector of rule.selectors) {
      if (/^\.(section__(?:inner|header|title)|btn)(?![\w-])/.test(selector.trim())) sharedSelectors.push(selector);
    }
  });
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({errors: [], sharedSelectors}));
} catch (error) {
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({errors: [`${error.reason || error.message} at ${error.line || '?'}:${error.column || '?'}`]}));
}
`````

`````python
"""
scripts/verify_stock_photo_grid.py - End-to-end verification of features grid stock photo generation.

Tests generating feature grids with abstract and domain concepts across:
1. Cloud/SaaS Observability ("Real-Time Pipeline Execution", "Automated Distributed Tracing",
   "Enterprise Security Governance", "Predictive Telemetry & AI Alerts")
2. Modern Architecture Studio ("Sustainable Passive Design", "Raw Natural Materiality",
   "Precision BIM Modeling", "Luxury Villa Residence")
3. Specialty Coffee Roastery ("Micro-Lot Direct Trade", "Commercial Precision Roasting",
   "Peak Freshness Delivery", "Handcrafted Pour Over Bar")

Validates:
- Every image is a real, plausible photograph (Unsplash / Pexels)
- Zero Wikimedia/Wikipedia URLs or document scans/diagrams
- All images pass photographic sanity filtering
- Abstract concepts are translated to photographable visual terms
- No duplicate URLs across hero and grid items
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Add workspace root to sys.path
BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
if str(BASE_DIR) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(BASE_DIR))

from agent.site_brief import generate_content_brief, _is_valid_photograph


def verify_domain_features_grid(prompt: str, domain_name: str):
    print("\n" + "=" * 75)
    print(f"VERIFYING FEATURES GRID FOR: {domain_name.upper()}")
    print(f"Prompt: {prompt}")
    print("=" * 75)

    brief = generate_content_brief(prompt, provider="auto", resolve_images=True)

    assert brief, "Failed to generate brief"
    assert "images" in brief, "Brief missing 'images' payload"

    images_payload = brief["images"]
    hero = images_payload.get("hero")
    items = images_payload.get("items", [])
    attribution = brief.get("image_attribution", "")

    print(f"\n[Hero Image]")
    assert hero and hero.get("url"), f"Missing hero image for {domain_name}"
    hero_url = hero["url"]
    print(f"  URL:    {hero_url}")
    print(f"  Alt:    {hero.get('alt')}")
    print(f"  Source: {hero.get('source')}")
    print(f"  Credit: {hero.get('credit')}")

    assert "wikimedia" not in hero_url.lower(), f"Forbidden Wikimedia in hero: {hero_url}"
    assert "wikipedia" not in hero_url.lower(), f"Forbidden Wikipedia in hero: {hero_url}"
    assert hero_url.startswith("https://images.unsplash.com/") or hero_url.startswith("https://images.pexels.com/"), (
        f"Hero URL must be Unsplash or Pexels: {hero_url}"
    )
    assert _is_valid_photograph(hero), f"Hero failed photographic sanity check: {hero}"

    print(f"\n[Grid Item Images] ({len(items)} items resolved)")
    seen_urls = {hero_url}

    for idx, itm in enumerate(items):
        itm_name = itm.get("name", f"Item #{idx+1}")
        url = itm.get("url", "")
        alt = itm.get("alt", "")
        credit = itm.get("credit", "")
        source = itm.get("source", "")

        print(f"  Item {idx+1}: '{itm_name}'")
        print(f"    URL:    {url}")
        print(f"    Alt:    {alt}")
        print(f"    Source: {source} | Credit: {credit}")

        assert url, f"Item '{itm_name}' missing URL"
        assert "wikimedia" not in url.lower(), f"Forbidden Wikimedia in item: {url}"
        assert "wikipedia" not in url.lower(), f"Forbidden Wikipedia in item: {url}"
        assert url.startswith("https://images.unsplash.com/") or url.startswith("https://images.pexels.com/"), (
            f"Item URL must be Unsplash or Pexels: {url}"
        )
        assert _is_valid_photograph(itm), f"Item failed photographic sanity check: {itm}"
        assert url not in seen_urls, f"Duplicate image URL used across cards: {url}"
        seen_urls.add(url)

    print(f"\n[Attribution Line]")
    print(f"  {attribution}")
    assert "photographers" in attribution.lower(), f"Missing photography attribution: {attribution}"
    assert "wikimedia" not in attribution.lower(), f"Attribution mentions Wikimedia: {attribution}"

    print(f"\nSUCCESS: {domain_name} features grid verified with {len(items)} plausible stock photographs.")


if __name__ == "__main__":

            "Specialty Coffee Roastery",
`````

`````javascript
/**
 * test_confirm_toast_replacement.mjs
 * 
 * Verifies Issue #11: Replace Native confirm() and alert()
 * 
 * Tests:
 * 1. Codebase Scan: Assert ZERO instances of window.confirm and window.alert in frontend/src
 * 2. Component Structure: ConfirmDialog and ToastProvider definitions and ARIA contracts
 * 3. 8 Required Use Cases Coverage:
 *    - Delete project (ConfirmDialog)
 *    - Clear projects (ConfirmDialog)
 *    - Cancel all (ConfirmDialog)
 *    - Revert checkpoint (ConfirmDialog)
 *    - Overwrite file (ConfirmDialog)
 *    - Delete file (ConfirmDialog)
 *    - Export failure (ToastProvider)
 *    - Build failure (ToastProvider)
 * 4. Dialog Accessibility & Focus Trap verification
 * 5. Toast Store & Provider verification
 */

import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';
import assert from 'assert';

console.log('=== Running Issue #11: ConfirmDialog & ToastProvider Tests ===\n');

const FRONTEND_SRC = path.resolve('frontend/src');

// ── Test 1: Codebase Audit for window.confirm and window.alert ────────────────
console.log('[Test 1] Auditing frontend/src for window.confirm and window.alert...');

function getFilesRecursively(dir) {
  let results = [];
  const list = fs.readdirSync(dir);
  for (const file of list) {
    const filePath = path.join(dir, file);
    const stat = fs.statSync(filePath);
    if (stat && stat.isDirectory()) {
      results = results.concat(getFilesRecursively(filePath));
    } else if (file.endsWith('.ts') || file.endsWith('.tsx') || file.endsWith('.js') || file.endsWith('.jsx')) {
      results.push(filePath);
    }
  }
  return results;
}

const allFrontendFiles = getFilesRecursively(FRONTEND_SRC);
let forbiddenFound = [];

for (const file of allFrontendFiles) {
  const content = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf-8');
  const lines = content.split('\n');
  lines.forEach((line, index) => {
    // Check for native window.confirm or window.alert
    if (/window\.confirm\s*\(/.test(line)) {
      forbiddenFound.push({ file, line: index + 1, match: 'window.confirm', text: line.trim() });
    }
    if (/window\.alert\s*\(/.test(line)) {
      forbiddenFound.push({ file, line: index + 1, match: 'window.alert', text: line.trim() });
    }
    // Check for raw alert(...) calls (excluding CSS or attributes)
    if (/(?<![\.\w])alert\s*\(/.test(line) && !line.includes('role="alertdialog"') && !line.includes('alert_dialog')) {
      forbiddenFound.push({ file, line: index + 1, match: 'alert()', text: line.trim() });
    }
  });
}

assert.strictEqual(forbiddenFound.length, 0, `Found forbidden native dialogs: ${JSON.stringify(forbiddenFound, null, 2)}`);
console.log(`  ✓ Checked ${allFrontendFiles.length} files: 0 native confirm() or alert() calls found.\n`);

// ── Test 2: ConfirmDialog Component & ARIA Accessibility Contract ─────────────
console.log('[Test 2] Verifying ConfirmDialog Component & ARIA Attributes...');

const confirmDialogPath = path.join(FRONTEND_SRC, 'components/common/ConfirmDialog.tsx');
assert.ok(fs.existsSync(confirmDialogPath), 'ConfirmDialog.tsx must exist');
const confirmDialogCode = fs.readFileSync(confirmDialogPath, 'utf-8');

assert.ok(confirmDialogCode.includes('role="alertdialog"'), 'ConfirmDialog must have role="alertdialog"');
assert.ok(confirmDialogCode.includes('aria-modal="true"'), 'ConfirmDialog must have aria-modal="true"');
assert.ok(confirmDialogCode.includes('aria-labelledby='), 'ConfirmDialog must link aria-labelledby to title');
assert.ok(confirmDialogCode.includes('aria-describedby='), 'ConfirmDialog must link aria-describedby to message');

// Keyboard Focus Trap checks
assert.ok(confirmDialogCode.includes("e.key === 'Tab'"), 'ConfirmDialog must trap Tab key navigation');
assert.ok(confirmDialogCode.includes("e.shiftKey"), 'ConfirmDialog must handle Shift+Tab reverse wrapping');
assert.ok(confirmDialogCode.includes("e.key === 'Escape'"), 'ConfirmDialog must handle Escape to close/cancel');

// Defensive initial focus check for destructive actions
assert.ok(
  confirmDialogCode.includes("variant === 'danger'") && confirmDialogCode.includes("cancelBtnRef.current?.focus()"),
  'ConfirmDialog must focus cancel button first for danger/destructive actions to prevent accidental Enter'
);

console.log('  ✓ ConfirmDialog includes role="alertdialog", focus trapping, Escape handling, and safe default focus.\n');

// ── Test 3: ToastProvider Component & Accessibility Contract ──────────────────

const toastProviderPath = path.join(FRONTEND_SRC, 'components/common/ToastProvider.tsx');

// ── Test 4: Verify All 8 Required Use Cases ───────────────────────────────────
`````

`````javascript
// scripts/test_project_websocket_frontend.mjs
// Verifies frontend Vite proxy config and ProjectWebSocketClient behaviors

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const __filename = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);
const __dirname = path.dirname(__filename);
const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');

// ── Test 1: Vite Proxy Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────
console.log('--- Test 1: Verify Vite dev server /ws proxy configuration ---');
const viteConfigContent = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'frontend', 'vite.config.ts'), 'utf-8');

assert.match(viteConfigContent, /'\/ws':\s*\{/, "Vite config must define '/ws' proxy entry");
assert.match(viteConfigContent, /target:\s*['"]ws:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:5002['"]/, "Vite /ws proxy target must be ws://127.0.0.1:5002");
assert.match(viteConfigContent, /ws:\s*true/, "Vite /ws proxy must enable ws: true");
assert.match(viteConfigContent, /changeOrigin:\s*true/, "Vite /ws proxy must set changeOrigin: true");
console.log('✓ Vite /ws proxy configuration verified!');

// ── Setup Mock Environment for WebSocket Client ──────────────────────────────
class MockWebSocket {
  static OPEN = 1;
  static CLOSED = 3;

  constructor(url) {
    this.url = url;
    this.readyState = MockWebSocket.OPEN;
    this.sent = [];
    setTimeout(() => {
      if (this.onopen) this.onopen();
    }, 5);
  }

  send(data) {
    this.sent.push(JSON.parse(data));
  }

  close() {
    this.readyState = MockWebSocket.CLOSED;
    if (this.onclose) this.onclose({ code: 1000, reason: 'Normal Closure' });
  }

  receive(data) {
    if (this.onmessage) {
      this.onmessage({ data: typeof data === 'string' ? data : JSON.stringify(data) });
    }
  }
}

globalThis.WebSocket = MockWebSocket;
globalThis.window = {
  location: {
    protocol: 'http:',
    host: 'localhost:5173',
  },
};

const { ProjectWebSocketClient } = await import('../frontend/src/services/project-ws.ts');

// ── Test 2: Project WebSocket Connection and Monotonic Sequence Numbers ───────
console.log('--- Test 2: Connection URL & Monotonic Sequence Number Tracking ---');
const client = new ProjectWebSocketClient();
const receivedEvents = [];

client.connect('proj-test-101', {
  onEvent: (event) => receivedEvents.push(event),
  onResult: () => {},
  onDone: () => {},
});

// Wait for onopen
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 20));
assert.equal(client.getProjectId(), 'proj-test-101');
assert.equal(client.getLastEventId(), 0);

// Simulate server sending initial greeting
client['socket'].receive({
  type: 'connection.ready',
  project_id: 'proj-test-101',
  latest_seq: 0,
});

// Simulate server sending events with monotonic seq 1, 2, 3
client['socket'].receive({
  type: 'agent.status',
  seq: 1,
  data: { status: 'Planning' },
});
assert.equal(client.getLastEventId(), 1);

client['socket'].receive({
  type: 'activity.started',
  seq: 2,
  data: { activity: 'Building layout' },
});
assert.equal(client.getLastEventId(), 2);

client['socket'].receive({
  type: 'task.started',
  seq: 3,
  data: { task_id: 't-1', mode: 'site' },
});
assert.equal(client.getLastEventId(), 3);

// Verify monotonically advancing sequence
assert.equal(receivedEvents.length, 3);
assert.equal(receivedEvents[0].seq, 1);
assert.equal(receivedEvents[1].seq, 2);
assert.equal(receivedEvents[2].seq, 3);
console.log('✓ Monotonic sequence tracking verified!');

// ── Test 3: Bidirectional Client Messages ─────────────────────────────────────
console.log('--- Test 3: Bidirectional Client Message Dispatch ---');
client.sendTaskStart('Create a dashboard', 'site', { style_preset: 'modern' });
client.sendPromptQueue('Add dark mode switch');
client.sendPreviewSelection({ component: 'Header', elementId: 'logo' });
client.sendTaskCancel('user_stopped');

const sent = client['socket'].sent;
assert.equal(sent.length, 4);

assert.equal(sent[0].type, 'task.start');
assert.equal(sent[0].prompt, 'Create a dashboard');
assert.equal(sent[0].mode, 'site');

assert.equal(sent[1].type, 'prompt.queue');
assert.equal(sent[1].prompt, 'Add dark mode switch');

assert.equal(sent[2].type, 'preview.selection');
assert.equal(sent[2].selection.component, 'Header');

assert.equal(sent[3].type, 'task.cancel');
assert.equal(sent[3].reason, 'user_stopped');

console.log('✓ Bidirectional client messages verified!');

// ── Test 4: Reconnect and Missed Event Replay ────────────────────────────────
console.log('--- Test 4: Reconnect URL with lastEventId & Replay on subscribe.events ---');
// Remember current lastEventId was 3
assert.equal(client.getLastEventId(), 3);

// Simulate socket reconnecting
client.connect('proj-test-101', {
  onEvent: (event) => receivedEvents.push(event),
}, 'task-abc');

assert.match(client['socket'].url, /\?lastEventId=3$/, 'Reconnection URL must include ?lastEventId=3 query param');

// Wait for onopen
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 20));
const reconnectSent = client['socket'].sent;
assert.ok(reconnectSent.some((m) => m.type === 'subscribe.events' && m.lastEventId === 3), 'Must send subscribe.events on reconnect');

// Simulate server replaying missed events 4 and 5
client['socket'].receive({
  type: 'file.created',
  seq: 4,
  data: { path: 'src/Dashboard.tsx' },
});
client['socket'].receive({
  type: 'preview.ready',
  seq: 5,
  data: { url: 'http://localhost:5173' },
});

assert.equal(client.getLastEventId(), 5);
console.log('✓ Reconnect with missed event replay verified!');

// ── Test 5: Fallback to SSE when WebSocket Fails ─────────────────────────────
console.log('--- Test 5: Graceful SSE Fallback ---');
let fallbackTriggered = false;
client.setFallbackFactory((taskId, cb) => {
  fallbackTriggered = true;
  return { disconnect() {} };
});

// Force mock socket failure
client['startSSEFallback']();
assert.equal(fallbackTriggered, true, 'Fallback to SSE must be triggered when WebSocket is unavailable');
console.log('✓ SSE fallback mechanism verified!');

client.disconnect();
assert.equal(client.getProjectId(), null);
assert.equal(client.getLastEventId(), 0);
`````

- **Lines**: 107 | **Size**: 3,992 bytes | **SHA-256**: `91befecb4d3891ec300063e6ddfd04517fec0b6d4d6bd83596785aee0420f2bd` | **Newline**: `True`
- **Fence**: 5 backticks
- **Description**: Headless script testing workspace panel resizer interactions.

`````javascript
/**
 * scripts/test_workspace_resizer.mjs
 * Validates the Workspace Resizer improvements:
 * 1. e.currentTarget pointer capture (not e.target)
 * 2. pointercancel and lostpointercapture handling
 * 3. setIsResizing(false) guaranteed in all cancellation/up paths
 * 4. touchAction: 'none' for touch devices
 * 5. role="separator" and keyboard-resizable accessibility
 * 6. double-click reset
 * 7. user width preference persistence via localStorage
 * 8. dynamic window resize clamping
 */

import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';
import assert from 'assert';

console.log('[Test] Running Workspace Resizer Pointer Capture validation...');

const resizerPath = path.resolve('frontend/src/components/workspace/WorkspaceResizer.tsx');
const resizerCode = fs.readFileSync(resizerPath, 'utf-8');

// 1. Verify e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture and e.currentTarget.releasePointerCapture
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)'),
  'FAILED: Must use e.currentTarget.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)'
);
assert(
  !resizerCode.includes('(e.target as HTMLElement).setPointerCapture'),
  'FAILED: Must NOT use e.target.setPointerCapture'
);
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('e.currentTarget.releasePointerCapture(e.pointerId)'),
  'FAILED: Must use e.currentTarget.releasePointerCapture(e.pointerId)'
);
console.log('✓ Verified e.currentTarget pointer capture & release');

// 2. Verify pointercancel and lostpointercapture handlers
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('onPointerCancel={handlePointerCancel}'),
  'FAILED: Must attach onPointerCancel'
);
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('onLostPointerCapture={handleLostPointerCapture}'),
  'FAILED: Must attach onLostPointerCapture'
);
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('setIsResizing(false)'),
  'FAILED: Must always call setIsResizing(false) on release or cancel'
);
console.log('✓ Verified pointercancel and lostpointercapture event handlers');

// 3. Verify touch-action: none for touch device support
assert(
  resizerCode.includes("touchAction: 'none'"),
  "FAILED: Must specify touchAction: 'none' to prevent mobile browser gesture collisions"
);
console.log('✓ Verified touch-action: none for touch support');

// 4. Verify keyboard accessibility
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('role="separator"'),
  'FAILED: Splitter must have role="separator"'
);
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}'),
  'FAILED: Must support keyboard resizing via onKeyDown'
);
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('ArrowLeft') && resizerCode.includes('ArrowRight'),
  'FAILED: Arrow keys must resize the splitter'
);
console.log('✓ Verified keyboard-resizable accessibility');

// 5. Verify double-click reset
assert(
  resizerCode.includes('onDoubleClick={handleDoubleClick}'),
  'FAILED: Must support double-click reset'
);
console.log('✓ Verified double-click reset');

// 6. Verify window resize clamping and window fail-safe listeners
assert(
  resizerCode.includes("window.addEventListener('resize', handleWindowResize)"),
  'FAILED: Must clamp workspace width on window resize'
);
assert(
  resizerCode.includes("window.addEventListener('pointerup', stopResizing)") ||
  resizerCode.includes("window.addEventListener('pointercancel', stopResizing)"),
  'FAILED: Window-level fail-safe listeners must be present'
);
console.log('✓ Verified window resize clamping and window-level fail-safe listeners');

// 7. Verify localStorage persistence in workspace-store.ts
const storePath = path.resolve('frontend/src/state/workspace-store.ts');
const storeCode = fs.readFileSync(storePath, 'utf-8');
assert(
  storeCode.includes("localStorage.getItem('slm_workspace_width')"),
  'FAILED: Must read initial width from localStorage'
);
assert(
  storeCode.includes("localStorage.setItem('slm_workspace_width'"),
  'FAILED: Must write updated width to localStorage'
);
console.log('✓ Verified user preference persistence in localStorage');

console.log('\nAll workspace resizer assertions PASSED successfully!');
`````

- **Lines**: 27 | **Size**: 1,147 bytes | **SHA-256**: `2f1344e229088652d515b92b408cfc5cbb6600354c9c96110db8c86d867e7ea2` | **Newline**: `True`
- **Fence**: 5 backticks
- **Description**: Linux launcher bash script for the ReactAgent SLM Workbench UI.

`````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# SiteAgent - start the workbench at http://127.0.0.1:5000
#   bash scripts/run_web_ui.sh            design kit (fast; the model writes the copy)
#   bash scripts/run_web_ui.sh --native   the model writes each section's code too
#                                          (needs a native adapter in models/)
# ==============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ -f .venv/bin/python ]; then PY=.venv/bin/python
elif [ -f .venv/Scripts/python.exe ]; then PY=.venv/Scripts/python.exe
else PY=python; fi

if [ "${1:-}" = "--native" ]; then
  shift
  ADAPTER="$(ls -d models/*native* 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -n 1 || true)"
  if [ -z "$ADAPTER" ]; then
    echo "No native adapter in models/. Download one with: python scripts/download_models.py --adapter USER/REPO"
    exit 1
  fi
  export MODEL_PATH="$ADAPTER" SITE_STRATEGY=native
  echo "Using adapter $ADAPTER (native mode)"
fi

echo "Starting SiteAgent workbench at http://127.0.0.1:5000 ..."
"$PY" server/app.py "$@"
`````

#### `scripts/setup.sh`

- **Path**: `file:///C:/Users/AYUSH/Documents/slm/scripts/setup.sh`
- **Lines**: 27 | **Size**: 1,085 bytes | **SHA-256**: `84c1e2a6672e36a8357cd2b7b6efda50de30c43156136e0a5f0e4143b7a8b250` | **Newline**: `True`
- **Fence**: 5 backticks
- **Description**: Automated environment initialization script for Linux.

`````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# SiteAgent - one-command setup (macOS, Linux, Git Bash on Windows)
#   bash scripts/setup.sh [--cpu] [--skip-model] [--adapter USER/REPO]
# Creates .venv, installs PyTorch for your hardware and everything else, builds the
# workbench UI, downloads Qwen3-4B and runs the doctor.
# ==============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

PY="${PYTHON:-}"
if [ -z "$PY" ]; then
  for candidate in python3.12 python3.11 python3.13 python3.10 python3 python; do
    if command -v "$candidate" >/dev/null 2>&1; then PY="$candidate"; break; fi
  done
fi
[ -n "$PY" ] || { echo "Python 3.10-3.13 is required."; exit 1; }

if [ ! -d .venv ]; then
  echo "Creating virtual environment in .venv with $PY"
  "$PY" -m venv .venv
fi
if [ -f .venv/bin/python ]; then VENV_PY=.venv/bin/python; else VENV_PY=.venv/Scripts/python.exe; fi

"$VENV_PY" scripts/install.py "$@"
echo
echo "Start the workbench:  bash scripts/run_web_ui.sh"
`````
