`````python
    )

    t4_thought = thought(
        f"Writing the final section, Footer, for {d['name']}. "
        "I'll organize it into a structured multi-column layout containing the brand wordmark, "
        f"tagline, contact card (address: {d['contact']['address']}, phone: {d['contact']['phone']}, email: {d['contact']['email']}), "
        "operating hours, and an automatic copyright line."
    )

    t4_tsx = f"""import React from 'react';
import './Footer.css';

export function Footer() {{
  const year = new Date().getFullYear();

  return (
    <footer className="{p}-footer" id="footer" aria-label="Site Footer">
      <div className="{p}-footer__inner">
        <div className="{p}-footer__brand">
          <p className="{p}-footer__logo">{d['name']}</p>
          <p className="{p}-footer__tagline">{d['tagline']}</p>
        </div>

        <address className="{p}-footer__contact">
          <h4 className="{p}-footer__heading">Visit & Connect</h4>
          <p>{d['contact']['address']}</p>
          <p><a href="tel:{d['contact']['phone']}">{d['contact']['phone']}</a></p>
          <p><a href="mailto:{d['contact']['email']}">{d['contact']['email']}</a></p>
        </address>

        <div className="{p}-footer__hours">
          <h4 className="{p}-footer__heading">Hours of Operation</h4>
          <p>{d['contact']['hours']}</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="{p}-footer__bottom">
        <p>&copy; {{year}} {d['name']}. All rights reserved.</p>
      </div>
    </footer>
  );
}}
"""

    prim_r = int(d['primary'][1:3], 16)
    prim_g = int(d['primary'][3:5], 16)
    prim_b = int(d['primary'][5:7], 16)
    accent_r = int(d['accent'][1:3], 16)
    accent_g = int(d['accent'][3:5], 16)
    accent_b = int(d['accent'][5:7], 16)
    footer_bg = f"rgb({max(6, prim_r // 3)}, {max(6, prim_g // 3)}, {max(8, prim_b // 3)})"
    footer_border = f"rgba({accent_r}, {accent_g}, {accent_b}, 0.14)"

    t4_css = f""".{p}-footer {{

"""

    t4_action = write_site("src/components/Footer.tsx", t4_tsx, "src/components/Footer.css", t4_css)

    t5_thought = thought(

    )

    t5_finish = finish(

        f"- Header: sticky navbar with logo, nav links, CTA button, and mobile menu\n"
        f"- Hero: bold responsive banner structured for the {layout_archetype} archetype with tagline and CTAs\n"
        f"- {d['section_name']}: {layout_archetype}-driven section displaying all {len(d['items'])} items with tags & descriptions\n"
        f"- Footer: structured layout with business info, full address, phone, email, and hours\n"
        f"Color scheme: primary ({d['primary']}), accent ({d['accent']}), {d['heading_font']} headings on {d['body_font']} body."
    )

    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": SITE_AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
        {"role": "user", "content": initial_user},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": f"{t1_thought}\n{t1_action}"},

def main():
    output_path = Path("site_trajectories_batch5.jsonl")
    data_output_path = Path("data/site_trajectories_batch5.jsonl")
    print("=" * 70)
    print("      GENERATING BATCH 5: 50 GOLD-STANDARD SITE TRAJECTORIES        ")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Total domains configured: {len(DOMAINS)}")

    trajectories = []
    for i, d in enumerate(DOMAINS, 1):
        traj = build_trajectory(d)
        trajectories.append(traj)
        print(f"[{i:02d}/50] Generated: {d['id']} ({d['name']}) [archetype: {d['layout_archetype']}]")

    # Write to root output
    with output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for traj in trajectories:
            f.write(json.dumps(traj) + "\n")

    # Write to data directory
    data_output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with data_output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for traj in trajectories:
            f.write(json.dumps(traj) + "\n")

    print("-" * 70)
    print(f"Successfully generated {len(trajectories)} trajectories to {output_path.name} and {data_output_path}!")
    print(f"File size: {output_path.stat().st_size:,} bytes")
`````

`````python
# Guarantee 100% unique accents across all domains
_seen_accents = set()
for _i, _d in enumerate(DOMAINS):
    _acc = _d["accent"]
    if _acc in _seen_accents:
        _r = int(_acc[1:3], 16)
        _g = int(_acc[3:5], 16)
        _b = int(_acc[5:7], 16)
        _r = min(255, max(0, _r + ((_i * 7) % 23) - 10))
        _g = min(255, max(0, _g + ((_i * 11) % 23) - 10))
        _b = min(255, max(0, _b + ((_i * 13) % 23) - 10))
        _d["accent"] = f"#{_r:02x}{_g:02x}{_b:02x}"
    _seen_accents.add(_d["accent"])

def build_brief_xml(d, layout_archetype="grid"):
    items_xml = []
    for item in d["items"]:
        items_xml.append(f'  <item name="{item["title"]}" tag="{item["tag"]}" description="{item["desc"]}" />')
    items_str = "\n".join(items_xml)
    guidelines = _LAYOUT_ARCHETYPE_GUIDELINES.get(layout_archetype, "")
    motion_obj = _MOTION_VOCABULARY.get(layout_archetype, "")
    motion_guidelines = motion_obj.get("guidelines", str(motion_obj)) if isinstance(motion_obj, dict) else str(motion_obj)

    return f"""<content_brief>
  <business_name>{d["name"]}</business_name>
  <tagline>{d["tagline"]}</tagline>
  <business_type>{d["type"]}</business_type>
  <layout_archetype>{layout_archetype}</layout_archetype>
  <layout_guidelines>{guidelines}</layout_guidelines>
  <motion_guidelines>{motion_guidelines}</motion_guidelines>
  <primary_color>{d["primary"]}</primary_color>
  <accent_color>{d["accent"]}</accent_color>
  <font_heading>{d["heading_font"]}</font_heading>
  <font_body>{d["body_font"]}</font_body>
  <sections>header, hero, {d["section_id"]}, footer</sections>
{items_str}
  <contact>
    <address>{d["contact"]["address"]}</address>
    <phone>{d["contact"]["phone"]}</phone>
    <email>{d["contact"]["email"]}</email>
    <hours>{d["contact"]["hours"]}</hours>
  </contact>
</content_brief>"""


def make_hero_code(p, d, layout_archetype):
    accent_r = int(d['accent'][1:3], 16)
    accent_g = int(d['accent'][3:5], 16)
    accent_b = int(d['accent'][5:7], 16)

    if layout_archetype == "bento":
        t2_user = (
            f"Write the Hero section: high-tech centered banner with tagline as h1, ambient radial glow, "
            f"subheading, dual CTAs, and a high-impact metric highlight strip. Files: src/components/Hero.tsx + src/components/Hero.css"
        )
        t2_thought = (
            f"Header was approved. Now I'll create the Hero section for {d['name']} using the Bento high-tech layout. "
            f"The headline will render the tagline in {d['heading_font']} typography. "
            f"I'll add radial ambient glowing backdrops using {d['accent']} at 16% opacity, supporting copy, "
            f"a primary '{d['cta']}' button, secondary link to #{d['section_id']}, and a live metric highlights strip."
        )
        t2_tsx = f"""import React from 'react';
import './Hero.css';

export function Hero() {{
  return (
    <section className="{p}-hero {p}-hero--bento" id="hero" aria-labelledby="{p}-hero-title">
      <div className="{p}-hero__atmosphere" aria-hidden="true" />
      <div className="{p}-hero__inner">
        <div className="{p}-hero__badge">
          <span className="{p}-hero__badge-pulse" aria-hidden="true" />
          <span>{d['name']} · Verified</span>
        </div>

        <h1 id="{p}-hero-title" className="{p}-hero__title">
          {d['tagline']}
        </h1>

        <p className="{p}-hero__subtitle">
          {d['hero_sub']}

        )
        t3_thought = (
            f"Now creating the core content component '{sec_ts_name}' for {d['name']} with the Timeline layout archetype. "
            f"I'll render the {len(d['items'])} items sequentially along a vertical milestone track with step indicators, "
            f"node connectors, and detailed descriptive cards."
        )
        milestones = [
            {"step": f"Phase 0{idx+1}", "title": it["title"], "tag": it["tag"], "desc": it["desc"]}
            for idx, it in enumerate(d["items"])
        ]
        milestones_json = json.dumps(milestones, indent=2)

        t3_tsx = f"""import React from 'react';
import './{sec_ts_name}.css';

interface Milestone {{
  step: string;
  title: string;
  tag: string;
  desc: string;
}}

const MILESTONES: Milestone[] = {milestones_json};

export function {sec_ts_name}() {{
  const trackRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  React.useEffect(() => {{
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {{
        entries.forEach((entry) => {{
          if (entry.isIntersecting) {{
            entry.target.classList.add('is-revealed');
          }}
        }});
      }},
      {{ threshold: 0.2 }}
    );

    const nodes = trackRef.current?.querySelectorAll('.{p}-timeline__node');
    nodes?.forEach((node) => observer.observe(node));

    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }}, []);

  return (

}}
"""

        t3_tsx = f"""import React from 'react';
import './{sec_ts_name}.css';

interface Item {{
  title: string;
  tag: string;
  desc: string;
}}

const ITEMS: Item[] = {items_json};

export function {sec_ts_name}() {{
  const gridRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  React.useEffect(() => {{
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
      (entries) => {{
        entries.forEach((entry) => {{
          if (entry.isIntersecting) {{
            entry.target.classList.add('is-visible');
          }}
        }});
      }},
      {{ threshold: 0.15 }}
    );

    const cards = gridRef.current?.querySelectorAll('.{p}-card');
    cards?.forEach((card) => observer.observe(card));

    return () => observer.disconnect();
  }}, []);

  return (
    <section className="{p}-catalog" id="{d['section_id']}" aria-labelledby="{p}-catalog-title">
      <div className="{p}-catalog__inner">
        <div className="{p}-catalog__header">
          <p className="{p}-catalog__eyebrow">Featured Highlights</p>
          <h2 id="{p}-catalog-title" className="{p}-catalog__title">
            {d['section_name']}
          </h2>
          <p className="{p}-catalog__desc">
            {catalog_desc}
          </p>
        </div>

        <div ref={{gridRef}} className="{p}-catalog__grid">
          {{ITEMS.map((item, idx) => (
            <article key={{item.title}} className="{p}-card" style={{{{ transitionDelay: `${{idx * 60}}ms` }}}}>
              <div className="{p}-card__top">
                <span className="{p}-card__index">0{{idx + 1}}</span>
                <span className="{p}-card__tag">{{item.tag}}</span>
              </div>
              <h3 className="{p}-card__title">{{item.title}}</h3>
              <p className="{p}-card__desc">{{item.desc}}</p>
            </article>
          ))}}
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}}
"""

def build_trajectory(d):
    target_arch = d.get("layout_archetype", "grid")

    layout_archetype = select_layout_archetype(prompt_seed, business_type=d["type"], business_name=d["name"])
    brief_xml = build_brief_xml(d, layout_archetype=layout_archetype)
    p = d["prefix"]

    # ── Turn 1: Header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

        f"{brief_xml}\n\n"
        "You will build the site ONE SECTION AT A TIME. Start with the first section now.\n\n"
        f"FIRST SECTION REQUIRED: Write the Header section: a sticky navigation bar with the business name/logo on the left, "
        f"navigation links (Home, {d['section_name']}, Contact) on the right, plus '{d['cta']}' CTA button. "
        "Files: src/components/Header.tsx + src/components/Header.css"
    )

    t1_thought = thought(
        f"I'll start by crafting the Header for {d['name']}. "
        f"It needs to reflect the {d['type']} brand identity: deep background ({d['primary']}) with crisp contrast, "
        f"the elegant {d['heading_font']} typography for the wordmark, and the signature {d['accent']} accent for the CTA button. "
        "I'll also implement a scroll listener to trigger glassmorphism and subtle border illumination on scroll."
    )

    t1_tsx = f"""import React, {{ useState, useEffect }} from 'react';
import './Header.css';

export function Header() {{
  const [scrolled, setScrolled] = useState(false);
  const [menuOpen, setMenuOpen] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {{
    const onScroll = () => setScrolled(window.scrollY > 15);
    window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, {{ passive: true }});
    return () => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);
  }}, []);

  return (
    <header className={{`{p}-header${{scrolled ? ' {p}-header--scrolled' : ''}}`}} role="banner">
      <div className="{p}-header__inner">
        <a href="#" className="{p}-header__logo" aria-label="{d['name']} Home">
          {d['name']}
        </a>

        <nav className="{p}-header__nav" aria-label="Main Navigation">
          <a href="#hero" className="{p}-header__link">Home</a>
          <a href="#{d['section_id']}" className="{p}-header__link">{d['section_name']}</a>
          <a href="#footer" className="{p}-header__link">Contact</a>
        </nav>

        <div className="{p}-header__actions">
          <a href="mailto:{d['contact']['email']}" className="{p}-header__cta">
            {d['cta']}
          </a>
          <button
            type="button"
            className="{p}-header__toggle"
            aria-label="Toggle navigation menu"
            aria-expanded={{menuOpen}}
            onClick={{() => setMenuOpen(!menuOpen)}}
          >
            <span className="{p}-header__bar" />
            <span className="{p}-header__bar" />
            <span className="{p}-header__bar" />
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>

      {{menuOpen && (
        <div className="{p}-header__mobile-menu">
          <a href="#hero" onClick={{() => setMenuOpen(false)}}>Home</a>
          <a href="#{d['section_id']}" onClick={{() => setMenuOpen(false)}}>{d['section_name']}</a>
          <a href="#footer" onClick={{() => setMenuOpen(false)}}>Contact</a>
        </div>
      )}}
    </header>
  );
}}
"""

    # ── Turn 5: Complete & Finish ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    t5_user = obs_done([
        "src/components/Header.tsx", "src/components/Header.css",
        "src/components/Hero.tsx", "src/components/Hero.css",
        f"src/components/{sec_ts_name}.tsx", f"src/components/{sec_ts_name}.css",
        "src/components/Footer.tsx", "src/components/Footer.css"
    ])

    t5_thought = thought(
        f"All 4 sections have been built and accepted for {d['name']} using layout archetype '{layout_archetype}'. "
        "The site is complete with cohesive design tokens, responsive grid layouts, "
        "valid TypeScript components, and scoped modern CSS."
    )

    t5_finish = finish(
        f"Built the complete {d['name']} ({d['type']}) website with 4 sections (archetype: {layout_archetype}):\n"
        f"- Header: sticky navbar with logo, nav links, CTA button, and mobile menu\n"
        f"- Hero: bold responsive banner structured for the {layout_archetype} archetype with tagline and CTAs\n"
        f"- {d['section_name']}: {layout_archetype}-driven section displaying all {len(d['items'])} items with tags & descriptions\n"
        f"- Footer: structured layout with business info, full address, phone, email, and hours\n"
        f"Color scheme: primary ({d['primary']}), accent ({d['accent']}), {d['heading_font']} headings on {d['body_font']} body."
    )

    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": SITE_AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
        {"role": "user", "content": initial_user},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": f"{t1_thought}\n{t1_action}"},
        {"role": "user", "content": t2_user},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": f"{t2_thought}\n{t2_action}"},
        {"role": "user", "content": t3_user},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": f"{t3_thought}\n{t3_action}"},
        {"role": "user", "content": t4_user},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": f"{t4_thought}\n{t4_action}"},
        {"role": "user", "content": t5_user},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": f"{t5_thought}\n{t5_finish}"}
    ]

    return {
        "task_id": d["id"],
        "layout_archetype": layout_archetype,
        "messages": messages
    }


def main():
    output_path = Path("site_trajectories_batch4.jsonl")
    data_output_path = Path("data/site_trajectories_batch4.jsonl")
    print("=" * 70)
    print("      GENERATING BATCH 4: 50 GOLD-STANDARD SITE TRAJECTORIES        ")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Total domains configured: {len(DOMAINS)}")

    trajectories = []
    for i, d in enumerate(DOMAINS, 1):
        traj = build_trajectory(d)
        trajectories.append(traj)
        print(f"[{i:02d}/50] Generated: {d['id']} ({d['name']}) [archetype: {d['layout_archetype']}]")

    # Write to root output
    with output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for traj in trajectories:
            f.write(json.dumps(traj) + "\n")

    # Write to data directory
    data_output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with data_output_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for traj in trajectories:
            f.write(json.dumps(traj) + "\n")

    print("-" * 70)
    print(f"Successfully generated {len(trajectories)} trajectories to {output_path.name} and {data_output_path}!")
    print(f"File size: {output_path.stat().st_size:,} bytes")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
`````

`````markdown
# SiteAgent Benchmark Separation and Leakage Protection Policy

## Release evidence

The mock full-site harness writes `runs/mock_full_website_benchmark_report.json`; it is never promotion evidence. Live runs write `runs/full_website_benchmark_report.json` and include four per-site outcome stages: model-native generation, deterministic repair, model repair, and final rendered site. Each stage reports its own pass count and provenance. A passing final site does not count as a native model pass.

Promotion requires a live report with these four scorecards and per-site records. The previously promoted motion adapter has been revoked because its LoRA tensor shape is incompatible with the current Qwen3 base. The compatible candidate remains unpromoted until held-out live evaluation covers completion, prompt fidelity, interaction, visual quality, motion, and runtime 3D on desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion settings.

3D validation reports static scene/performance policy separately from browser runtime success. A bare canvas fails the scene contract. Browser evidence is written to each generated workspace as `three_d_runtime_evidence.json`, including canvas pixels, WebGL state, sampled motion frames, mobile visibility, reduced-motion visibility, and fallback visibility without WebGL.

## 1. Overview and Problem Definition

Repeatedly training or prompt-tuning against failures on a single evaluation benchmark converts the evaluation set into an implicit development set. Over time, models overfit to specific phrasing, edge cases, and test assertions of that dataset, invalidating claimed benchmark gains.

To prevent evaluation leakage and maintain true generalization, SiteAgent enforces a strict two-tier benchmark architecture:
1. **Development Benchmark** (`data/eval/dev_benchmark.jsonl`)
2. **Sealed Final Benchmark** (`data/eval/sealed_final_benchmark.jsonl`)

---

## 2. Benchmark Split Specifications

| Dimension | Development Benchmark | Sealed Final Benchmark |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Path** | `data/eval/dev_benchmark.jsonl` | `data/eval/sealed_final_benchmark.jsonl` |
| **Task Count** | 150 tasks | 153 tasks |
| **Integrity Seal** | Disjointness verified | Cryptographic SHA-256 manifest (`sealed_final_benchmark_manifest.json`) |
| **Permitted Uses** | • Daily debugging<br>• Training decisions & ablation studies<br>• Failure harvesting & repair analysis<br>• DPO pair generation<br>• Prompt engineering & system prompt tuning | • Major milestone checkpoints only<br>• Final candidate release qualification |
| **Prohibited Uses** | • Overwriting with sealed benchmark prompts | • Training on task failures<br>• DPO generation from task prompts<br>• Prompt tuning to fit specific test codes<br>• Frequent/continuous evaluation loops |
| **Evaluation Frequency** | Continuous / Per-experiment | Infrequent / Major release milestones |

---

## 3. The 6 Mandatory Leakage Checks

Every candidate dataset (training, validation, synthetic, or dev splits) must pass all 6 leakage checks fail-closed against the Sealed Final Benchmark before preflight or training can commence:

### 1. Exact Prompt Matching
- **Definition**: Direct verbatim match between candidate prompt and benchmark prompt after trimming whitespace.
- **Rule**: If `candidate_prompt.strip() == benchmark_prompt.strip()`, reject immediately.

### 2. Normalized Matching
- **Definition**: Casefolded, punctuation-stripped, and whitespace-collapsed text matching.
- **Rule**: Eliminates trivial evasion (e.g. adding a period, changing casing, or substituting double spaces).

### 3. Symbol Overlap
- **Definition**: Extraction of component names (`PascalCase`), custom hooks (`useX`), backticked identifiers (`` `X` ``), CSS classes (`styles.X`), and `data-testid` values.
- **Rule**: If candidate shares core symbols with a benchmark task AND token Jaccard similarity exceeds 0.35, the sample is flagged as an unauthorized clone of the benchmark test case.

### 4. Token Similarity
- **Definition**: Word-level Jaccard similarity over alphanumeric tokens:
  $$\text{Jaccard}(A, B) = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|}$$
- **Rule**: Fails if $\text{Jaccard} \ge 0.50$.

### 5. Family-Level Holdout
- **Definition**: Metadata identifiers (`family_id`, `source_task_id`, `task_id`).
- **Rule**: Tasks derived from the same source component or architectural family as a sealed benchmark item cannot appear in training or validation splits.

### 6. Semantic Similarity Checks
- **Definition**: Composite similarity measuring:
  - Word bigram Jaccard (40%)
  - Character 4-gram Jaccard (35%)
  - Word token Jaccard (25%)
- **Rule**: Detects paraphrased prompts that express the exact same specification with reordered phrasing or synonyms. Fails if composite similarity $\ge 0.65$.

---

## 4. Cryptographic Manifest & Tamper Protection

The Sealed Final Benchmark is cryptographically anchored by `data/eval/sealed_final_benchmark_manifest.json`:
- **SHA-256 Digest**: Computed over the entire raw bytes of `sealed_final_benchmark.jsonl`.
- **Task Count Integrity**: Verifies exact task count (153).
- **Per-Task Hashing**: Retains per-task prompt hashes for fine-grained tamper detection.

Any manual modification, accidental corruption, or truncation of the sealed benchmark immediately aborts training and preflight with an integrity error.

---

## 5. Verification Tooling

### CLI Audit Tool
Audit any candidate training, validation, or dev dataset using:
```bash
python scripts/verify_benchmark_leakage.py --dataset data/training_data.jsonl
```

Audit the Development Benchmark:
```bash
python scripts/verify_benchmark_leakage.py --dataset data/eval/dev_benchmark.jsonl
```

### Preflight Integration
During SFT training (`python -m training.train_sft`), `check_benchmark_disjointness` automatically validates:
1. Manifest integrity of `sealed_final_benchmark.jsonl`
2. All 6 leakage dimensions against `sealed_final_benchmark.jsonl`
3. Disjointness against `dev_benchmark.jsonl` and `premium_sites.jsonl`
`````

`````markdown
# Website quality evidence workflow

## Promotion selection and training guards (2026-10-05)

Automatic workbench adapter selection now requires `promotion_evidence` in the promotion pointer.
Its `native_gate`, `component_benchmark`, `site_benchmark`, and `human_review` entries each contain
`path` and `sha256`. Reports must match the selected adapter. The native report must pass the current
three-domain generation path without repairs or fallbacks. Live site reports must display all four
outcome scorecards, evaluate at least 30 native sites at an 85% pass rate or better, pass the existing
promotion metrics, include passed browser motion and 3D checks, and cover the exact sites scored by
the existing two-reviewer, 12-domain blinded human gate. Labels and an architecture manifest alone
do not establish release eligibility. Missing or changed evidence selects the base model.

`--override-methodology-gate` only overrides hyperparameter policy; SFT native completion and reviewed
data admission remain mandatory. DPO now also checks the native report for its initial adapter before
GPU loading, accepts `--native-gate-report`, and refuses an existing output directory. CPU preflight
does not certify a training run or promotion. Preserve candidates and historical adapters.

Use `python -m scripts.audit_curriculum_evidence --output runs/curriculum_evidence_audit.json` to count
final supervised action types, navigation, full Main file targets, source/review metadata, and preference
receipt artifacts. Inline booleans and provenance labels are counted separately from matching files.
This inventory measures available evidence and coverage; it does not assign human visual scores.

Run `python scripts/audit_site_training_coverage.py` before preparing another adapter. The report at `runs/p1_training_coverage.json` counts rows and source families separately. The current 787-row candidate set has only three explicitly tagged portfolio families and three ecommerce families; its rows do not carry top-level source, license, validation, or human visual-review records. These are coverage and provenance findings, not scores.

New full-site trajectories belong in a separate `reviewed_full_sites` train/held-out split. Each row needs a source, license, family ID, domain, compiler/build/runtime/interaction results, browser captures at desktop/mobile/reduced motion, and a named human reviewer with scores for layout, hierarchy, typography, content specificity, imagery/assets, motion timing, and mobile composition. Repair rows also need the diagnostics that caused the repair. `training/train_sft.py` rejects a `reviewed_full_sites` dataset if these fields are missing or source families cross the split. Historical candidate and motion datasets remain untouched.

Capture a running site with `python scripts/capture_visual_review.py http://127.0.0.1:5173 runs/review/example-id`. This saves full-page screenshots, scroll videos, viewport settings, and browser errors. A reviewer must inspect the artifacts and assign scores; the capture script does not declare visual quality. `data/eval/visual_holdout_v1.jsonl` contains 30 family-disjoint briefs across 12 domains. Capture both baseline and candidate for each brief under `runs/visual_pair_sources/<task_id>/{baseline,candidate}/`, then use `scripts/blinded_visual_review.py prepare` to randomize A/B and create score forms. Keep its private mapping outside the public package. Two independent humans must score both A and B for each of the 30 sites. Only `scripts/blinded_visual_review.py assemble` should unblind completed forms into `runs/visual_review_report.json`, tied to the adapter fingerprint. Static CSS and pixel scores remain diagnostic guardrails.

For generation, the content brief now includes a typed requirement manifest with exact user facts, sections/routes, requested interactions, visual/motion constraints, and shared cart/filter state contracts. Final validation checks the manifest and uses browser interaction and motion probes for explicit requests. Use the saved `motion_runtime_evidence.json` and `three_d_runtime_evidence.json` when reviewing behavior. A new adapter should not be promoted until the held-out live website evaluation and human review both pass.

The workbench defaults to Full Site, offers an optional structured prompt for topic, audience, pages, content, style, motion/3D, and assets, and opens the preview after a site build. On mobile the sidebar starts closed and has a separate saved preference. The preview shows reported build, runtime, motion, and 3D checks; it does not yet collect live iframe console output or a reduced-motion result for every preview. The current coverage audit and browser captures are preparation for reviewed examples, not a completed reviewed training set or evidence of a better adapter.

The first full eligible training pass combined all 787 accepted quality-v3 rows with the 36 motion curriculum rows. `data/full_site_training/manifest.json` records exact source hashes, 823 rows, and family separation from the 104-row validation split. `models/qwen3-siteagent-full-v1-candidate` was trained for one epoch and passed adapter compatibility with the current base. It remains a candidate until live held-out sites and the blinded human review pass. The three original reference websites have desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion captures in `runs/reviewed_source_candidates/`; those captures are review candidates, not human-approved examples.
`````

`````markdown
# SiteAgent quality audit — 2026-09-25

## Scope and evidence

This is a read-only engineering and product audit of the current workspace. It examines model selection, candidate training data, site planning and generation, repair, motion and 3D validation, benchmark scoring, and the React workbench. It does not claim a new model has been trained or promoted.

Checks performed:

- Frontend `npm run build`: TypeScript and Vite passed. Vite reported a 606.56 kB minified JavaScript entry chunk.
- Focused Python suites for site planning, 3D, motion, benchmark, and model fingerprinting: 91 passed.
- Live workbench at `http://127.0.0.1:5000/`: desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844 loaded without page errors or horizontal document overflow. Screenshots: `runs/audit_ui/desktop.png` and `runs/audit_ui/mobile.png`.
- Existing live model runs: `runs/cross_domain_portfolio_updated.json` failed at 0.6589; `runs/cross_domain_ecommerce_smoke.json` failed at 0.7855. The ecommerce saved workspace passed after deterministic project repair and rescored at 0.883 in `runs/cross_domain_ecommerce_postrepair.json`. These are one site each, not a statistical estimate.
- `runs/full_website_benchmark_report.json` reports 36/36 passes but identifies `mock: true` and `model: mock-runner`; this does not measure live model quality.

## P0: release and trust blockers

### 1. The promoted motion adapter is incompatible with the current base

`models/promoted_model.json` points to `models/qwen3-siteagent-motion-r16` and claims passed gates. Its first MLP down-projection LoRA A tensor has shape `[16, 11008]`, whereas the current `base-model/config.json` is Qwen3 with intermediate size 9728. `verify_lora_adapter_compatibility` rejects the adapter. The compatible `models/qwen3-siteagent-authentic-r16-candidate` has `[16, 9728]`, but has not passed a broad promotion gate. `server/app.py` currently skips incompatible defaults and falls back to the base model. The running server, started 2026-09-20, still reports the motion adapter as ready, so its in-memory state and the current on-disk selection logic are divergent.

**Action:** remove the invalid promotion claim; expose actual loaded base/adapter fingerprints and compatibility in `/api/status`; only promote a candidate after live held-out tests for completion, fidelity, interaction, visual quality, motion, and 3D. Restart the single model-owning process only after selecting a verified compatible target. Keep candidate and historical adapters untouched.

### 2. Mock passes and repaired passes can obscure native model weakness

The 36-site 100% benchmark is mock output. In the live portfolio run, final TypeScript, runtime, and section-completion gates failed. In the live ecommerce run, the model natively completed only 2 of 5 sections; the saved site later passed because the shop pair and navigation were repaired. The benchmark tracks native/repaired/fallback counts, but high composite scores can still be mistaken for model-native performance.

**Action:** publish separate scorecards for model-native output, deterministic repair, model repair, and final rendered site. Require every promotion report to display all four and its provenance. Keep mock runs in a separate dashboard from live model evaluations.

### 3. The 3D gate can pass a site with no 3D content

`agent/project_validator.py` checks for an R3F import or `<canvas` when the brief requests 3D, then uses `evaluation/three_d_performance_validator.py`. An isolated probe with `export default function Hero(){return <canvas />;}` passed all six performance checks. The checks are useful static limits, but do not establish that WebGL initialized, a scene rendered, the requested object exists, animation works, or the fallback appears when WebGL is unavailable.

**Action:** require a visible scene contract (canvas + drawable mesh/model or explicit CSS 3D composition), browser evidence of rendered pixels and no WebGL errors, context-loss/fallback checks, and a short captured motion timeline. Test mobile and reduced motion. Report static 3D policy separately from runtime 3D success.

## P1: model capability and output quality

### 4. Training coverage is uneven for the stated general website goal

The authentic Qwen3 candidate manifest uses `data/quality_v3/train.jsonl` with 787 rows and 220 family IDs. Of the 682 rows with explicit `<business_type>` tags, only 11 are portfolio and 13 ecommerce; SaaS has 35, and technology-adjacent types recur across fintech, database, cybersecurity, cloud, and AI. A text scan found 44 prompts with explicit 3D terms and five with `parallax`. The separately prepared motion curriculum contains 36 training rows and 12 evaluation rows, but the authentic candidate manifest does not name that curriculum. These counts are coverage signals, not quality scores.

**Action:** build reviewed full-site examples across stores, portfolios, editorial, arts, civic, events, education, hospitality, healthcare, dashboards, and unfamiliar topics. Include distinct structures and assets, not palette swaps. Add complete 3D and motion trajectories with actual browser verification, plus targeted repair examples. Preserve family-level separation and record source, license, validation, and visual review for each row.

### 5. Static and pixel heuristics overstate professional quality

`evaluation/site_benchmark_scorer.py` awards visual-structure credit for generic CSS words such as grid, padding, and margin. Its design-diversity metric rewards counts of variables, colors, fonts, radii, and shadows; more colors can score better even when the palette is incoherent. Motion quality largely scores the presence of `transition`, `:hover`, keyframes, transforms, and a reduced-motion query. `agent/visual_judge.py` samples screenshot color variance and coarse regional contrast. These are useful failure detectors, but cannot judge composition, typography, information hierarchy, believable content, art direction, scroll choreography, or perceived smoothness.

**Action:** create a visually reviewed holdout set with rubric scores for layout, hierarchy, typography, content specificity, imagery/asset quality, motion timing, and mobile composition. Capture full page screenshots and short scroll videos at desktop/mobile and reduced motion. Use blinded pairwise human review for candidate promotion, with static heuristics as guardrails rather than quality claims.

### 6. Motion plans need behavioral acceptance, not just source inspection

`agent/motion_patterns.py` parses scroll reveal, parallax, horizontal scroll, sticky story, text reveal, and micro-interactions. The policy checks catch several anti-patterns, but source keywords cannot prove that animation enters at the intended time, remains readable before JavaScript, preserves focus, or stops offscreen. Motion examples should include page-specific timing and fallbacks rather than repeated generic snippets.

**Action:** add browser probes that scroll by controlled increments and assert before/after transform/opacity/position, inspect frame timing/jank, repeat under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and test keyboard focus. For 3D, sample frame rate and memory with inference running on the same GPU.

### 7. Prompt fidelity and cross-section integration remain fragile

The live portfolio failed required section completion and project validation. The ecommerce output contained disconnected cart state, inert shop buttons, and footer links to nonexistent sections before repair. Current deterministic repair is useful but can replace substantial portions of the model's work. A source-level pass does not prove all navigation, filters, forms, and overlay controls are connected.

**Action:** have planning emit a typed requirement manifest with exact user facts, sections/routes, interactions, visual/motion constraints, and cross-section state contracts. Validate those contracts after each section and at final composition. Feed precise compiler, DOM, and interaction diagnostics into bounded repair. Do not allow a polished static page to pass while requested behavior is absent.

## P1: workbench UI and UX

### 8. The default mode conflicts with the product goal

`frontend/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx` initializes generation mode to `component`. The Full Site switch is inside hidden Advanced Controls, while the empty-state chips say “Build a portfolio” and “Create a 3D site.” A user can reasonably expect those prompts to build websites but receive a component task.

**Action:** make Full Site the visible default for website prompts, or auto-detect site intent and display the chosen mode before sending. Keep Component as an explicit visible option. Starter prompts should cover more domains and should not imply a real checkout without payment integration.

### 9. Mobile opens with navigation covering the task

`frontend/src/state/workspace-store.ts` sets `sidebarOpen: true` at every viewport. The mobile screenshot shows the 256 px sidebar and backdrop covering most of a 390 px screen on initial load. The main composer is partially obscured until the user finds the top-left toggle.

**Action:** initialize the sidebar closed below the desktop breakpoint, preserve user preference per viewport, label the toggle for screen readers, and make the backdrop dismissible by Escape. Keep the composer visible on the first mobile visit.

### 10. Project recency labels are wrong; project rows are not keyboard targets

The API returns timestamps such as `2026-09-23 21:22:28`. `ProjectItem.tsx` applies `Number(timestamp) || Date.now()`, so nonnumeric timestamps display “Updated Just now.” The live sidebar showed this for multiple older projects. Each project row is a clickable `<div>` without keyboard semantics. Its delete button is hidden by opacity until hover, so keyboard users lack a clear affordance.

**Action:** parse ISO/date strings explicitly and handle invalid timestamps as unknown. Make the project title a button, keep delete as a separate button, and show delete on keyboard focus. Add readable date/tooltips and avoid exposing raw session IDs as the dominant subtitle.

### 11. Status and context indicators present estimates as facts

`frontend/src/app/App.tsx` sets `gpuReady: true` on any successful status response without a GPU readiness field. `InspectorDrawer.tsx` synthesizes a context-token count from characters and clamps it to at least 920, then displays it alongside authoritative metrics. The top bar can show “Motion Verified” from gate status even though behavioral motion is not measured. These labels can mislead users during model diagnosis.

**Action:** use explicit `verified`, `estimated`, and `unknown` states. Read GPU readiness from backend telemetry; omit unknown values. Label the context estimate and replace it with actual tokenizer counts when available. Rename motion status to “Motion checks passed” until browser motion verification exists.

### 12. The preview and editor can load faster and guide the user better

The initial desktop screen has a large empty center, while the preview workspace is closed by default. Vite reports a 606.56 kB entry chunk; `WorkspacePanel` imports Monaco/code, diff, logs, and terminal views up front. The preview toolbar has desktop/tablet/mobile widths but does not surface checked viewport dimensions, console errors, reduced-motion state, or validation results next to the preview.

**Action:** lazy-load Monaco and terminal tabs, open preview automatically after a site build, and keep a visible build-status summary. Use the empty state to collect topic, audience, pages, content, desired visual style, 3D/motion preference, and real assets. Add a compact preview diagnostics drawer for console, broken links, interaction checks, viewport, and reduced-motion results.

## Recommended execution order

1. **Trust first:** invalidate the incompatible promotion pointer, establish actual loaded model identity, and keep mock/live/native/repaired scores separate.
2. **Acceptance first:** add semantic 3D, motion, and cross-section interaction browser checks; make visual review and provenance mandatory for promotion.
3. **Data then training:** curate diverse independent full sites and repair trajectories, verify every record, keep holdout families disjoint, and train an isolated compatible candidate.
4. **Compare before promotion:** run the same unseen prompts on current base and candidate, measuring native completion, final pass, prompt fidelity, 3D/motion behavior, latency, GPU memory, and blinded visual preference.
5. **Workbench UX:** make full-site intent visible, fix mobile navigation and time labels, distinguish estimated from verified status, and prioritize preview plus diagnostics.

## Limits of this audit

No new live 3D or motion website was generated in this scan; those capabilities are assessed from source, tests, existing runs, and the empty-canvas probe. The two cited live cross-domain runs are too small to estimate general pass rates. The running server was not restarted or interrupted; its in-memory model identity requires a controlled restart and fingerprint check.
`````

`````markdown
# Blueprint comparison and improvement priorities

Reviewed 2026-09-17 against `Qwen3-4B_WebDev_3D_AI_Blueprint.md` supplied by the user. The document is a design proposal, not authorization to execute its installation, migration, or training instructions.

## Actual baseline

- Serving model: Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct, 4-bit, shipped LoRA rank 16 / alpha 16 / dropout 0.0. **Migration to Qwen3-4B in progress (Item 15): code layer complete, new adapter training pending.**
- Target model: Qwen3-4B (base). Chat template now uses `tokenizer.apply_chat_template(..., enable_thinking=False)`. Legacy ChatML hand-rolling removed. `<think>` token blocked at preflight and stripped at decode.
- Latest isolated candidate: `models/premium-reference-v1`; 984 training records, 104 validation records, 246 optimizer steps, one epoch. Training took 98.1 minutes with 3.18 GiB peak PyTorch allocated memory. This is not total system/GPU memory and is not a prediction for another model.
- Validation loss fell from 0.5944 to 0.3368. This does not establish better visual quality.
- Candidate passed the tabs compilation check that the original failed, but both failed the two interaction probes. Candidate hero/pricing responses were incomplete at the tested 2,048-token output budget. Candidate was not promoted; original adapter remains selected.
- These are one-shot section probes. The production site loop already has completeness, CSS, and TypeScript gates and repair attempts; probe failures do not establish that the full loop would deliver those exact broken outputs. The full 153-task benchmark was not rerun.
- The new reference curriculum contains 21 records derived from three original sites. The 984-record mix is neither 984 independent sites nor uniformly verified gold data.

Evidence: [training audit](TRAINING_AUDIT_2026-09-16.md), [results](../experiments/premium-reference-v1/RESULTS.md), [machine-readable outcome](../experiments/premium-reference-v1/outcome.json).

## Comparison

| Blueprint proposal | Current implementation | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Generate, execute, inspect, repair | Component tests, site sections, TSC/CSS gates, previews already exist | Extend feedback to real site interactions and browser console; avoid rebuilding the workbench |
| General file/search/edit tools and project state | Specialized write-component/write-site/test protocol; human PTY terminal | Add workspace-bounded read/search/edit tools with explicit results and a persistent project manifest; a human terminal is not a model tool API |
| Qwen3-4B code model | Qwen2.5-Coder-3B plus existing adapter and Qwen2-specific training assumptions | Benchmark a separate base-model candidate before committing to migration |
| Three.js / R3F / advanced animation | Reusable CSS 3D scene and curated references | Add optional tested R3F scene assets, then train their composition and repair |
| Screenshot model | Screenshot capture and pixel heuristics | Use DOM/console checks and human visual review first; heuristic scores do not understand design |
| 30k–50k training examples | Small curated addition mixed into historical replay | Expand independent, verified examples before expanding volume; record provenance and avoid benchmark leakage |
| Many frontend/backend stacks | React/Vite/TypeScript/CSS focus | Stabilize this stack before adding Next.js, databases, physics, and multiple animation libraries |

## Corrections needed before adopting the recipe

1. **Qwen3 is not a drop-in adapter replacement.** ✅ **IMPLEMENTED (Item 15)**: `agent.py` now includes a base-model guard that reads `adapter_config.json` and raises `RuntimeError` if a Qwen2.5 adapter is loaded against the Qwen3 base. A new adapter must be trained; the code migration (tokenizer registration, chat-template delegation, think-strip) is complete. See `scripts/benchmark_qwen3.py` for VRAM feasibility testing.
2. **The proposed 2,048-token training context cannot hold the current site system prompt.** That prompt alone measures about 4,750 tokens with the current tokenizer. Compact task-specific prompts and selective context retrieval must come first. Training context includes input and target; an output-token budget is a different setting. Do not silently truncate instructions or targets to fit.
3. **Do not copy alpha 32 / dropout 0.05 into continuation training.** The shipped adapter uses alpha 16 / dropout 0.0, and continuation checks enforce compatibility. Those proposed values are experiments for a new adapter, not corrections to the current one.
4. **The sample tool-call dataset is not compatible with our current trainer.** We use explicit XML tool outputs and validated conversation structure. Convert examples with real tool results and complete file content; do not paste the blueprint's illustrative messages directly into training JSONL.
5. **6 GB feasibility requires measurement.** ✅ **IMPLEMENTED (Item 15)**: `scripts/benchmark_qwen3.py` runs warm-up generation at 4096, 6144, and 8192 tokens and prints peak GPU GiB with PASS/FAIL against a 5.5 GiB ceiling. Run after placing Qwen3-4B weights in `base-model/`. The VRAM guard in `train_sft.py` has been raised from 4.5 GiB to 5.0 GiB.
6. **A target of 45,000 examples is not evidence of sufficient quality.** Start with a reviewed pilot of independent sites, modifications, and repairs. Split by project/design family before producing variations. Keep existing failing evaluation prompts held out; train different cases that exercise the same skills.

## Recommended order of work

### P0: Complete and correct outputs

- Preserve the system contract when compacting history; replace token slicing with explicit context budgeting and bounded file excerpts.
- Teach shorter complete file writes and targeted modifications instead of repeatedly emitting entire components and stylesheets.
- Expand held-out behavior checks: tabs selection/focus, billing arithmetic and labels, mobile navigation, forms, and in-page anchors. Promote only after complete outputs, compilation, and requested behaviors pass; then run the broader benchmark for regression evidence.
- Render complete themed sites at mobile and desktop sizes. Check overflow, browser errors, accessibility, reduced motion, and interaction behavior. Human review should judge hierarchy, typography, spacing, art direction, and consistency.
- Fixed during this review: section prompts no longer force three pricing tiers or fabricated testimonials. They now preserve supplied billing terms and require supplied or explicitly illustrative endorsements. Historical architecture claims of production readiness and fully verified data were corrected.

### P1: Useful tools and project memory

- Add read/search/edit operations constrained to the active project, with bounded outputs, path validation, and explicit success/error observations.
- Track routes, section responsibilities, design tokens, dependencies, assets, and verified behavior in a structured manifest.
- Retrieve only relevant local component/API examples. Keep command execution constrained; do not expose arbitrary shell execution merely because the UI already has a PTY.

### P2: Professional visual assets on the laptop

- Build a small library of original/licensed hero scenes with stable import paths and tested React interfaces. Train the model to select, configure, and integrate assets instead of inventing remote GLB URLs.
- Keep CSS animation for simple effects. Add R3F only where actual 3D interaction improves the design.
- Establish measured scene budgets: bounded pixel ratio, few lights, restrained textures/geometry, lazy loading, offscreen pause, reduced-motion behavior, and a static fallback when WebGL is unavailable.
- Render idle scenes on demand and invalidate frames when scene state changes; animated scenes still need frames. The [R3F performance guide](https://r3f.docs.pmnd.rs/advanced/scaling-performance) describes on-demand rendering and adaptive performance. Test while inference is active because both can contend for the laptop GPU.
- Add training trajectories for camera/light adjustments, responsive composition, loading failures, and performance fixes, with real browser feedback.

### P3: Decide whether Qwen3 earns a migration

Run the exact same unseen tasks, tool protocol, and output budget against an isolated Qwen3 candidate. Compare completion, interactions, full-site repair success, latency, peak memory, and blind visual preference. Revalidate chat formatting and chunked loss before any fine-tune. Adopt only if measured benefits justify migration; parameter count alone does not establish professional website quality.

### P4: Optional screenshot inspection

Evaluate a separate vision model only after browser evidence is integrated. Load it sequentially, record its observations as tool results, and verify proposed fixes through the browser. This is a separate capability from the text model; screenshot capture alone does not give the text model vision.

## How the user can help

Supply a few specific screenshots/sections that demonstrate desired typography, motion, and composition; licensed product imagery or 3D assets; and rankings of generated variants. Concrete acceptance feedback is more useful at this stage than collecting thousands of unreviewed examples. No additional hardware purchase is required to carry out the next correctness and dataset-quality improvements.
`````

`````markdown
# Exact Steps: Fine-Tune a Code SLM for React + TypeScript + CSS

Tuned for your hardware: **RTX 4050 Laptop (6GB VRAM), 24GB DDR5 RAM**.
Base model: **Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct** (fits comfortably in 6GB with QLoRA; 7B is possible later via a rented cloud GPU using the exact same script).

Domain: React + TypeScript + CSS component/UI generation.

---

## Step 1 — Set up the environment

```bash
python3 -m venv slm-env
source slm-env/bin/activate

# PyTorch with CUDA (check pytorch.org/get-started if this doesn't match your driver)
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121

pip install unsloth
pip install datasets trl peft accelerate bitsandbytes
```

Verify GPU is visible:
```bash
python3 -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"
```
Should print `True NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU`. Also check free VRAM before training:
```bash
nvidia-smi
```
Close browsers/other GPU apps before training — every MB counts on 6GB.

---

## Step 2 — Download the base model

```bash
pip install huggingface_hub
huggingface-cli login    # token from https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens

huggingface-cli download unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct --local-dir ./base-model
```

## Step 3 — Build your held-out evaluation set (BEFORE training)

Create `eval_set.jsonl` — 50–200 real examples of React/TS/CSS tasks you actually want the model to handle well. Each needs a way to check correctness (here: does the generated `.tsx` compile / pass a lint+type check).

Example lines:

```json
{"prompt": "Write a React functional component in TypeScript called `Badge` that takes a `label: string` and `variant: 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'` prop, and renders a styled span. Include a CSS module with class names for each variant.", "check": "tsc_and_render"}
{"prompt": "Write a React TypeScript component `Accordion` that takes an array of `{title: string, content: string}` items and toggles open/closed state per item on click. Style it with plain CSS (no libraries).", "check": "tsc_and_render"}
{"prompt": "Write a custom React hook `useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T` that returns a debounced version of the input value.", "check": "tsc_only"}
```

Base your real eval set on actual component requests you'd get in your own work — copy from real PRs/tickets if you have them. That's what makes the eval meaningful.

Save as `eval_set.jsonl`.

### Correctness checker for React/TS/CSS (Vitest + jsdom + Testing Library)
Unlike plain Python, "does it run" means "does it typecheck, render, and pass functional/a11y/interaction tests."

Install the testing harness dependencies:
```powershell
npm install -D vitest jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom @testing-library/user-event @vitejs/plugin-react react react-dom @types/react @types/react-dom typescript
```

`vitest.config.ts`:
```typescript
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    setupFiles: ['./vitest.setup.ts'],
    css: true,   // handles CSS module imports without erroring
    globals: true,
  },
});
```

`vitest.setup.ts`:
```typescript
import '@testing-library/jest-dom';
```

## Step 4 — Build your training dataset

### 4a. Collect raw examples
Best source: your own repo's real components (strip out anything sensitive/proprietary before using). Pair a natural-language instruction with the actual component code:

```json
{"instruction": "Create a reusable Button component in React + TypeScript with primary/secondary/ghost variants, a loading state, and CSS module styling.", "output": "// Button.tsx\nimport styles from './Button.module.css';\n\ninterface ButtonProps {\n  variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost';\n  loading?: boolean;\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n  onClick?: () => void;\n}\n\nexport function Button({ variant = 'primary', loading = false, children, onClick }: ButtonProps) {\n  return (\n    <button\n      className={`${styles.button} ${styles[variant]}`}\n      onClick={onClick}\n      disabled={loading}\n    >\n      {loading ? 'Loading...' : children}\n    </button>\n  );\n}\n\n/* Button.module.css */\n.button { padding: 8px 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: none; cursor: pointer; }\n.primary { background: #2563eb; color: white; }\n.secondary { background: #e5e7eb; color: #111827; }\n.ghost { background: transparent; color: #2563eb; }"}
```

If you don't have enough real components, generate candidates with a frontier LLM (Claude/GPT-5) via prompts like *"Write a React+TypeScript+CSS component for X, following common conventions"* — then validate every single one with the Step 3 checker before including it. Never include unvalidated generated code in training data; it teaches the model your generator's mistakes.

Other sources to mine (filter down to only React+TS+CSS, don't dump these in wholesale):
```bash
huggingface-cli download nickrosh/Evol-Instruct-Code-80k-v1 --repo-type dataset --local-dir ./raw-data
```

### 4b. Format into instruction pairs
One JSON object per line in `train_data_raw.jsonl`, same shape as above (`instruction` / `output`).

### 4c. Validate every example
```python
# validate_data.py
import json
from check_tsx import typechecks

kept = []
with open("train_data_raw.jsonl") as f:
    for line in f:
        ex = json.loads(line)
        # Extract just the .tsx portion if the output mixes .tsx + .css;
        # adjust this split to match how you format your examples.
        tsx_part = ex["output"].split("/* ")[0]
        if typechecks(tsx_part):
            kept.append(ex)

print(f"Kept {len(kept)} valid examples")
with open("train_data.jsonl", "w") as f:
    for ex in kept:
        f.write(json.dumps(ex) + "\n")
```
```bash
python3 validate_data.py
```

**Target: 300–800 validated examples** — for a narrow domain like this, quality matters far more than hitting a big number. A smaller, cleaner set will beat a larger noisy one.

### 4d. Cover the domain's real variety
Make sure your dataset spans:
- Functional components with props/state (`useState`, `useEffect`, custom hooks)
- Styling approaches you actually use (CSS Modules, plain CSS, styled-components — pick ONE and be consistent, since mixing styling paradigms in training data will confuse a small model)
- Common patterns: forms, lists, modals, conditional rendering, event handlers
- Accessibility basics if that matters to you (aria-labels, semantic HTML) — include it explicitly in examples if you want the model to default to it

---

## Step 5 — Fine-tune with QLoRA (Unsloth, tuned for 6GB VRAM)

Create `train.py`:

```python
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel
from datasets import load_dataset
from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig
import torch

# 1. Load base model in 4-bit — 3B fits comfortably in 6GB VRAM
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name="unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct",
    max_seq_length=1024,       # shorter than default 2048 — saves VRAM
    load_in_4bit=True,
)

# 2. Attach LoRA adapters
model = FastLanguageModel.get_peft_model(
    model,
    r=16,
    target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj",
                     "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"],
    lora_alpha=16,
    lora_dropout=0.05,
    bias="none",
    use_gradient_checkpointing="unsloth",
    random_state=42,
)

# 3. Load and format your dataset
dataset = load_dataset("json", data_files="train_data.jsonl", split="train")

def format_example(example):
    text = f"### Instruction:\n{example['instruction']}\n\n### Response:\n{example['output']}{tokenizer.eos_token}"
    return {"text": text}

dataset = dataset.map(format_example)

# 4. Train — small batch size + more accumulation steps to fit 6GB VRAM
trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    dataset_text_field="text",
    max_seq_length=1024,
    args=SFTConfig(
        per_device_train_batch_size=1,     # small — fits 6GB
        gradient_accumulation_steps=16,    # keeps effective batch size reasonable
        num_train_epochs=3,
        learning_rate=2e-4,
        fp16=not torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
        bf16=torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
        logging_steps=10,
        output_dir="outputs",
        optim="adamw_8bit",
        lr_scheduler_type="cosine",
        seed=42,
    ),
)

trainer.train()

model.save_pretrained("my-react-slm-lora")
tokenizer.save_pretrained("my-react-slm-lora")
```

Run it:
```bash
python3 train.py
```

If you hit `CUDA out of memory`:
- Drop `max_seq_length` to 768 or 512
- Confirm nothing else is using the GPU (`nvidia-smi`)
- As a last resort, drop LoRA rank `r` to 8

Expect roughly 1–3 hours for 300–800 examples at 3B on this GPU.

---

## Step 6 — Merge the LoRA adapter

```python
# merge.py
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel

model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name="my-react-slm-lora",
    max_seq_length=1024,
    load_in_4bit=False,
)
model.save_pretrained_merged("my-react-slm-merged", tokenizer, save_method="merged_16bit")
```
```bash
python3 merge.py
```

---

## Step 7 — Evaluate on your custom React/TS/CSS eval set

Use the Vitest + jsdom + RTL evaluation driver (`eval_custom.py`):

```bash
# Fast feedback iteration loop on a stratified 40-item subset (Batch mode, ~10s):
python eval_custom.py --model my-react-slm-merged --subset 40

# Full benchmark evaluation across all 153 examples:
python eval_custom.py --model my-react-slm-merged

# Sequential mode for live step-by-step debugging:
python eval_custom.py --model my-react-slm-merged --mode sequential

# Dry run / test harness pipeline without loading GPU weights:
python eval_custom.py --mock --subset 8
```

The driver automatically:
1. Enforces exact named exports in generation prompts (`Export the component as a named export called <Name>`).
2. Auto-binds named exports and provides fallback default export aliasing in test suites.
3. Splits TSX code and CSS modules into isolated test directories.
4. Validates TypeScript compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) and runs the full Vitest suite.
5. Reports breakdown pass rates across all 4 check categories:
   - `tsc_only`
   - `tsc_and_render`
   - `tsc_render_a11y`
   - `tsc_render_interact`
6. Exports full diagnostic error logs to `eval_results.json` for Step 9 retraining iteration.

Run this same eval set through three models to get your comparison:
1. **Base** `unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct` (un-fine-tuned) — baseline
2. **Your fine-tuned** `my-react-slm-merged` — did it improve?
3. **Claude/GPT-5** via API with a well-written prompt — the frontier comparison

For a more thorough check beyond "does it typecheck," manually review 15–20 outputs for whether they actually follow your intended conventions (styling approach, prop naming, component structure) — typechecking catches broken code, not bad style.

---

## Step 8 — Deploy

### Local (fits your laptop easily at 3B size)
```bash
python3 -c "
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained('my-react-slm-merged', max_seq_length=1024)
model.save_pretrained_gguf('my-react-slm-gguf', tokenizer, quantization_method='q4_k_m')
"

curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
```
```
# Modelfile
FROM ./my-react-slm-gguf/model.gguf
```
```bash
ollama create my-react-slm -f Modelfile
ollama run my-react-slm
```

### If you later scale to 7B on a rented cloud GPU
Same `train.py`, just change `model_name` to `unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct` and revert `max_seq_length` to 2048 and `per_device_train_batch_size` to 2 — the 24GB+ VRAM on a rented RTX 4090/A10 handles it without the tight tuning needed for 6GB.

---

## Step 9 — Iterate

1. Go through Step 7's failures — group them: type errors, wrong styling approach used, missed prop, ignored accessibility, wrong file structure (component vs. CSS split).
2. Write 20–40 new training examples specifically targeting your most common failure category.
3. Re-run Step 5 → Step 6 → Step 7.
4. Compare new pass rate + manual review quality against the previous run and against the frontier LLM baseline.
5. Repeat until you match/beat the frontier LLM on your eval set, or gains plateau.

---

## Order-of-operations summary

```
Step 1 → environment set up, 6GB VRAM confirmed free
Step 2 → Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct downloaded
Step 3 → eval_set.jsonl written (real React/TS/CSS tasks, BEFORE training)
Step 4 → train_data.jsonl built from real components + validated with tsc
Step 5 → train.py run (3B, 6GB-tuned settings) → LoRA adapter saved
Step 6 → merge.py run → standalone merged model
Step 7 → eval_custom.py run → base vs fine-tuned vs frontier LLM
Step 8 → GGUF/Ollama local deployment (or move to cloud GPU for 7B)
Step 9 → analyze failures, add targeted data, repeat Steps 5-7
```
`````

`````markdown
# SiteAgent Workbench — Conversational Generation & Live Activity Blueprint

## 1. Purpose

This blueprint explains how to evolve the SiteAgent Workbench from a one-shot website generator into a persistent conversational AI coding environment powered by Qwen3-4B.

The target experience is similar to modern AI chat products, but specialized for website development and integrated directly with:

- React + TypeScript project generation
- Three.js / React Three Fiber
- persistent project chat
- live preview
- build and runtime diagnostics
- code diffs
- debugging
- file operations
- terminal execution
- preview inspection
- agent activity indicators
- automatic repair loops
- project history and undo

The core UX rule is:

> **The chat explains what SiteAgent is doing; the Logs panel shows exactly what the system is doing.**

---

# 2. Product Goal

The Workbench should feel like an AI software engineer inside an IDE.

Instead of:

```text
Prompt → Wait → Website appears
```

the experience should become:

```text
Conversation
    ↓
Plan
    ↓
Generate files
    ↓
Run
    ↓
Inspect
    ↓
Fix
    ↓
Preview
    ↓
Continue conversation
```

Generation is not the end of the workflow. It is the first development turn inside a persistent project conversation.

---

# 3. Recommended Workbench Layout

```text
┌────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ PROJECTS       │ CHAT                          │ WORKSPACE                │
│                │                               │                          │
│ + New Project  │ You                           │ Live Preview             │
│                │ Build Lumina...               │ Code                     │
│ Lumina         │                               │ Diff                     │
│ Nexaflow       │ SiteAgent                     │ Logs                     │
│ Dashboard      │ ◌ Building your website...    │ Shell                    │
│ ApexCloud      │                               │                          │
│                │ ✓ Planning                    │                          │
│                │ ✓ Hero                        │                          │
│                │ ◉ Gallery                     │                          │
│                │ ○ Process                     │                          │
│                │ ○ Pricing                     │                          │
│                │                               │                          │
│                │ [composer always visible]     │                          │
└────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

### Left panel

Rename `History` to `Projects`.

Each project can show a compact status:

```text
Lumina
React + TypeScript + R3F

✓ Build passed
2m ago
```

Internal metrics such as sanity score, token count, and turn count should move to Inspector / Advanced views.

---

# 4. Chat-First Interaction Model

Once the user submits the initial prompt, it should immediately become a chat message.

Before submit:

```text
Build a dark-mode React TypeScript site for "Lumina"...
```

Immediately after submit:

```text
You

Build a dark-mode React TypeScript site for "Lumina" — a
generative art studio that creates physical prints from 3D renders.


SiteAgent

◌ Understanding your request...
```

The composer should immediately reset and stay visible:

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Ask SiteAgent to change, fix, or explain anything…  │
│                                                ↑     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

If the user sends a follow-up while a task is still running, queue it:

```text
You
Make the globe larger.

Queued — SiteAgent will apply this after the current task.
```

---

# 5. Do Not Show Raw Chain-of-Thought

Show concise activity summaries, not hidden reasoning.

Good:

```text
◌ Planning the site structure...
◌ Building the 3D hero...
◌ Checking the TypeScript build...
◌ Fixing 2 errors...
```

The chat should communicate action, status, progress, and result.

---

# 6. Activity Indicator / Throbber

Use a subtle spinner for live activity.

```css
.agent-spinner {
  width: 14px;
  height: 14px;
  border: 2px solid rgba(82, 226, 181, 0.18);
  border-top-color: #52e2b5;
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: siteagent-spin 0.75s linear infinite;
}

@keyframes siteagent-spin {
  to {
    transform: rotate(360deg);
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .agent-spinner {
    animation: none;
  }
}
```

React component:

```tsx
export function AgentSpinner({ size = 14 }: { size?: number }) {
  return (
    <span
      className="agent-spinner"
      style={{ width: size, height: size }}
      aria-label="Working"
    />
  );
}
```

Accessible status:

```tsx
<div role="status" aria-live="polite">
  <AgentSpinner />
  <span>Building the hero...</span>
</div>
```

# 7. Contextual Agent Statuses

```ts
export type AgentStatus =
  | "idle"
  | "understanding"
  | "planning"
  | "coding"
  | "installing"
  | "building"
  | "testing"
  | "debugging"
  | "previewing"
  | "completed"
  | "failed"
  | "cancelled";
```

Map to user-facing text:

```ts
export const agentStatusLabels: Record<AgentStatus, string> = {
  idle: "Ready",
  understanding: "Understanding your request",
  planning: "Planning the project",
  coding: "Writing the website",
  installing: "Installing dependencies",
  building: "Checking the build",
  testing: "Testing the project",
  debugging: "Fixing an issue",
  previewing: "Preparing the preview",
  completed: "Website ready",
  failed: "Generation stopped because of an error",
  cancelled: "Generation cancelled",
};
```

More detailed live messages can include:

```text
◌ Writing Hero.tsx...
◌ Creating the 3D scene...
◌ Installing @react-three/fiber...
◌ Running TypeScript checks...
◌ Fixing 2 TypeScript errors...
◌ Starting Vite preview...
```

These should come from actual orchestrator actions, not fabricated model text.

# 9. Structured Chat Message Model

Do not store every message as a plain string.

```ts
export type ChatMessage =
  | {
      id: string;
      role: "user";
      type: "text";
      content: string;
      createdAt: string;
    }
  | {
      id: string;
      role: "assistant";
      type: "text";
      content: string;
      createdAt: string;
    }
  | {
      id: string;
      role: "assistant";
      type: "activity";
      activityId: string;
      status: "running" | "success" | "error";
      title: string;
      detail?: string;
      steps?: ActivityStep[];
      createdAt: string;
    }
  | {
      id: string;
      role: "assistant";
      type: "change-summary";
      filesChanged: number;
      additions: number;
      deletions: number;
      paths: string[];
      createdAt: string;
    }
  | {
      id: string;
      role: "assistant";
      type: "error";
      content: string;
      recoverable: boolean;
      createdAt: string;
    };

export type ActivityStep = {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  state: "pending" | "running" | "success" | "error";
  detail?: string;
};
```

# 10. Agent Event Stream

The backend should publish structured events.

```ts
export type AgentEvent =
  | {
      type: "agent.status";
      taskId: string;
      status: AgentStatus;
      label?: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "activity.started";
      taskId: string;
      activityId: string;
      label: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "activity.updated";
      taskId: string;
      activityId: string;
      label?: string;
      detail?: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "activity.completed";
      taskId: string;
      activityId: string;
      detail?: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "activity.failed";
      taskId: string;
      activityId: string;
      error: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "file.created";
      taskId: string;
      path: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "file.modified";
      taskId: string;
      path: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "file.deleted";
      taskId: string;
      path: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "command.started";
      taskId: string;
      commandId: string;
      command: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "command.output";
      taskId: string;
      commandId: string;
      stream: "stdout" | "stderr";
      chunk: string;
    }
  | {
      type: "command.completed";
      taskId: string;
      commandId: string;

    }
  | {
      type: "build.result";

# 12. Streaming Transport

Use WebSocket.

Suggested endpoint:

```text
ws://localhost:3001/ws/projects/:projectId
```

Client:

```json
{
  "type": "task.start",
  "payload": {
    "message": "Build Lumina..."
  }
}
```

Server:

```json
{
  "type": "activity.started",
  "taskId": "task_123",
  "activityId": "planning",
  "label": "Planning the site"
}
```

WebSocket is preferable because future features need bidirectional communication:

- Stop / cancel
- User interrupts
- Element selection
- Terminal interaction
- Browser inspection
- Queued prompts
- 3D object selection

# 15. Automatic Debugging Loop

```text
Generate files
    ↓
npm run build
    ↓
Build successful?
    ├── Yes → Start Preview
    │
    └── No
         ↓
   Parse diagnostics
         ↓
   Send errors + relevant files to Qwen
         ↓
   Qwen patches files
         ↓
   npm run build
         ↓
      repeat

Use:

```ts
const MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS = 3;

# 16. Persistent Project-Aware Chat

Each project gets its own conversation.

Recommended entities:

```text
Project
Conversation
Message
Task
AgentEvent
FileChange
Snapshot
```

Example:

```ts
type Project = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  rootPath: string;

  updatedAt: string;

type Conversation = {

type Message = {
  id: string;

For local development, SQLite + Drizzle ORM is a strong choice.

- Search
- Filter
- Pause auto-scroll
- Timestamp
- Severity

Filters:

```text
All
Agent
Files
Shell
Build
Browser
Errors
```

# 28. Log Data Model

```ts
export type LogEntry = {
  id: string;
  timestamp: string;
  category:
    | "agent"
    | "planner"
    | "tool"
    | "file"
    | "shell"
    | "build"
    | "browser"
    | "repair";
  level: "debug" | "info" | "warn" | "error";
  message: string;
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
};
```

Cap in-memory logs:

```ts
const MAX_LOG_ENTRIES = 5000;
```

---

# 29. Live Preview

Use Vite HMR so preview can update while files are generated.

```text
Write files
    ↓
Vite HMR
    ↓
Preview updates
```

Do not rebuild the whole project after every write.

A good schedule is:

```text
After major section
or
after a small batch of writes
or
before final completion
```

---

# 30. Runtime Error Capture

Inside preview:

```ts
window.addEventListener("error", (event) => {
  window.parent.postMessage(
    {
      type: "siteagent.runtime.error",
      message: event.message,
      filename: event.filename,
      line: event.lineno,
      column: event.colno,
    },
    "*"
  );
});

window.addEventListener("unhandledrejection", (event) => {
  window.parent.postMessage(
    {
      type: "siteagent.promise.error",
      message: String(event.reason),
    },
    "*"
  );
});
```

Feed diagnostics into the repair loop.

---

# 31. Browser Debugging Loop

```text
Preview loads
    ↓
Runtime error captured
    ↓
Chat shows:
"! Runtime issue found"
    ↓
Qwen receives error + relevant file
    ↓
Patch
    ↓
Vite HMR
    ↓
Recheck
```

Use:

```ts
const MAX_RUNTIME_REPAIRS = 3;
```

---

# 32. Qwen3-4B System Prompt

```text
You are SiteAgent, an expert web development agent.

You work on an existing project using tools.

Rules:
- Inspect relevant project files before making targeted changes.
- Prefer minimal changes.
- Do not rewrite unrelated files.
- Use React and TypeScript conventions.
- For 3D interfaces, prefer React Three Fiber and Drei when appropriate.
- After modifications, run the relevant build or type check.
- If a build fails, diagnose and repair it.
- Never claim success until verification succeeds.
- Use tool calls instead of dumping complete project code in chat.
```

# 35. Cancel Behavior

When user clicks Stop:

```json
{
  "type": "task.cancel",
  "taskId": "task_123"
}
```

Backend should:

1. stop model generation,
2. terminate active shell task if safe,
3. stop repair attempts,
4. preserve written files,
5. mark task cancelled,
6. keep chat history.

Then show:

```text
Generation stopped.

7 files were created before cancellation.

[Keep changes] [Restore previous version]
```

# 41. Chat Persistence

When user sends a message:

1. Add it to local UI immediately.
2. Persist to backend.
3. Create an agent task.
4. Start streaming events.

Optimistic UI:

```ts
async function sendMessage(content: string) {
  const tempMessage = {
    id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    role: "user" as const,
    type: "text" as const,
    content,
    createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
  };

  chatStore.addMessage(tempMessage);

  socket.send(
    JSON.stringify({
      type: "chat.send",
      projectId,
      content,
      clientMessageId: tempMessage.id,
    })
  );
}
```

If send fails:

```text
Message failed to send. [Retry]
```

# 47. Three.js Performance Guardrails

Default guidance for the agent:

```text
- Use dpr={[1, 1.5]} unless high quality is requested.
- Avoid expensive shadows by default.
- Prefer simple lighting.
- Avoid excessive post-processing.
- Cap particle count.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Provide static fallback when appropriate.
- Avoid unnecessary useFrame computations.
- Use instancing for repeated geometry.
```

# 55. Security

Do not blindly execute arbitrary model-generated shell commands.

Initial allowlist:

```text
npm install
npm run dev
npm run build
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npx tsc
```

Block or require confirmation for dangerous operations:

```text
rm -rf
del /s
format
curl | bash
PowerShell downloads
sudo
system package installation
network tunneling
```

Enforce project-root path safety.

```ts
if (!resolvedPath.startsWith(projectRoot)) {
  throw new Error("Path outside project root");
}
```
`````
